#### §21.7.16.1. The Categorical-Asymmetry Diagnostic — The Two Programs Operate at Distinct Levels

The distance between the Woit Euclidean Twistor Unification program and the McGucken framework is categorical, not gradient. The two programs operate at distinct levels of physics articulation, with the distinction being one of *kind* rather than *degree*. The present subsection establishes this categorical asymmetry as a foundational diagnostic.

**Definition 21.7.16.1 (Mathematical-Formal-Reorganization Level).** *A physics program operates at the mathematical-formal-reorganization level if its content consists of reorganizing the mathematical-formal infrastructure of one or more sectors of physics using new mathematical machinery, without supplying a physical-geometric principle from which the sectors descend as theorems. The program proposes a new mathematical-formal infrastructure (e.g., twistor geometry, Euclidean signature, SO(4) decomposition, spinor representations on complex projective space) and uses this infrastructure to articulate observations about an existing sector of physics. The content is at the level of mathematical-formal reorganization: the same physics is reformulated in different mathematical-formal terms, with no derivation of the sector as a theorem of a foundational principle.*

**Definition 21.7.16.2 (Foundational-Physical-Geometric-Derivation Level).** *A physics program operates at the physical-geometric-derivation level if its content consists of identifying a physical-geometric principle from which one or more sectors of physics descend as formal chains of theorems. The program supplies the physical-geometric principle (e.g., dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic of the McGucken framework) and derives the sectors of physics as formal theorems of the principle, with the derivation being a chain of formal proofs from the foundational principle through intermediate propositions to the empirical content of each sector. The content is at the level of physical-geometric derivation: the sectors of physics are not reformulated using new mathematical machinery; they are derived as theorems of the foundational principle.*

#### §21.7.16.1. The Motl 2005 *"Wick rotation"* Post — A Senior-Figure Orthodox-Formalism Defense of the Wick Rotation with Explicit Acknowledgment That the Physical-Interpretation Question Is Open


Luboš Motl's February 2005 *"Wick rotation"* post [149] was published on the *Lubos Motl's Reference Frame* weblog in response to objections raised in an earlier discussion-thread post about the Ooguri-Vafa-Verlinde *entropic principle* paper. The content of the post that is for the present paper consists of five points.

*The explicit citation of Einstein's x_4 = ict formula as the source of the Wick rotation.* Motl writes verbatim: *"Note that Einstein's favorite formula to write down the Lorentz-invariant line interval was ds\ensuremath{^{2}} = dx_1\ensuremath{^{2}} + dx_2\ensuremath{^{2}} + dx_3\ensuremath{^{2}} + dx_4\ensuremath{^{2}} where x_4 = i \ensuremath{\cdot} c \ensuremath{\cdot} t. Notice that this formula has the form of the ordinary Pythagorian theorem in four dimensions, except for the pure imaginary value of x_4"* [149]. This is — in February 2005 — a senior-figure articulation that the Wick rotation is the coordinate identification involving x_4 = ict, with Einstein 1905-onward as the source. Motl articulates the integrated-coordinate-shadow content (the \ensuremath{\tau} = x\ensuremath{_{4}}/c coordinate identity of Theorem 22.1 of §22 of the present paper) without articulating the differential principle dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic from which the integrated shadow descends per Theorem 22.1 Step 1.

This is a senior-figure 2005 admission that the physical-interpretation question of the Wick rotation is open, with explicit mention of the black-hole information paradox as a place where the deeper meaning might emerge — twenty-one years before Hawking's 2004 concession was elaborated in Susskind 2008, and one year before Hawking's 2005 reformulation of his concession at the Dublin GR17 conference per §30.9.10.7 of the present paper.

#### §21.7.16.2. The Woit 2005 *"Wick Rotation"* Post and the Woit 1988 *Nuclear Physics B* 303 Priority for the Spinor-Tier SU(2)-Electroweak Identification


Peter Woit's February 28, 2005 *"Wick Rotation"* post [150], published on the *Not Even Wrong* weblog as a parallel and explicitly cross-referenced response to the Motl 2005 discussion thread, articulates the spinor-tier Euclidean-SU(2)-as-electroweak content that the 2023 *Euclidean Twistor Unification* paper [5] would subsequently develop at the QFT register, with the post's content distributed across the post body and the 61-comment thread.

*(W2005.1) The spinor-Wick-rotation problem as a clue.* Verbatim: *"To define spinors, we need not just a metric, but a spin connection. In Minkowski space this is a connection on a Spin(3,1)=SL(2,C) bundle, in Euclidean space on a Spin(4)=SU(2)xSU(2) bundle, and these are quite different things, with associated spinor fields with quite different properties. So the whole 'Wick Rotation' question is very confusing even in flat space-time when one is dealing with spinors"* [150]. The diagnosis: Woit's articulation presupposes that there is a "time direction" to pick — a fourth dimension within which one selects an orientation. This presupposition descends from the post-1908 mis-reading of Poincaré-Minkowski-Einstein x\ensuremath{_{4}} = ict as "time is the fourth dimension." The McGucken correction articulated explicitly across the five FQXi essays 2008–2013 [153, 157, 156, 154, 155]: time is not a dimension at all; time is an emergent scalar that arises because the fourth dimension x\ensuremath{_{4}} is expanding at velocity c relative to the three spatial dimensions per dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic, with x\ensuremath{_{4}} = ict being the integrated coordinate shadow of the differential principle, not a re-identification of time with the fourth dimension.

#### §21.7.16.3. The Distler 2006 *"Causal Dynamical Triangulations"* Post — The Shelling-Non-Uniqueness Critique of the CDT Wick Rotation and Its McGucken-Framework Dissolution


Jacques Distler's January 2, 2006 *"Causal Dynamical Triangulations"* post [152], published on the *Musings* weblog at golem.ph.utexas.edu, supplies a senior-figure critique of the CDT program's Wick rotation procedure at the mathematical register, with the critique developed in the post's *"Update (2/4/2006): Shellings"* section and refined in the *"Update (1/5/2006)"* further analysis.

The Distler 2006 Critique — Verbatim Content. Distler articulates the shelling-non-uniqueness critique of the CDT Wick rotation in two points.

*(D2006.1) The CDT Wick rotation requires a discrete time-coordinate that is not uniquely determined by the triangulation.* Verbatim: *"to actually define the lattice model, one needs to do a certain 'Wick-rotation.' This requires us to choose a (discrete) time-coordinate, t, on each triangulation, T, that is, an assignment of an integer, t_i, to each vertex, v_i, of the triangulation. Since we are trying to model a diffeomorphism-invariant theory, we would like this time-coordinate to be determined by the triangulation itself, rather than being an arbitrary extra piece of data"* [152]. This articulates the senior-figure fact that the CDT Wick rotation requires a procedural choice — the discrete time-coordinate — that the orthodox-formalism CDT construction supplies without articulating a physical principle for the choice.

*(D2006.2) The shelling-non-uniqueness problem for d > 2.* Verbatim: *"For d = 2, the answer to both questions is affirmative. So the triangulation, itself, defines a unique discrete time-coordinate, with respect to which one can do the required Wick-rotation. For d > 2, however, the answer to both questions is, in general, 'No!' There are triangulations, T, for which no compatible global choice of discrete time coordinate is possible. Such triangulations are called, 'non-shellable.' There are triangulations for which there is more than one possible assignment of global time-coordinate. That is, the triangulation is 'shellable,' but admits more than one shelling"* [152]. This articulates the specific critique that for d > 2 (the physically relevant case of 4D quantum gravity), the CDT Wick-rotation procedure has two distinct problems:

- Problem 1 — Non-shellable triangulations. Some triangulations admit no compatible discrete time-coordinate at all. These triangulations cannot be Wick-rotated. The CDT response is to discard them — *"Ambjørn et al can simply say, 'We will throw away all the non-shellable triangulations'"* [152] — which is, in Distler's diagnosis, *"perhaps, surmountable"* but introduces a non-local restriction on the configuration space.
- Problem 2 — Shelling non-uniqueness. Some shellable triangulations admit *multiple* compatible discrete time-coordinates. The CDT response — *"arbitrarily choosing a particular shelling and proceeding"* [152] — corresponds to *"introducing some extraneous, non-diffeomorphism-invariant, data into your model"*.

Distler's conclusion: *"Even if the resulting theory has a continuum limit (which, as I said, seems doubtful), the arbitrary choice of shelling means that there is no reason to believe that the resulting continuum theory is diffeomorphism-invariant"* [152].


The McGucken-Framework Dissolution of the Distler 2006 Critique. The Distler 2006 critique is specific to the CDT Wick-rotation procedure operating on lattice triangulations at the discrete level. The critique does not generalize to the McWick rotation \ensuremath{\tau} = x\ensuremath{_{4}}/c, which operates on the real four-manifold the McGucken Manifold as the coordinate identification per Theorem 22.1 of §22 of the present paper, not as a procedural choice on a triangulation.

The closure of the 121-year gap is the McGucken-Wick (McWick) Rotation Theorem, established as Theorem 9 of [2]. We state the theorem here in the form required for the present paper's reconstruction, with the proof structure summarized.


### Theorem 22.1 (McWick Rotation; cf. [2, Theorem 9])

*Statement.* Under the McGucken Principle dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic, the substitution

$$t \;\longmapsto\; -i\tau, \qquad \tau \in \mathbb{R} \tag{22.1}$$

is identically the coordinate identification

$$\tau \;=\; \frac{x_4}{c} \tag{22.2}$$

on the real four-dimensional McGucken manifold \text{the McGucken Manifold} with coordinates (x\ensuremath{_{1}}, x\ensuremath{_{2}}, x\ensuremath{_{3}}, x\ensuremath{_{4}}). Specifically, for any function F of time,

$$F(t)\Big|_{t \to -i\tau} \;=\; F\!\left(-i\tau\right) \;=\; F\!\left(\frac{x_4}{ic}\right) \;=\; F\!\left(\frac{-ix_4}{c}\right), \tag{22.3}$$

with the second equality holding by the coordinate identification \ensuremath{\tau} = x\ensuremath{_{4}}/c and the integrated coordinate shadow x\ensuremath{_{4}} = ict.

*Proof structure.* The proof proceeds in three steps.

Step 1 (The integrated coordinate shadow). The McGucken Principle dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic has integrated solution

$$x_4(t) \;=\; x_4(0) + ict, \tag{22.4}$$

which, taking x_4(0) = 0 at the spacetime event under consideration, gives x\ensuremath{_{4}} = ict as the integrated coordinate shadow of the active expansion. The relation (22.4) is *not* a notational convention; it is the integral of the McGucken Principle, with x\ensuremath{_{4}} a real coordinate on \text{the McGucken Manifold} and \ensuremath{t} the projected time coordinate on the Lorentzian spacetime M_3,t.

Step 2 (Inversion of the integrated relation). Inverting (22.4) gives

$$t \;=\; \frac{x_4}{ic} \;=\; \frac{-ix_4}{c} \;=\; -i \cdot \frac{x_4}{c}. \tag{22.5}$$

Setting \ensuremath{\tau}:= x_4/c, the inversion (22.5) becomes

$$t \;=\; -i\tau. \tag{22.6}$$

Step 3 (Coordinate-identity status of the Wick substitution). The substitution t \ensuremath{\rightarrow} −i\ensuremath{\tau} used in the orthodox Wick-rotation literature is identically the relation (22.6), with \ensuremath{\tau} \ensuremath{\in} \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}} a real coordinate. Equation (22.6) is *not* an analytic continuation from a complex parameter; it is a coordinate identity on the real four-dimensional McGucken Manifold, with \ensuremath{\tau} = x\ensuremath{_{4}}/c a rescaling of the real x\ensuremath{_{4}}-coordinate by the constant c.

For any function F of time, the substitution F(t) \ensuremath{\rightarrow} F(-i\ensuremath{\tau}) is therefore the coordinate-identity rewriting of F in terms of the \ensuremath{\tau} = x\ensuremath{_{4}}/c coordinate rather than the \ensuremath{t} coordinate. The Wick substitution is a coordinate change of perspective on the real four-dimensional McGucken Manifold, not an analytic continuation of a complex parameter. {\rule{0.7em}{0.7em}}

## §22.c. The c-Side of the Wick Rotation: How dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic Encodes the Velocity of Light into the Wick Rotation at Every Position

> **Definitions used in this section:**
>
> - **$\text{the McGucken Manifold}$** — the *McGucken Manifold*: the real four-dimensional manifold on which the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ operates at every event; the Lorentzian-signature reading of $\text{the McGucken Manifold}$ recovers the arena of general relativity.
> - **$\text{McGucken Sphere at }p$** — the *McGucken Sphere at event $p$*: the spherically-symmetric wavefront generated by $dx_4/dt = ic$ at event $p \in \text{the McGucken Manifold}$, expanding at velocity $+ic$ into the region perpendicular to the three spatial dimensions.
> - **McGucken Principle** — $dx_4/dt = ic$: the fourth dimension $x_4$ expands at velocity $ic$ from every event of $\text{the McGucken Manifold}$. The imaginary unit $i$ marks the perpendicularity of $x_4$ to the three spatial dimensions; the empirical world runs under this differential form.
> - **McWick rotation** — the coordinate identity $\tau = x_4/c$ on the real four-dimensional McGucken Manifold. Physically equivalent to the Wick rotation $t \to -i\tau$, but distinguished by being a coordinate identity on a real manifold rather than an analytic continuation in a complex $t$-plane.



The orthodox-tradition treatment of the Wick rotation focuses on the *imaginary unit i* in the substitution t \ensuremath{\mapsto} -i\ensuremath{\tau} as the "interesting" part, treating the velocity of light c as a dimensional-conversion constant tucked into the background dimensional analysis. The McGucken Principle dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic supplies the recognition that *ic* is one indivisible physical quantity with one physical meaning — the velocity of the fourth dimension's expansion — and that the *c-half* of the principle is woven into the Wick rotation at every position alongside the *i-half*. The orthodox-tradition Wick rotation is *partial* in the sense that it makes the imaginary-unit-half of dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic explicit (via the -i in t \ensuremath{\mapsto} -i\ensuremath{\tau}) while leaving the velocity-c-half implicit in the dimensional bookkeeping. The McGucken-Wick (McWick) rotation makes both halves explicit and supplies the physical content of each.

This section establishes the ten identifications of the velocity of light c in the Wick rotation, each as a formal theorem of dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic on the real four-manifold the McGucken Manifold. §22.c.1 establishes the dimensional-bridge identity \ensuremath{\tau} = x_4/c from which the entire analysis descends. §22.c.2 establishes the inseparability of i and c in the McGucken Principle. §22.c.3 establishes c\ensuremath{^{2}} as the metric-signature carrier whose sign flips under the rotation. §22.c.4 establishes that the +i\ensuremath{\varepsilon} Feynman prescription selects the +c direction, not the -c direction. §22.c.5 establishes the photon null worldline as the Wick-rotation tracer, with the McGucken Sphere as the spatial-coordinate-register description of the same null structure. §22.c.6 establishes the Lorentzian signature as a theorem of dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic, forced by c via i\ensuremath{^{2}} = -1. §22.c.7 establishes the wave-diffusion Wick-rotation bridge, with the same velocity c setting both the wave-propagation rate in the Lorentzian register and the diffusion rate c\ensuremath{^{2}} in the Euclidean register. §22.c.8 establishes the c\ensuremath{^{3}}-factor in the Hawking temperature as descending from three positions of c in dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic. §22.c.9 provides the historical-remark on the Poincaré 1905, Minkowski 1908, and Einstein 1912 *reunification* of i and c in the single symbol *ic* that the orthodox tradition subsequently split. §22.c.10 consolidates the eight prior theorems into Theorem 22.c.10, the McWick Rotation as the Coordinate Identity \ensuremath{\tau} = x_4/c on the McGucken Manifold.


### §22.c.1. The Dimensional-Bridge Identity \ensuremath{\tau} = x_4/c


**Theorem 22.c.1 (Dimensional-Bridge Identity).** *Let t denote the time coordinate (SI units: seconds) and let x_4 denote the McGucken fourth-coordinate (SI units: meters) of the real four-manifold the McGucken Manifold under the McGucken Principle dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic. Let \ensuremath{\tau} denote the Wick-rotated coordinate of the orthodox tradition, obtained by the formal substitution t \ensuremath{\mapsto} -i\ensuremath{\tau} in the Lorentzian metric, with \ensuremath{\tau} assigned units of seconds in the orthodox-formalism convention. Then \ensuremath{\tau} is identified with the real coordinate x_4/c on the McGucken Manifold:*

$$\tau = \frac{x_4}{c}.$$

*Proof.* Integrating the McGucken Principle dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic over time from a fiducial event with x_4(0) = 0 gives the integrated coordinate-shadow descent

$$x_4(t) = \int_0^t i c \, dt' = i c t.$$

The Lorentzian metric in (t, x_1, x_2, x_3)-coordinates is

$$ds^2 = -c^2 \, dt^2 + dx_1^2 + dx_2^2 + dx_3^2,$$

with c\ensuremath{^{2}} as the dimensional coefficient making c\ensuremath{^{2}} dt\ensuremath{^{2}} a quantity of SI units meters\ensuremath{^{2}}. The orthodox Wick substitution t \ensuremath{\mapsto} -i\ensuremath{\tau} converts the metric to

$$ds_E^2 = +c^2 \, d\tau^2 + dx_1^2 + dx_2^2 + dx_3^2,$$

which is the Euclidean metric in (\ensuremath{\tau}, x_1, x_2, x_3)-coordinates. Equating the time-component differential c\ensuremath{^{2}} d\ensuremath{\tau}\ensuremath{^{2}} to the McGucken fourth-coordinate differential dx_4\ensuremath{^{2}} — the only choice consistent with the Euclidean metric on the (x_1, x_2, x_3, x_4)-real-coordinate register of the McGucken Manifold being the standard Euclidean form \ensuremath{\delta}_{ij} = diag(+1, +1, +1, +1) [41, Theorem 1] — gives

$$c^2 \, d\tau^2 = dx_4^2 \quad \Leftrightarrow \quad c \, d\tau = \pm \, dx_4.$$

Taking the positive branch consistent with the sign convention dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = +ic of the McGucken Principle gives c d\ensuremath{\tau} = dx_4, hence (integrating from the fiducial event with \ensuremath{\tau}(0) = 0, x_4(0) = 0)

$$\tau = \frac{x_4}{c}.$$

The orthodox-formalism unit assignment \ensuremath{\tau} in seconds is consistent: with x_4 in meters and c in meters per second, \ensuremath{\tau} = x_4/c is in seconds, as required. {\rule{0.7em}{0.7em}}

significance of Theorem 22.c.1. The orthodox tradition writes \ensuremath{\tau} = it and calls \ensuremath{\tau} "imaginary time" in units of seconds — an interpretation that treats \ensuremath{\tau} as a formal complex-analytic continuation of the real time coordinate, with no physical content beyond the analyticity assumption. The McGucken framework reads the *same* \ensuremath{\tau} as the real coordinate x_4/c on the real four-manifold the McGucken Manifold, with c as the dimensional-bridge constant converting between the time-coordinate register (seconds) and the fourth-coordinate register (meters). The Wick rotation, under this reading, is the dimensional conversion between two real coordinate registers on the *same* real manifold, with c as the conversion factor.

This dimensional-bridge identity is the primitive for the entire analysis of §22.c. Theorems 22.c.2 through 22.c.10 each elaborate one specific position in which the factor c of \ensuremath{\tau} = x_4/c appears as a dimensional quantity in physics, with each position cross-referenced back to Theorem 22.c.1 as the origin.


### §22.c.2. The Inseparability of i and c in the McGucken Principle


**Theorem 22.c.2 (Inseparability of i and c).** *The right-hand side ic of the McGucken Principle dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic is one indivisible physical quantity — the velocity of the fourth dimension's expansion — and not a product of two independent physical constants i and c that can be replaced or removed separately. Removing either factor destroys the physical content of the principle: removing c destroys dimensional consistency; removing i destroys the Lorentzian-signature content. Both factors are necessary, and the symbol ic is the unique single-symbol carrier of the physical content "velocity of x\ensuremath{_{4}}-expansion perpendicular to the three spatial dimensions."*

*Proof.* The argument is in two parts: (i) removing c destroys dimensional consistency; (ii) removing i destroys the Lorentzian-signature content. Each part proceeds by direct substitution and comparison with established results.

(i) *Removing c:* Suppose one replaces c in dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic with a dimensionless constant \ensuremath{\alpha}, giving dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = i\ensuremath{\alpha}. Then the dimensional analysis is: [dx_4/dt] has units of [x_4]/[t] = (meters)/(seconds) = meters per second. The right-hand side i\ensuremath{\alpha} is dimensionless (since both i and \ensuremath{\alpha} are dimensionless). Equating the two yields [x_4] = seconds, contradicting the established identification of x_4 as the McGucken fourth spatial coordinate with units of meters [41, Proposition 2.3; 153, Section "Deriving Relativity from dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic"]. The contradiction establishes that c is necessary in dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic as the dimensional carrier of velocity (meters per second).

(ii) *Removing i:* Suppose one removes i in dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic and writes dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = c. Then x_4 has the same register as the three spatial coordinates x_1, x_2, x_3 (real velocity rate c rather than imaginary velocity rate ic), and the metric on the McGucken Manifold in the (x_1, x_2, x_3, x_4)-real-coordinate register is the standard Euclidean form \ensuremath{\delta}_{ij} = diag(+1, +1, +1, +1). Substituting the integrated coordinate-shadow x_4 = ct (without the i) into the metric and computing g_tt in (t, x_1, x_2, x_3)-coordinates gives

$$g_{tt} = g_{x_4 x_4} \cdot \left(\frac{dx_4}{dt} \right)^2 = (+1) \cdot c^2 = +c^2,$$

yielding signature diag(+c\ensuremath{^{2}}, +1, +1, +1), which is Euclidean (after rescaling), not Lorentzian. This contradicts the established identification of the Lorentzian signature \ensuremath{\eta} = diag(-1, +1, +1, +1) on the McGucken Manifold [Theorem 6 of 44; Theorem 22.c.6 of the present section, established below]. The contradiction establishes that i is necessary in dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic as the carrier of the perpendicular-direction structure generating the Lorentzian signature via i\ensuremath{^{2}} = -1.

Together, parts (i) and (ii) establish that both i and c are in dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic, with i as the perpendicular-direction carrier and c as the rate-of-expansion carrier. The product ic is one indivisible physical quantity — the velocity of the fourth dimension's expansion perpendicular to the three spatial dimensions — and not a product of two independent factors. {\rule{0.7em}{0.7em}}

significance of Theorem 22.c.2. The orthodox tradition has historically split i and c in foundational discussion: the i has been carried forward as the "imaginary unit of physics" with extensive discussion of its physical meaning (Bohr 1949 on the "striking similarities" of i in the formalisms of quantum mechanics and relativity [156, Bohr quote]; Heisenberg 1927 on the i in pq - qp = i\ensuremath{\hbar} as recording perpendicular change; the twelve canonical "factor of i" insertions catalogued in [MGWickIRotation, §3]), while c has been treated as a dimensional constant of nature whose value is given empirically but whose role in the foundational structure of the Wick rotation has been left unarticulated beyond the Einstein 1905 light-speed-invariance postulates.

The McGucken framework reunifies i and c into the single symbol ic as the physical content of the McGucken Principle. The Wick rotation, read, rotates between coordinate registers in which the two halves of ic manifest in different forms — but the two halves are *always* present, on both sides of the rotation. Theorem 22.c.2 is the prerequisite for the entirety of §22.c.


**Corollary 22.c.2.1 (The Three Physical Contents of dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic — Sphere Expansion at Velocity c, Perpendicularity of the Fourth Axis, and Compton-Clock Oscillation of the Wavefront-Rider Amplitude — and Their Preservation Across the McWick Rotation).** *The McGucken Principle dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic contains two algebraic symbols on its right-hand side — the constant c and the imaginary unit i — and generates three distinct physical contents from those two symbols, because the imaginary unit i discharges two distinct physical duties per Remark 21.5 of §21. The three physical contents are: first, the expansion of the McGucken-Sphere wavefront \text{McGucken Sphere at }p at velocity c per unit coordinate time from every event of the real four-manifold, carried by the c-factor of dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic; second, the perpendicularity of the fourth axis x\ensuremath{_{4}} to the three spatial dimensions x\ensuremath{_{1}}, x\ensuremath{_{2}}, x\ensuremath{_{3}}, carried by the i-factor of dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic discharging its perpendicularity-marker duty per Remark 21.5 the perpendicularity-marker duty; and third, the Compton-clock oscillation of the wavefront-rider amplitude at the angular frequency \ensuremath{\omega}_C = mc\ensuremath{^{2}}/\ensuremath{\hbar} on a massive worldline, carried by the same i-factor of dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic discharging its rotor duty per Remark 21.5 the rotor / phase-carrier duty, with substrate-tick action \ensuremath{\Delta}S = h per Compton period per Theorem 30.9.6septies.2 of §30.9.2septies. All three of these physical contents — the McGucken Sphere expansion at velocity c, the perpendicularity of the fourth axis, and the Compton-clock oscillation of the wavefront-rider amplitude — are preserved across the McWick rotation \ensuremath{\tau} = x\ensuremath{_{4}}/c of Theorem 22.1: the rotation is a coordinate identity on the real four-manifold and cannot generate or destroy any physical content of x\ensuremath{_{4}}. What the rotation does is swap the algebraic form-representation of each of the three contents between two coordinate registers, per the position-of-i toggle of Theorem 30.9.6septies.1 of §30.9.2septies.*

*Proof.* The claim is established in five steps: Step 1 decodes the c-factor of dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic into the McGucken Sphere-expansion content at velocity c; Step 2 decodes the i-factor of dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic discharging its perpendicularity-marker duty per Remark 21.5 the perpendicularity-marker duty into the perpendicularity of the fourth axis x\ensuremath{_{4}} to the three spatial dimensions x\ensuremath{_{1}}, x\ensuremath{_{2}}, x\ensuremath{_{3}}; Step 3 decodes the i-factor of dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic discharging its rotor duty per Remark 21.5 the rotor / phase-carrier duty into the Compton-clock oscillation of the wavefront-rider amplitude at angular frequency \ensuremath{\omega}_C = mc\ensuremath{^{2}}/\ensuremath{\hbar}; Step 4 records that the three physical contents (Sphere expansion at velocity c, perpendicularity of the fourth axis, and Compton-clock oscillation of the wavefront-rider amplitude) are generated from the two algebraic symbols (c and i) of dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic because the imaginary unit i does two jobs and the constant c does one; Step 5 establishes McWick-rotation invariance of all three physical contents.

*Step 1 — The c-factor of dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic as the carrier of the McGucken Sphere-expansion content at velocity c.* Per Theorem 22.c.2 above, the c-factor in dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic supplies dimensional consistency: [dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt] = meters per second requires the right-hand side to carry velocity dimension, and c = 299,792,458 m/s is the velocity content. The McGucken-Sphere wavefront \text{McGucken Sphere at }p generated at every event p \ensuremath{\in} \text{the McGucken Manifold} by the principle per the §22 definition block expands with spatial radius c(t - t\ensuremath{_{0}}) growing at rate c per unit coordinate time — the geometric-wavefront content of §22.c.5 and the two-projection reading of §22.c.5bis, on both the photon-null-worldline case (v_{x\ensuremath{_{4}}} = 0, Sphere-tangent share) and the massive-worldline case (v_{x\ensuremath{_{4}}} = c, full-share expansion perpendicular to the worldline). The Huygens 1690 spherical-wavefront primitive receives its rate content from the c-factor per the reciprocal-generative content of [MGReciprocal, Proposition R3]. The c-factor of dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic is the rate carrier of the McGucken Sphere-expansion-at-velocity-c content and nothing else.

*Step 2 — The i-factor of dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic discharging Remark 21.5 the perpendicularity-marker duty, as the carrier of the perpendicularity of the fourth axis x\ensuremath{_{4}} to the three spatial dimensions x\ensuremath{_{1}}, x\ensuremath{_{2}}, x\ensuremath{_{3}}.* Per Theorem 22.c.2 part (ii) and Remark 21.5 the perpendicularity-marker duty, the i-factor in dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic records the geometric perpendicularity of the fourth axis x\ensuremath{_{4}} to the three spatial dimensions x\ensuremath{_{1}}, x\ensuremath{_{2}}, x\ensuremath{_{3}} on the real four-dimensional McGucken Manifold. The algebraic content of the perpendicularity is i\ensuremath{^{2}} = \ensuremath{-}1: the fourth axis is "rotated 90 degrees" relative to the spatial three-slice, and the square of the perpendicularity marker returns the negative sign that generates the Lorentzian signature \ensuremath{\eta} = diag(\ensuremath{-}c\ensuremath{^{2}}, +1, +1, +1) per Theorem 22.c.6 below. Removing the i-factor collapses the fourth axis to a fourth spatial coordinate and destroys the Lorentzian content per part (ii) of the proof of Theorem 22.c.2. The duty of $i$ as the perpendicularity marker of the fourth axis of the i-factor is the orientation content of dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic — the direction the expansion is going, relative to the three spatial dimensions.

*Step 3 — The same i-factor of dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic discharging Remark 21.5 the rotor / phase-carrier duty, as the carrier of the Compton-clock oscillation of the wavefront-rider amplitude at angular frequency \ensuremath{\omega}_C = mc\ensuremath{^{2}}/\ensuremath{\hbar}.* The same i-factor discharges a second physical duty per Remark 21.5 the rotor / phase-carrier duty: when the wavefront-rider amplitude on a massive worldline is integrated under Schrödinger evolution i \ensuremath{\hbar} \ensuremath{\partial}\ensuremath{_{t}}\ensuremath{\psi} = \ensuremath{\hat{H}} \ensuremath{\psi}, the interior i generates unitary rotation of the amplitude at the Compton angular frequency \ensuremath{\omega}_C = mc\ensuremath{^{2}}/\ensuremath{\hbar}, with the rest-mass Hamiltonian eigenvalue mc\ensuremath{^{2}} supplying the phase-rotation rate on the rest worldline. The rotor content is algebraically the period-4 action i \ensuremath{\to} i\ensuremath{^{2}} = \ensuremath{-}1 \ensuremath{\to} i\ensuremath{^{3}} = \ensuremath{-}i \ensuremath{\to} i\ensuremath{^{4}} = +1 in the complex plane, exponentiated as $e^{-i\omega_C t}$ per substrate-tick multiplication. The rate \ensuremath{\omega}_C is species-specific through the mass m of the rider coupled to the substrate advance, while the substrate-tick action per Compton period is the mass-independent invariant \ensuremath{\Delta}S = mc\ensuremath{^{2}} \ensuremath{\cdot} (2\ensuremath{\pi}\ensuremath{\hbar}/(mc\ensuremath{^{2}})) = 2\ensuremath{\pi}\ensuremath{\hbar} = h per Steps 3 and 7 of Theorem 30.9.6septies.2. The duty of $i$ as the rotor and phase carrier of the i-factor is the dynamics content of dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic — the oscillation of the amplitude at the Compton-clock rate, carrying action h per rotation. The rotor the rotor / phase-carrier duty requires a coupled mass m to set its rate; the perpendicularity the perpendicularity-marker duty does not — the perpendicularity of x\ensuremath{_{4}} to the three spatial dimensions is present in dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic at the substrate scale independent of any coupled matter, while the Compton-clock oscillation of the wavefront-rider amplitude manifests as an empirical oscillation rate only after a mass-m rider couples to the substrate advance per the Compton-de Broglie coupling of [MGComptonDeBroglie].

*Step 4 — Two algebraic symbols, three physical contents.* Steps 1–3 establish that dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic contains two algebraic symbols on its right-hand side (c and i) and generates three distinct physical contents: the McGucken Sphere-expansion content at velocity c (from the c-factor), the perpendicularity of the fourth axis x\ensuremath{_{4}} to the three spatial dimensions (from the i-factor discharging its perpendicularity-marker the perpendicularity-marker duty of Remark 21.5), and the Compton-clock oscillation of the wavefront-rider amplitude at angular frequency \ensuremath{\omega}_C = mc\ensuremath{^{2}}/\ensuremath{\hbar} (from the same i-factor discharging its rotor the rotor / phase-carrier duty of Remark 21.5). The count arithmetic is: the c-factor discharges one physical duty (Sphere-expansion-rate carrier), and the i-factor discharges two physical duties (perpendicularity-marker and rotor) per the the two duties of $i$ (its duty as perpendicularity marker of the fourth axis, and its duty as rotor and phase carrier) two-duties articulation of Remark 21.5. Two symbols, three contents, because the imaginary unit does two jobs and the constant c does one. The three contents are physically independent: the McGucken Sphere-expansion content is a scalar rate, the perpendicularity content is a direction relative to \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}\ensuremath{^{3}}, and the Compton-clock oscillation content is an angular frequency coupled to a rest mass; no two of the three reduce to each other; all three are necessary for the empirical content of dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic. Removing the c-factor destroys dimensional consistency (part (i) of Theorem 22.c.2); removing the i-factor's perpendicularity-marker duty destroys the Lorentzian signature and reduces the fourth axis to a spatial fourth (part (ii) of Theorem 22.c.2); removing the i-factor's rotor duty destroys the Compton-clock oscillation and the h-carrying substrate-tick action of Theorem 30.9.6septies.2.

*Step 5 — McWick-rotation invariance of all three physical contents.* The McWick rotation \ensuremath{\tau} = x\ensuremath{_{4}}/c of Theorem 22.1 is a coordinate identity on the real four-dimensional McGucken Manifold — it is a relabeling of the fourth axis from length units to time units (or, equivalently, a redistribution of where the i-factor lives in the coordinate identification of the fourth axis, via x\ensuremath{_{4}} = ict in the t-parametrisation versus x\ensuremath{_{4}} = c\ensuremath{\tau} in the \ensuremath{\tau}-parametrisation). No coordinate identity on a real manifold generates or destroys physical content of the manifold's structure: the three physical contents — the McGucken Sphere-expansion at velocity c, the perpendicularity of the fourth axis x\ensuremath{_{4}} to x\ensuremath{_{1}}, x\ensuremath{_{2}}, x\ensuremath{_{3}}, and the Compton-clock oscillation of the wavefront-rider amplitude at \ensuremath{\omega}_C = mc\ensuremath{^{2}}/\ensuremath{\hbar} — are properties of the real x\ensuremath{_{4}}, and the McWick rotation, being a coordinate relabeling of x\ensuremath{_{4}}, cannot touch them. What the rotation does is swap the form-representation of each of the three contents between two registers. The McGucken Sphere-expansion content at velocity c: the rate c per unit t (unrotated) becomes c per unit \ensuremath{\tau} (rotated) — the rate is preserved, its unit-carrier is relabeled. The perpendicularity of the fourth axis: the interior-i inside the coordinate identity x\ensuremath{_{4}} = ict (unrotated) becomes retired-i absorbed into the axis label \ensuremath{\tau} (rotated), with the perpendicularity now manifest as \ensuremath{\tau} being a direct real coordinate of the fourth axis rather than a factor-i-scaled coordinate — the perpendicularity is preserved, its algebraic marker is relocated. The Compton-clock oscillation of the wavefront-rider amplitude: the interior-i inside the Schrödinger amplitude factor $e^{-i\omega_C t}$ (unrotated) becomes retired-i inside the Boltzmann weight $e^{-\omega_C \tau} = e^{-mc^2 \tau/\hbar}$ (rotated) — the rate \ensuremath{\omega}_C is preserved (the same angular frequency in either register), its algebraic form is converted from unit-modulus rotation in the complex plane to real exponential decay along the direct real axis \ensuremath{\tau}, per the two-projection reading of §22.c.5bis. The position-of-i toggle of Theorem 30.9.6septies.1 is the operator-algebra articulation of this rotation-invariance-with-form-swap content. Steps 1–5 establish Corollary 22.c.2.1 at pure-algebraic-derivation rigor. $\square$

*significance of Corollary 22.c.2.1.* The two-symbols-three-contents decomposition supplies the sharper reading of Theorem 22.c.2. Theorem 22.c.2 establishes that both algebraic symbols in the right-hand side ic of the McGucken Principle are physically necessary; Corollary 22.c.2.1 identifies the three physical contents these two symbols generate and establishes that all three are preserved across the McWick rotation. The corollary supplies the counting arithmetic that makes the the two duties of $i$ (its duty as perpendicularity marker of the fourth axis, and its duty as rotor and phase carrier) two-duties framing of Remark 21.5 quantitative at the physical-content register: the mystery is not that two algebraic symbols produce two physical contents (one each), but that two algebraic symbols produce three physical contents because the imaginary unit does two jobs. The Wick rotation preserves all three because all three are properties of the real physical fourth axis x\ensuremath{_{4}}, and the McWick rotation is a coordinate identity on that real axis per Theorem 22.1. The orthodox Wick-rotation register operates the substitution t \ensuremath{\to} \ensuremath{-}i\ensuremath{\tau} without articulating any of these three physical contents or their invariance under the rotation, because the orthodox tradition treats \ensuremath{\tau} as an analytic-continuation parameter without a physical referent per Remark 30.9.6.2 of §30.9.2ter of the present paper; the McWick register articulates all three contents and their invariance because it treats \ensuremath{\tau} as a real coordinate on the real four-manifold whose fourth axis carries the three physical contents inseparably. The corollary is the prerequisite for the reading of §22.c.5bis (the two-projection reading of the massive worldline as two form-representations of the same three-content substrate advance) and for the reading of §30.9.10.7 (the Schrödinger equation as carrying both its Algebraic-Channel unitary content and its Geometric-Channel Second-Law content simultaneously, related by the McWick rotation swapping the form-representations of the three physical contents — Sphere-expansion at velocity c, perpendicularity of the fourth axis, and Compton-clock oscillation of the wavefront-rider amplitude — between the two channels).


### §22.c.3. The Metric-Signature Carrier c\ensuremath{^{2}}


**Theorem 22.c.3 (c\ensuremath{^{2}} as the Metric-Signature Carrier).** *The Lorentzian metric on the McGucken Manifold in (t, x_1, x_2, x_3)-coordinates and the Euclidean metric in (\ensuremath{\tau}, x_1, x_2, x_3)-coordinates are*

$$ds^2 = -c^2 \, dt^2 + dx_1^2 + dx_2^2 + dx_3^2 \quad \text{(Lorentzian)},$$

$$ds_E^2 = +c^2 \, d\tau^2 + dx_1^2 + dx_2^2 + dx_3^2 \quad \text{(Euclidean)}.$$

*The Wick rotation is the sign-flip of the coefficient of the time-component differential dt\ensuremath{^{2}} \ensuremath{\leftrightarrow} d\ensuremath{\tau}\ensuremath{^{2}}, with c\ensuremath{^{2}} as the dimensional-and-magnitude carrier in both signatures. The dimensional consistency of the spacetime interval is forced by c\ensuremath{^{2}}; the sign-flip of the signature is forced by i\ensuremath{^{2}} = -1 in (ic)\ensuremath{^{2}} = -c\ensuremath{^{2}}; and the two halves together encode dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic on the metric register.*

*Proof.* The Euclidean metric on the (x_1, x_2, x_3, x_4)-real-coordinate register of \text{the McGucken Manifold} is the standard Euclidean form \ensuremath{\delta}_{ij} = diag(+1, +1, +1, +1) [41, Theorem 1 on the Euclidean substrate of the McGucken Manifold]. Substituting the integrated coordinate-shadow x_4 = ict of the McGucken Principle gives

$$(dx_4)^2 = (ic \cdot dt)^2 = i^2 \cdot c^2 \cdot (dt)^2 = -c^2 \, (dt)^2.$$

Substituting into the Euclidean-signature metric dx_4\ensuremath{^{2}} + dx_1\ensuremath{^{2}} + dx_2\ensuremath{^{2}} + dx_3\ensuremath{^{2}} on the (x_1, x_2, x_3, x_4)-real-coordinate register gives

$$dx_4^2 + dx_1^2 + dx_2^2 + dx_3^2 = -c^2 \, dt^2 + dx_1^2 + dx_2^2 + dx_3^2,$$

which is the Lorentzian metric in (t, x_1, x_2, x_3)-coordinates. The c\ensuremath{^{2}} appears as the coefficient of dt\ensuremath{^{2}} because c is the rate of integration dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic; the minus sign appears because i\ensuremath{^{2}} = -1.

Under the Wick rotation t \ensuremath{\mapsto} -i\ensuremath{\tau}, the time-component differential transforms as dt \ensuremath{\mapsto} -i d\ensuremath{\tau}, hence (dt)\ensuremath{^{2}} \ensuremath{\mapsto} -(d\ensuremath{\tau})\ensuremath{^{2}}, and the c\ensuremath{^{2}} (dt)\ensuremath{^{2}} term transforms as

$$-c^2 \, dt^2 \mapsto -c^2 \cdot (-d\tau^2) = +c^2 \, d\tau^2,$$

yielding the Euclidean metric in (\ensuremath{\tau}, x_1, x_2, x_3)-coordinates. Equivalently, the Wick-rotated coordinate \ensuremath{\tau} = x_4/c of Theorem 22.c.1 gives d\ensuremath{\tau} = dx_4/c, hence c\ensuremath{^{2}} d\ensuremath{\tau}\ensuremath{^{2}} = dx_4\ensuremath{^{2}}, recovering the Euclidean-register metric directly.

The c\ensuremath{^{2}}-coefficient is invariant under the Wick rotation; only the sign of the coefficient flips. The Wick rotation is therefore the operation that sends the coefficient of the time-component from -c\ensuremath{^{2}} to +c\ensuremath{^{2}}, with c\ensuremath{^{2}} as the dimensional-and-magnitude carrier and the sign-flip i\ensuremath{^{2}} = -1 as the rotation content. {\rule{0.7em}{0.7em}}

significance of Theorem 22.c.3. The Lorentzian-vs-Euclidean signature distinction in metric geometry is canonically articulated in the orthodox tradition without explicit attribution of the c\ensuremath{^{2}} to a physical principle. The McGucken-reading: the c\ensuremath{^{2}} appears in both signatures because c is the rate dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic of integration; the sign-flip of the signature is the i\ensuremath{^{2}} = -1 of (ic)\ensuremath{^{2}} = -c\ensuremath{^{2}}; and the Wick rotation is the operation that toggles the sign while preserving c\ensuremath{^{2}} as the dimensional carrier. The factor c\ensuremath{^{2}} in the metric is the metric-register record of the c-half of dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic, just as the i in the path-integral weight e^(iS/\ensuremath{\hbar}) is the path-integral-register record of the i-half. The Wick rotation rotates between the two halves.


### §22.c.4. The +i\ensuremath{\varepsilon} Feynman Prescription Selects +c, Not -c


**Theorem 22.c.4 (The +i\ensuremath{\varepsilon} Feynman Prescription Selects +c).** *The Feynman propagator with the +i\ensuremath{\varepsilon} prescription*

$$G_F(k) = \frac{i}{k^2 - m^2 + i\varepsilon}, \quad \varepsilon \to 0^+,$$

*selects positive-frequency modes propagating forward in the McGucken fourth-coordinate x_4 at velocity +c (consistent with dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = +ic) and negative-frequency modes propagating backward in x_4 at velocity -c (consistent with dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = -ic for antimatter modes via the Feynman-Stückelberg interpretation). The +i\ensuremath{\varepsilon} prescription is the contour-integration encoding of the sign-choice +ic in the McGucken Principle.*

*Proof.* The Feynman propagator in position space is

$$G_F(x - y) = \int \frac{d^4 k}{(2\pi)^4} \frac{i \, e^{-ik \cdot (x - y)}}{k^2 - m^2 + i\varepsilon},$$

with metric signature (+, -, -, -) so that k\ensuremath{^{2}} = k_0\ensuremath{^{2}} - k\ensuremath{^{2}}. The +i\ensuremath{\varepsilon} prescription shifts the poles at k_0 = \ensuremath{\pm}\ensuremath{\omega} with $\omega = +\sqrt{\mathbf{k}^2 + m^2}$ infinitesimally off the real axis: the +\ensuremath{\omega} pole moves to +\ensuremath{\omega} - i\ensuremath{\varepsilon} (below the real axis), and the -\ensuremath{\omega} pole moves to -\ensuremath{\omega} + i\ensuremath{\varepsilon} (above the real axis). For x^0 - y^0 > 0 (future-directed in the time coordinate t), closing the contour in the lower-half k_0-plane — where the exponential factor e^-ik_0(x^0 - y^0) decays — picks up the +\ensuremath{\omega} pole, giving positive-frequency modes proportional to e^-i\ensuremath{\omega}(x^0 - y^0).

Under the McGucken reading of t in terms of the McGucken fourth-coordinate x_4 = ict — equivalently, \ensuremath{\tau} = x_4/c of Theorem 22.c.1 — the positive-frequency mode e^-i\ensuremath{\omega} t corresponds to a mode whose phase advances forward in x_4 at the rate set by the McGucken Principle dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = +ic. The second-quantised structure of [1, §VIII.2] makes this explicit: positive-frequency mode operators a_k^† create matter quanta with x_4-phase e^+i k \ensuremath{\cdot} x_4 propagating forward in x_4 at velocity +c; negative-frequency mode operators b_k^† create antimatter quanta with x_4-phase e^-i k \ensuremath{\cdot} x_4 propagating *forward* in t but with the *reversed* x_4-direction, consistent with the Feynman-Stückelberg identification of antimatter as matter propagating backward in x_4.

The +i\ensuremath{\varepsilon} prescription therefore selects, at the field-theoretic level, the same sign-choice that the McGucken Principle dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = +ic makes at the level: positive c for matter modes propagating forward in x_4. Reversing the prescription to -i\ensuremath{\varepsilon} would select the time-reversed propagator, which is the antimatter / x_4-reversed register, consistent with the chiral-asymmetry analysis of [1, §VIII.2 on x_4-reversal as charge conjugation \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}}]. {\rule{0.7em}{0.7em}}

significance of Theorem 22.c.4. The +i\ensuremath{\varepsilon} prescription is one of the twelve canonical "factors of i" in physics that the McGucken framework unifies under the suppression map \ensuremath{\sigma} from dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic [MGWickIRotation, §3 on the twelve-case unification]. The unification, prior to Theorem 22.c.4, established the i-half of the prescription: the prescription encodes the +i sign of +i\ensuremath{\varepsilon} as the +i of dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = +ic. Theorem 22.c.4 supplies the c-half of the same content: not only does +i\ensuremath{\varepsilon} select the *imaginary-direction* +i sign of dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = +ic, but it selects the *velocity-direction* +c sign as well. The prescription encodes both halves of dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic.

The significance for the Feynman-Stückelberg interpretation of antimatter is direct: matter modes propagate forward in x_4 at velocity +c; antimatter modes propagate backward in x_4 at velocity -c; the +i\ensuremath{\varepsilon} prescription selects the matter-channel by selecting the +c sign of \ensuremath{\pm} c. Time-ordering in the Feynman propagator is the directionality of x_4-expansion at velocity c. The Feynman-Stückelberg picture, articulated as a calculational convenience in the orthodox tradition, becomes literal under the McGucken reading: the propagator's time-ordering is the field-theoretic record of the sign-choice +c in dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = +ic.


### §22.c.5. The Photon Null Worldline and the McGucken Sphere as Wick-Rotation Tracers


**Lemma 22.c.5 (Photon Null Worldline as the Wick-Rotation Tracer).** *A photon propagating at velocity c through the three spatial dimensions has a null worldline ds\ensuremath{^{2}} = 0 in the Lorentzian metric on the McGucken Manifold. Under the McGucken Principle dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic, the photon is at absolute rest in the fourth coordinate: dx_4 = 0 along the photon's null worldline parametrized by the affine parameter \ensuremath{\lambda}. The photon "rides the wavefront" of the McGucken Sphere's spherically symmetric expansion at velocity c, with the McGucken Sphere providing the (x_1, x_2, x_3, x_4)-coordinate-register description of the same null structure that the photon's null worldline provides in the (t, x_1, x_2, x_3)-coordinate register.*

*Proof.* For a photon propagating in the +x_1 direction at velocity c, the worldline is (t(\ensuremath{\lambda}), x_1(\ensuremath{\lambda}), 0, 0) = (\ensuremath{\lambda}/c, \ensuremath{\lambda}, 0, 0) parametrized by \ensuremath{\lambda}. The Lorentzian interval is

$$ds^2 = -c^2 \, dt^2 + dx_1^2 = -c^2 \cdot \frac{d\lambda^2}{c^2} + d\lambda^2 = -d\lambda^2 + d\lambda^2 = 0,$$

confirming the null worldline.

For the McGucken fourth-coordinate x_4 along this worldline, the four-fold ontology of [47, Definition 3] specifies that a photon at velocity c in the three spatial dimensions occupies *Case (2)* of the ontology: Sphere-tangent share $v_{x_4} = 0$ (the $v = c$ limit of $v^2 + v_{x_4}^2 = c^2$, per Appendix A.3.1 of the present paper), so the photon has zero share in the x\ensuremath{_{4}}-expansion — the photon rides the wavefront rather than advancing in x\ensuremath{_{4}}. The coordinate rate dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic (Appendix A.1, R1) continues to hold at every event the photon crosses: the expansion of the McGucken Manifold proceeds at rate $ic$ around every event, including the events on the photon's worldline; what vanishes for the photon is the *share* of that expansion carried along the worldline, not the expansion itself. The photon's null worldline traces the boundary of the expanding McGucken Sphere of radius x_4 = ct centred on the emission event.

Equivalently, in the (t, x_1)-coordinates with metric -c\ensuremath{^{2}} dt\ensuremath{^{2}} + dx_1\ensuremath{^{2}} = 0, the photon's worldline lies on the null cone — the boundary of the future light-cone of the emission event. The McGucken Sphere of radius x_4 = ct expanding at velocity c from the emission event is the *spatial* register of the same null-cone structure: every point on the McGucken Sphere at McGucken-radius x_4 = ct is a point that a photon emitted at the origin could reach in time t. The photon's null worldline in (t, x_1, x_2, x_3)-coordinates and the McGucken Sphere's spherically symmetric expansion in (x_1, x_2, x_3, x_4)-coordinates are two coordinate-register descriptions of the same physical structure: the velocity-c expansion of x_4 from every spacetime event [153, "Einstein's Annus Mirabilis: The Photon Holds the Key to Time as an Emergent Phenomenon"; MGReciprocal, Proposition R3 on Huygens' Principle as a theorem of dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic]. {\rule{0.7em}{0.7em}}

significance of Lemma 22.c.5. The Wick rotation is canonically described in the orthodox tradition as a rotation that "removes" the null-cone structure: under Wick rotation, the Lorentzian metric (with light cones) becomes the Euclidean metric (with no null directions). The McGucken-reading is that the null-cone structure is the (t, x_spatial)-coordinate-register description of the velocity-c expansion of x_4 from every event; the Euclidean structure is the (x_spatial, x_4)-coordinate-register description of the same velocity-c expansion. The Wick rotation does not remove the velocity-c content; it rotates between the two coordinate registers, both of which carry c as a quantity (the null-cone slope c in the Lorentzian register, the McGucken-Sphere expansion rate c in the Euclidean register).

The photon is the *Wick-rotation tracer*: by following the photon's null worldline (Lorentzian register) one is following the McGucken Sphere's expanding wavefront (Euclidean register) under the coordinate transformation \ensuremath{\tau} = x_4/c of Theorem 22.c.1.


### §22.c.5bis. The Massive Worldline's Two Projections of the Perpendicular ic-Advance: Rest-Frame Phase Rotation Along x\ensuremath{_{4}} and Spatial-Slice Sphere Expansion at Velocity c


The McGucken Principle dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic states the physical reality that the fourth dimension x\ensuremath{_{4}} is expanding at the velocity of light c in a spherically-symmetric manner from every spacetime event. On a massive worldline at spatial rest, the full four-velocity budget is x\ensuremath{_{4}}-directed: the particle's advance is entirely along x\ensuremath{_{4}}, at coordinate rate ic. The advance produces one physical event — the perpendicular ic-advance of the substrate — which projects onto two distinct registers, and each register conceals what the other exposes. This is the projection reading of dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic on the massive worldline, complementary to the photon reading of §22.c.5.

**Projection 1: the amplitude in the rest frame, parametrised by coordinate time t.** The massive quantum's amplitude on its rest worldline is

$$\psi_{\text{rest}}(x, t) \;=\; \psi_0(x) \, \exp\!\big(-i \omega_C t\big), \qquad \omega_C \;=\; \frac{m c^2}{\hbar}.$$

The spatial profile \ensuremath{\psi}\ensuremath{_{0}}(x) is stationary; the phase factor $e^{-i\omega_C t}$ rotates in the complex plane at the Compton frequency \ensuremath{\omega}_C = mc\ensuremath{^{2}}/\ensuremath{\hbar}, one full rotation per Compton period \ensuremath{\Delta}t_C = 2\ensuremath{\pi}\ensuremath{\hbar}/(mc\ensuremath{^{2}}) (Compton 1923 / de Broglie 1924; §III.1-bis and Theorem 30.9.6septies.2 of the present paper). This rotation is the sole registrant of the ic-advance in the t-parametrised amplitude: the fourth-axis motion, which by the integrated shadow x\ensuremath{_{4}} = ict advances by \ensuremath{\Delta}x\ensuremath{_{4}} = ic\ensuremath{\cdot}\ensuremath{\Delta}t\ensuremath{_{C}} = i\ensuremath{\lambda}_C per Compton period (Step 6 of Theorem 30.9.6septies.2), shows up in the amplitude as a phase rotation of magnitude 2\ensuremath{\pi} per Compton period and as nothing else. The spatial support of the amplitude does not expand under this projection; the wavefront is invisible.

**Projection 2: the spatial slice \ensuremath{\Sigma}\ensuremath{_{t}} = {x\ensuremath{_{4}} = ict}, parametrised by the perpendicular axis.** Perpendicular to the massive worldline, in the three spatial dimensions x\ensuremath{_{1}}, x\ensuremath{_{2}}, x\ensuremath{_{3}}, the McGucken Sphere at event $p$ centred on the emission event p expands isotropically at velocity c per unit coordinate time, per the Huygens 1690 spherical wavefront primitive whose ic-advance origin is established in the reciprocal-generative content of the corpus [MGReciprocal, Proposition R3]. The McGucken Sphere carries no phase content in this projection; it is a real geometric surface of radius c(t \ensuremath{-} t\ensuremath{_{0}}) growing at rate c. The rotation, which is the sole registrant of the ic-advance in Projection 1, is not visible in this projection; the expansion, which is invisible in Projection 1, is the whole content here.

**The identity: Projections 1 and 2 record the same one perpendicular ic-advance.** Both projections read dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic. The advance has one direction — perpendicular to x\ensuremath{_{1}}, x\ensuremath{_{2}}, x\ensuremath{_{3}}, along x\ensuremath{_{4}} — and one rate — c per unit coordinate time. Projection 1 parametrises the advance by t and reads it as phase rotation at angular frequency \ensuremath{\omega}_C: the perpendicularity marker i in ic-per-dt puts the advance into the complex phase, and the c-half sets the rotation rate. Projection 2 parametrises the perpendicular direction of the advance by the spatial position vector in \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}\ensuremath{^{3}}, reads the isotropic front of the perpendicular expansion from the emission event, and sees the McGucken Sphere at event $p$ of radius ct growing at rate c. The perpendicularity marker i is not manifest in this projection because the perpendicular direction has been resolved into its own axis rather than encoded as a factor in a scalar coordinate rate. Two projections, one advance.

**The Wick rotation as the coordinate operation that swaps which projection is exposed in the equations.** The Wick rotation \ensuremath{\tau} = x\ensuremath{_{4}}/c of Theorem 22.1 is the coordinate identity that swaps between the two projection registers by relabeling the fourth axis from the t-parametrisation (in which x\ensuremath{_{4}} = ict carries i explicitly and the ic-advance shows as phase rotation) to the direct \ensuremath{\tau}-parametrisation (in which x\ensuremath{_{4}} = c\ensuremath{\tau} carries no i and the advance shows as expansion along \ensuremath{\tau}). Applied to the rest-frame amplitude, the substitution t = \ensuremath{-}i\ensuremath{\tau} converts the phase-carrier factor

$$\exp\!\big(-i \omega_C t\big) \;\xrightarrow{\;t = -i\tau\;}\; \exp\!\big(-\omega_C \tau\big) \;=\; \exp\!\left(-\frac{m c^2 \tau}{\hbar}\right),$$

replacing the unit-modulus rotation of Projection 1 by the real exponential decay of Projection 2's own dynamical face — the Boltzmann weight at inverse temperature \ensuremath{\beta} = \ensuremath{\tau}/\ensuremath{\hbar} for a state of rest-mass energy mc\ensuremath{^{2}}. The rotation of the amplitude in the complex plane, in the un-rotated register, is what the advance's perpendicularity looks like when the phase-plane is the register of exposure; the exponential decay of the amplitude along \ensuremath{\tau}, in the rotated register, is what the same perpendicular advance looks like when the direct real axis is the register of exposure. The advance itself, the ic-per-dt substrate motion of the McGucken Principle, is invariant across the two coordinate registers; the Wick rotation moves only which face of the advance is manifest in the equations, per the position-of-i mechanism of §30.9.6septies.

**Two content items concealed and revealed by the Wick rotation on the massive worldline.** In the un-rotated (Projection 1) register, the Wick rotation conceals the Compton phase-carrier factor $e^{-i\omega_C t}$ (retiring its rotation into the coordinate as $e^{-\omega_C \tau}$ Boltzmann weight) and the associated single-quantum spectroscopic content of the twentieth-century tradition per §30.9.10.3bis; it reveals the real spatial expansion of the McGucken Sphere at event $p$ at rate c and, on the wave-mechanical amplitude, the Fürth 1933 [413] free-particle diffusion coefficient D = \ensuremath{\hbar}/(2m) governing the heat-kernel spread of §22.c.7 whose Gaussian variance \ensuremath{\sigma}\ensuremath{^{2}} = \ensuremath{\hbar}\ensuremath{\tau}/m grows monotonically along the direct \ensuremath{\tau} axis. In the rotated (Projection 2) register, the Wick rotation conceals the isotropic spatial expansion at c (which is present in the un-rotated register too, but is dressed by the phase-coherent envelope $e^{-i\omega_C t}$ of Projection 1 that covers the wavefront until Wick rotation strips it) and reveals the interior-i phase rotation as the empirical signature of the Compton clock ticking at \ensuremath{\omega}_C = mc\ensuremath{^{2}}/\ensuremath{\hbar} per Compton period, one substrate-tick action \ensuremath{\Delta}S = h per rotation (Steps 3 and 7 of Theorem 30.9.6septies.2). The two projections are the same physical event; the Wick rotation is the coordinate change that makes visible in one register what was concealed by the other.

**Physical significance of Projection 1 and Projection 2 as the two operational registers of the ic-advance on the massive worldline.** The photon reading of §22.c.5 established that a null worldline is at Sphere-tangent share v_{x\ensuremath{_{4}}} = 0 while the coordinate rate dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic continues to hold at every event the photon crosses (Appendix A.3.1 of the present paper): the photon rides the wavefront in the sense that its share of the perpendicular advance vanishes, though the substrate advance itself does not. The massive-worldline reading of §22.c.5bis completes the picture for the complementary case: the matter particle at spatial rest carries the full share v_{x\ensuremath{_{4}}} = c of the perpendicular advance and registers it as phase rotation at \ensuremath{\omega}_C in its rest frame, while the same advance, projected perpendicular to the worldline into the observer's spatial slice, is the same Sphere \text{McGucken Sphere at }p whose expansion at c is the null-boundary the photon rides. Photon and matter particle, taken together, give two operational readings of the one substrate advance dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic: the photon's tangent-share is zero and its coordinate rate is ic, so the advance registers as null-cone-boundary geometry perpendicular to the worldline; the matter particle's tangent-share is c and its rest-frame amplitude carries the advance as phase, so the advance registers as Compton-clock rotation along the worldline and as the same Sphere-expansion perpendicular to it. The Wick rotation is the operation that swaps, on either worldline, which projection register of the ic-advance is exposed in the equations.


### §22.c.6. The Lorentzian Signature Forced by c via i\ensuremath{^{2}} = -1


**Theorem 22.c.6 (Lorentzian Signature Forced by c via i\ensuremath{^{2}} = -1).** *Assume the McGucken Principle dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic on the real four-manifold the McGucken Manifold. Then the metric on the McGucken Manifold in (t, x_1, x_2, x_3)-coordinates has Lorentzian signature*

$$\eta = \text{diag}(-c^2, +1, +1, +1),$$

*reducing to \ensuremath{\eta} = diag(-1, +1, +1, +1) in geometrized units c = 1. The minus sign on the time-component is forced by the i\ensuremath{^{2}} = -1 in (ic)\ensuremath{^{2}}; the magnitude c\ensuremath{^{2}} of the time-component is forced by the c-half of ic. Both halves of the McGucken Principle are in the signature.*

*Proof.* The Euclidean metric on the (x_1, x_2, x_3, x_4)-real-coordinate register of \text{the McGucken Manifold} is the standard Euclidean form \ensuremath{\delta}_{ij} = diag(+1, +1, +1, +1) [41, Theorem 1 on the Euclidean substrate of the McGucken Manifold]. The integrated coordinate-shadow x_4 = ict of the McGucken Principle relates the time coordinate t to the fourth coordinate x_4 via the velocity rate ic. The metric tensor component g_tt in (t, x_1, x_2, x_3)-coordinates is computed by tensor transformation as

$$g_{tt} = g_{x_4 x_4} \cdot \left(\frac{dx_4}{dt} \right)^2 = (+1) \cdot (ic)^2 = i^2 \cdot c^2 = -c^2.$$

The spatial components are unchanged: g_x_i x_i = +1 for i = 1, 2, 3. The signature is therefore \ensuremath{\eta} = diag(-c\ensuremath{^{2}}, +1, +1, +1), which in geometrized units c = 1 reduces to \ensuremath{\eta} = diag(-1, +1, +1, +1). Both factors i and c of the McGucken Principle contribute content: the i\ensuremath{^{2}} = -1 generates the minus sign of the time-component (the Lorentzian-vs-Euclidean signature distinction), and the c\ensuremath{^{2}} generates the magnitude of the time-component (the dimensional content of the Lorentzian metric). {\rule{0.7em}{0.7em}}

significance of Theorem 22.c.6. Theorem 22.c.6 is the cleanest demonstration that the McGucken Principle dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic supplies *both* physical contents of the Lorentzian signature: the i-half generates the sign-flip i\ensuremath{^{2}} = -1, and the c-half generates the magnitude c\ensuremath{^{2}}. Removing either factor destroys the signature, per the proof of Theorem 22.c.2: dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = i alone would give signature diag(-1, +1, +1, +1) but with t in units of meters (since dx_4 would have units of meters and i is dimensionless), destroying the relation to physical time; dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = c alone would give signature diag(+c\ensuremath{^{2}}, +1, +1, +1) = diag(+1, +1, +1, +1) after rescaling, destroying the Lorentzian-vs-Euclidean distinction. The Lorentzian signature is a theorem of dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic specifically — both halves.

The McGucken-foundational origin of the Lorentzian signature established by Theorem 22.c.6 closes a foundational question that the orthodox tradition has carried without physical answer for over a century: *why* is the signature of spacetime Lorentzian rather than Euclidean? The Greaves-Halvorson, the Maudlin, and the various structuralist-philosophy-of-physics literatures have addressed this question at the level of *how the signature is consistent with empirical phenomena* without addressing the physical origin. The McGucken framework supplies the origin: the Lorentzian signature is the metric-register record of dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic, with both halves of the principle.


### §22.c.7. The Wave-Diffusion Wick-Rotation Bridge


**Theorem 22.c.7 (The Wave-Diffusion Wick-Rotation Bridge).** *Assume the McGucken Principle dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic on the McGucken Manifold. The Lorentzian wave equation*

$$\frac{1}{c^2} \frac{\partial^2 \psi}{\partial t^2} - \nabla^2 \psi = 0$$

*(governing spherically symmetric wave propagation at velocity c from every spacetime event, in the Huygens 1690 register of [MGReciprocal, Proposition R3]) and the Euclidean Schrödinger-rotated diffusion equation*

$$\frac{\partial \psi}{\partial \tau} = D \, \nabla^2 \psi, \quad D = \frac{\hbar c^2}{2 E}$$

*(governing diffusion with diffusion coefficient D proportional to c\ensuremath{^{2}}, in the heat-kernel register of the Wick-rotated Schrödinger equation) are Wick-rotation images of one another, related by \ensuremath{\tau} = it in the orthodox-formalism convention, or equivalently by \ensuremath{\tau} = x_4/c in the McGucken-foundational convention of Theorem 22.c.1. The same velocity c that sets the wave-propagation rate in the Lorentzian register sets the diffusion rate c\ensuremath{^{2}} in the Euclidean register.*

*Proof.* The argument is in two parts: (i) the wave-equation Wick rotation to the four-dimensional Euclidean Laplace equation, with c\ensuremath{^{2}} as coefficient; (ii) the Schrödinger-equation Wick rotation to the diffusion equation, with c\ensuremath{^{2}} as coefficient via the relativistic energy-mass relation E = mc\ensuremath{^{2}}.

(i) *Wave-equation Wick rotation:* The Lorentzian wave equation has time-derivative term (1/c\ensuremath{^{2}}) \ensuremath{\partial}\ensuremath{^{2}}/\ensuremath{\partial} t\ensuremath{^{2}}. Under the orthodox Wick substitution t \ensuremath{\mapsto} -i\ensuremath{\tau} (with the McGucken reading \ensuremath{\tau} = x_4/c per Theorem 22.c.1), the second time-derivative transforms as

$$\frac{\partial^2}{\partial t^2} = \frac{\partial^2}{\partial (-i\tau)^2} = \frac{1}{(-i)^2} \cdot \frac{\partial^2}{\partial \tau^2} = -\frac{\partial^2}{\partial \tau^2},$$

hence (1/c\ensuremath{^{2}}) \ensuremath{\partial}\ensuremath{^{2}}/\ensuremath{\partial} t\ensuremath{^{2}} becomes -(1/c\ensuremath{^{2}}) \ensuremath{\partial}\ensuremath{^{2}}/\ensuremath{\partial} \ensuremath{\tau}\ensuremath{^{2}}. The Lorentzian wave equation (1/c\ensuremath{^{2}}) \ensuremath{\partial}\ensuremath{^{2}} \ensuremath{\psi}/\ensuremath{\partial} t\ensuremath{^{2}} - \ensuremath{\nabla}\ensuremath{^{2}} \ensuremath{\psi} = 0 thereby transforms to

$$-\frac{1}{c^2} \frac{\partial^2 \psi}{\partial \tau^2} - \nabla^2 \psi = 0 \quad \Leftrightarrow \quad \frac{1}{c^2} \frac{\partial^2 \psi}{\partial \tau^2} + \nabla^2 \psi = 0,$$

which is the four-dimensional Euclidean Laplace equation (elliptic) in the (\ensuremath{\tau}, x_1, x_2, x_3)-coordinate register, with c\ensuremath{^{2}} as the dimensional carrier of the \ensuremath{\tau}-component coefficient. The Euclidean Laplace equation in the McGucken-foundational convention \ensuremath{\tau} = x_4/c becomes

$$\frac{\partial^2 \psi}{\partial x_4^2} + \nabla^2 \psi = 0,$$

which is the standard four-dimensional Euclidean Laplace equation on the (x_1, x_2, x_3, x_4)-coordinate register, recovered without any explicit factor of c because \ensuremath{\tau} = x_4/c has absorbed the dimensional content of c into the coordinate identification.

(ii) *Schrödinger-equation Wick rotation:* The non-relativistic free-particle Schrödinger equation is

$$i\hbar \frac{\partial \psi}{\partial t} = -\frac{\hbar^2}{2m} \nabla^2 \psi.$$

Substituting t \ensuremath{\mapsto} -i\ensuremath{\tau} gives \ensuremath{\partial}/\ensuremath{\partial} t = (1/(-i)) \ensuremath{\partial}/\ensuremath{\partial} \ensuremath{\tau} = i \ensuremath{\partial}/\ensuremath{\partial} \ensuremath{\tau}, hence i\ensuremath{\hbar} \ensuremath{\partial} \ensuremath{\psi}/\ensuremath{\partial} t = i\ensuremath{\hbar} \ensuremath{\cdot} i \ensuremath{\partial} \ensuremath{\psi}/\ensuremath{\partial} \ensuremath{\tau} = -\ensuremath{\hbar} \ensuremath{\partial} \ensuremath{\psi}/\ensuremath{\partial} \ensuremath{\tau}. The Schrödinger equation transforms to

$$-\hbar \frac{\partial \psi}{\partial \tau} = -\frac{\hbar^2}{2m} \nabla^2 \psi \quad \Leftrightarrow \quad \frac{\partial \psi}{\partial \tau} = \frac{\hbar}{2m} \nabla^2 \psi,$$

which is the diffusion equation with diffusion coefficient D_nr = \ensuremath{\hbar}/(2m). To make the relativistic content of c explicit, one substitutes the relativistic energy-mass relation E = mc\ensuremath{^{2}}, giving m = E/c\ensuremath{^{2}}, hence

$$D = \frac{\hbar}{2m} = \frac{\hbar c^2}{2 E},$$

with c\ensuremath{^{2}} as the factor of the diffusion coefficient.

Together, parts (i) and (ii) establish that *both* the wave-equation register (Lorentzian, velocity-c propagation) and the diffusion-equation register (Euclidean, diffusion-rate-c\ensuremath{^{2}} via E = mc\ensuremath{^{2}}) carry c as a quantity. The Wick rotation rotates between the two registers; c is preserved throughout. {\rule{0.7em}{0.7em}}

significance of Theorem 22.c.7. Theorem 22.c.7 establishes that the wave-versus-diffusion duality of the Wick rotation is c-determined at both ends: wave propagation at velocity c in the Lorentzian register, diffusion at rate c\ensuremath{^{2}} in the Euclidean register. The orthodox tradition treats this as a formal property of the analytic continuation t \ensuremath{\mapsto} -i\ensuremath{\tau}, with the dimensional analysis of the c\ensuremath{^{2}}-coefficient left as a bookkeeping consequence of the energy-mass relation. The McGucken framework reads it as the *same* physical velocity c manifesting in two coordinate registers — the Huygens-1690 spherical-wavefront-at-velocity-c register and the diffusion-rate-c\ensuremath{^{2}} register — with the Wick rotation as the rotation between the registers. Huygens 1690 articulated the wave-at-velocity-c register; the McGucken Principle of 2026 supplies the unified physical principle from which both the wave-at-c and the diffusion-at-c\ensuremath{^{2}} registers descend as theorems of dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic.


### §22.c.8. The c\ensuremath{^{3}}-Factor in the Hawking Temperature


**Theorem 22.c.8 (c\ensuremath{^{3}}-Periodicity of Imaginary Time at the Hawking Temperature).** *Consider a Schwarzschild black hole of mass M with horizon radius r_S = 2GM/c\ensuremath{^{2}} in the McGucken Manifold under the McGucken Principle dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic. The Wick-rotated Euclidean Schwarzschild metric has a conical singularity at r = r_S that is removed by identifying the imaginary-time coordinate \ensuremath{\tau} with period \ensuremath{\beta}_H given by*

$$\beta_H = \frac{1}{k_B T_H} = \frac{8 \pi G M}{\hbar c^3},$$

*with c\ensuremath{^{3}} in the denominator. The Hawking temperature is*

$$T_H = \frac{\hbar c^3}{8 \pi G M k_B},$$

*with c\ensuremath{^{3}} in the numerator. The c\ensuremath{^{3}} factor descends from the McGucken Principle dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic in three positions: (a) c\ensuremath{^{2}} in the Schwarzschild metric coefficient -c\ensuremath{^{2}} (1 - r_S/r) dt\ensuremath{^{2}} (per Theorem 22.c.3 and the Schwarzschild geometry); (b) one further factor of c from the dimensional bridge \ensuremath{\tau} = x_4/c (per Theorem 22.c.1); (c) the McGucken-Sphere expansion rate at velocity c underlying the spherical symmetry of the Schwarzschild horizon (per Theorem 22.c.7 and Lemma 22.c.5).*

*Proof.* The Schwarzschild metric in (t, r, \ensuremath{\theta}, \ensuremath{\phi})-coordinates is

$$ds^2 = -\left(1 - \frac{r_S}{r}\right) c^2 \, dt^2 + \left(1 - \frac{r_S}{r}\right)^{-1} dr^2 + r^2 \, d\Omega^2,$$

with r_S = 2GM/c\ensuremath{^{2}}. The c\ensuremath{^{2}} in the time-component coefficient descends from Theorem 22.c.3. Wick-rotating t \ensuremath{\mapsto} -i\ensuremath{\tau} gives the Euclidean Schwarzschild metric

$$ds_E^2 = \left(1 - \frac{r_S}{r}\right) c^2 \, d\tau^2 + \left(1 - \frac{r_S}{r}\right)^{-1} dr^2 + r^2 \, d\Omega^2,$$

with c\ensuremath{^{2}} as the time-component coefficient (per Theorem 22.c.3).

Near the horizon, change coordinates to the proper distance \ensuremath{\rho} from the horizon: r = r_S + \ensuremath{\rho}\ensuremath{^{2}}/(4 r_S) to leading order in \ensuremath{\rho}. Then (1 - r_S/r) \ensuremath{\approx} \ensuremath{\rho}\ensuremath{^{2}}/(4 r_S\ensuremath{^{2}}), and dr\ensuremath{^{2}} \ensuremath{\approx} d\ensuremath{\rho}\ensuremath{^{2}}. The Euclidean Schwarzschild metric near the horizon reduces (to leading order in \ensuremath{\rho}) to

$$ds_E^2 \approx \rho^2 \cdot \frac{c^2 \, d\tau^2}{4 r_S^2} + d\rho^2 + r_S^2 \, d\Omega^2 = \rho^2 \, d\theta^2 + d\rho^2 + r_S^2 \, d\Omega^2,$$

where

$$\theta = \frac{c}{2 r_S} \cdot \tau$$

is a dimensionless angle. The (\ensuremath{\rho}, \ensuremath{\theta})-half-plane is a flat two-dimensional cone with apex at \ensuremath{\rho} = 0. The cone has zero deficit angle (and hence no conical singularity) if and only if \ensuremath{\theta} has period 2\ensuremath{\pi}, i.e.,

$$\frac{c}{2 r_S} \cdot \beta_H = 2\pi \quad \Leftrightarrow \quad \beta_H = \frac{4 \pi r_S}{c}.$$

Substituting r_S = 2GM/c\ensuremath{^{2}} gives

$$\beta_H = \frac{4 \pi \cdot (2GM/c^2)}{c} = \frac{8 \pi G M}{c^3}.$$

The period \ensuremath{\beta}_H is identified with the inverse temperature \ensuremath{\beta}_H = 1/(k_B T_H) via the KMS condition of [Haag-Hugenholtz-Winnink 1967] (which is itself, in the McGucken framework, a theorem of dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic via the periodicity-of-imaginary-time identification of [44, §4]). Restoring the factor of \ensuremath{\hbar} from the KMS-condition dimensional analysis gives the Hawking temperature

$$T_H = \frac{1}{k_B \beta_H} = \frac{\hbar c^3}{8 \pi G M k_B}.$$

The factor of c\ensuremath{^{3}} descends from three positions: c\ensuremath{^{2}} in the metric coefficient c\ensuremath{^{2}} d\ensuremath{\tau}\ensuremath{^{2}} of Theorem 22.c.3, and one further factor of c from the Schwarzschild radius r_S = 2GM/c\ensuremath{^{2}} combined with the dimensional bridge \ensuremath{\tau} = x_4/c of Theorem 22.c.1. The spherical symmetry of the Schwarzschild horizon is the McGucken-Sphere structure of Lemma 22.c.5 in the gravitating-mass register, with c as the expansion rate of the McGucken Sphere from every spacetime event. {\rule{0.7em}{0.7em}}

significance of Theorem 22.c.8. The Hawking temperature is the deepest predictive result of semiclassical quantum gravity, derived via the Wick rotation to Euclidean Schwarzschild and the conical-singularity removal procedure articulated by Gibbons-Hawking 1977 and elaborated by Gibbons 1979. The c\ensuremath{^{3}} factor in the Hawking temperature is canonically presented in the orthodox tradition as a dimensional-analysis consequence of combining G, c, \ensuremath{\hbar} in the unique way that produces a temperature; the McGucken framework supplies the physical origin of the c\ensuremath{^{3}}-factor by tracing all three factors of c to positions of dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic in the derivation. The c-half of dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic is in the deepest result of black-hole thermodynamics: c\ensuremath{^{2}} in the metric coefficient, one further c from the dimensional bridge, and one further c from the McGucken-Sphere expansion rate, combining to c\ensuremath{^{3}} in the Hawking temperature [61, Theorem 22 on the Hawking temperature as a theorem of dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic; 62, Theorem 23 on the area law and the Planck length $\ell_P = \sqrt{\hbar G/c^3}$ carrying the same c\ensuremath{^{3}}].


### §22.c.8bis. The Empirical-Ground Problem of Orthodox Euclidean Quantum Gravity and Its Dissolution Under the McGucken Principle dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic: How the Euclidean Manifold, on Which No Observer Moves and No Signal Propagates, Nevertheless Predicts Real Physical Temperature and Real Physical Entropy


The McGucken Principle dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic states the physical reality that the fourth dimension x\ensuremath{_{4}} is expanding at the velocity of light in a spherically-symmetric manner from every spacetime event, generating the McGucken Sphere at event $p$ at every event p of the real four-dimensional McGucken Manifold. The Wick rotation to the Euclidean signature is the coordinate identity \ensuremath{\tau} = x\ensuremath{_{4}}/c of Theorem 22.1, retaining the real fourth axis as a real coordinate under relabeling from x\ensuremath{_{4}}-in-length-units to \ensuremath{\tau}-in-time-units. The present subsection identifies a problem at the ground of orthodox Euclidean quantum gravity that the orthodox tradition has never resolved — the empirical-ground problem — and establishes that the problem dissolves under the McGucken Principle dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic because the three physical contents of Corollary 22.c.2.1 of §22.c.2 — the McGucken-Sphere expansion at velocity c, the perpendicularity of x\ensuremath{_{4}} to the three spatial dimensions, and the Compton-clock oscillation of the wavefront-rider amplitude at angular frequency \ensuremath{\omega}_C = mc\ensuremath{^{2}}/\ensuremath{\hbar} — are all preserved across the McWick rotation, supplying real physical referents to the Euclidean-side thermal and entropic quantities that the orthodox tradition takes for granted without articulating what makes them physical.
