#### §29.7.10.26. Differential Structure as the Physical-Realizability Substrate for dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic, with Non-Smoothable Topological 4-Manifolds Identified as Physically Forbidden Configurations, and the Six Smuggling Sites of i Throughout the Donaldson-Seiberg-Witten-Witten-Floer Framework Beyond Donaldson's Original Setup

A critical observation supplements the content of §29.7.10.25 of the present subsection: the *differential structure* on which Donaldson's framework operates is precisely the substrate on which the McGucken Principle dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic can be formulated, and the framework operates by smuggling i through every constituent piece. The present subsection establishes the two foundational findings: **Theorem 29.7.10.18 (Differential Structure as Physical-Realizability Substrate)**, identifying non-smoothable topological 4-manifolds as physically forbidden configurations within the McGucken-framework reading; and **Theorem 29.7.10.19 (Donaldson Framework Cannot Escape dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic)**, identifying six distinct sites at which i is smuggled into the Donaldson-Seiberg-Witten-Witten-Floer framework as algebraic-shadow content of the McGucken Principle.


##### §29.7.10.26.1. Differential Structure Defined — The Substrate on Which dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic Is Expressible

**Definition 29.7.10.6 (Differential Structure on a Topological 4-Manifold).** *A differential structure (equivalently, a smooth structure or C^\ensuremath{\infty} structure) on a topological 4-manifold M consists of a maximal atlas of coordinate charts {(U_\ensuremath{\alpha}, \ensuremath{\phi}_\ensuremath{\alpha})}_{\ensuremath{\alpha} \ensuremath{\in} A} with \ensuremath{\phi}_\ensuremath{\alpha}: U_\ensuremath{\alpha} \ensuremath{\rightarrow} \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}\ensuremath{^{4}} homeomorphisms onto open subsets, such that all transition functions \ensuremath{\phi}_\ensuremath{\beta} \ensuremath{\circ} \ensuremath{\phi}_\ensuremath{\alpha}\ensuremath{^{-}}\ensuremath{^{1}}: \ensuremath{\phi}_\ensuremath{\alpha}(U_\ensuremath{\alpha} \ensuremath{\cap} U_\ensuremath{\beta}) \ensuremath{\rightarrow} \ensuremath{\phi}_\ensuremath{\beta}(U_\ensuremath{\alpha} \ensuremath{\cap} U_\ensuremath{\beta}) are smooth (C^\ensuremath{\infty}) wherever defined.*

*A differential structure supplies the following mathematical content: (i) the algebra C^\ensuremath{\infty}(M, \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}) of smooth real-valued functions on M; (ii) the tangent bundle TM and cotangent bundle T*M with smooth section spaces \ensuremath{\Gamma}(TM), \ensuremath{\Gamma}(T*M); (iii) vector fields, tensor fields, and differential k-forms \ensuremath{\Omega}^k(M) for k \ensuremath{\in} {0, 1, 2, 3, 4}; (iv) the exterior derivative d: \ensuremath{\Omega}^k \ensuremath{\rightarrow} \ensuremath{\Omega}^{k+1}, the Lie derivative \ensuremath{\mathcal{L}}_X, and partial-derivative operators \ensuremath{\partial}_\ensuremath{\mu} in local coordinates; (v) the ability to define rates of change dx_i/d\ensuremath{\tau} along smooth curves x: I \ensuremath{\rightarrow} M for I \ensuremath{\subseteq} \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}; (vi) the ability to formulate and solve partial differential equations on M.*

The foundational significance of Definition 29.7.10.6 for the McGucken framework is the following: the differential structure supplies precisely the substrate on which the McGucken Principle dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic can be formulated as a meaningful kinematic statement. Without a differential structure on the topological 4-manifold underlying physical spacetime, the equation dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic cannot be written down: there is no derivative operator d/dt, no smooth coordinate x\ensuremath{_{4}}, no rate of change. Differential structure is therefore a *necessary precondition* for the McGucken Principle to be expressible.

This is not the same as saying that differential structure *is* dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic. Differential structure is strictly weaker: it is the mathematical substrate on which many different kinematic principles could be formulated; dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic is one specific principle that the substrate supports. The relationship is substrate \ensuremath{\Longrightarrow} principle-expressibility, not substrate \ensuremath{\Longleftrightarrow} principle-content.


##### §29.7.10.26.2. The Wikipedia Articulation — Primary-Source Documentation of Donaldson Theory's Smooth-Manifold Dependence

The Wikipedia encyclopedic article on Donaldson theory contains the following diagnostic statement:

> *"The results of Donaldson theory depend therefore on the manifold having a differential structure, and are largely false for topological 4-manifolds."* — Wikipedia article *Donaldson theory* [357], accessed 2026

This statement, supplied as an encyclopedic summary, articulates the mathematical fact that Donaldson's framework requires the topological 4-manifold to carry a smooth structure; on topological 4-manifolds lacking smooth structure, Donaldson's theorems do not apply. The statement is the standard contemporary mathematical-physics articulation of the differential-structure-dependence of Donaldson theory.

Under the McGucken-framework reading developed in §29.7.10.26.3 of the present subsection, the Wikipedia statement is the mathematical primary-source documentation of the physical-realizability constraint that the McGucken Principle imposes on possible spacetime topologies: Donaldson theory operates exactly on the smooth-manifold class — i.e., the class of topologies on which the McGucken Principle can be smoothly extended. For topological 4-manifolds without smooth structure, Donaldson theory fails because those topologies cannot host the McGucken Principle.


##### §29.7.10.26.3. The Differential-Structure-as-Physical-Realizability-Substrate Theorem

**Theorem 29.7.10.18 (Differential Structure as Physical-Realizability Substrate for dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic).** *Let M be a topological 4-manifold and let \ensuremath{\iota}: M \ensuremath{\rightarrow} McGucken Manifold \text{the McGucken Manifold} be a candidate identification of M with a physical-spacetime region of the real four-dimensional McGucken Manifold of the McGucken framework. *the exclusion of signature $(0,4)$ (Euclidean, four space dimensions, zero time dimensions) as a separate physical reality — it is the $\tau = x_4/c$ coordinate-identity re-reading of the same Lorentzian manifold Differential-structure necessity. For the identification \ensuremath{\iota} to be compatible with the McGucken Principle dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic operating at every event of \text{the McGucken Manifold}, the topological 4-manifold M must admit a differential (smooth) structure compatible with the smooth structure on McGucken Manifold \text{the McGucken Manifold} induced by the principle.*

*the exclusion of signature $(4,0)$ (four time dimensions, zero space dimensions) — ruled out by the empirical of dx$_4$/dt = $+ic$ operating at every event with finite velocity $c$ Smooth-structure selection. *the exclusion of signature $(2,2)$ split signature — ruled out by the $+ic$ monotonicity of dx$_4$/dt = $+ic$ Physical forbidding of non-smoothable topologies. **Proof.**

*Proof of the exclusion of signature $(0,4)$ (Euclidean, four space dimensions, zero time dimensions) as a separate physical reality — it is the $\tau = x_4/c$ coordinate-identity re-reading of the same Lorentzian manifold.* The McGucken Principle dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic involves the derivative operator d/dt applied to a coordinate function x\ensuremath{_{4}}. By Definition 29.7.10.6 of §29.7.10.26.1 of the present subsection, the derivative operator d/dt and the smooth coordinate function x\ensuremath{_{4}} require a differential structure on the underlying manifold. If the topological 4-manifold M does not admit a differential structure, then the McGucken Principle cannot be formulated on M (the principle's defining equation cannot be written down). The identification \ensuremath{\iota}: M \ensuremath{\rightarrow} McGucken Manifold \text{the McGucken Manifold} compatible with the principle therefore requires M to admit a differential structure. \ensuremath{\blacksquare} for the exclusion of signature $(0,4)$ (Euclidean, four space dimensions, zero time dimensions) as a separate physical reality — it is the $\tau = x_4/c$ coordinate-identity re-reading of the same Lorentzian manifold.

*Proof of the exclusion of signature $(4,0)$ (four time dimensions, zero space dimensions) — ruled out by the empirical of dx$_4$/dt = $+ic$ operating at every event with finite velocity $c$.* For a smoothable topological 4-manifold M admitting multiple smooth structures (the canonical example: M = \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}\ensuremath{^{4}} admitting uncountably many smooth structures by Donaldson-Freedman 1982–1983), each smooth structure supplies a distinct candidate differential substrate on M. *Proof of the exclusion of signature $(2,2)$ split signature — ruled out by the $+ic$ monotonicity of dx$_4$/dt = $+ic$.* The Freedman 1982 [349] topological classification of simply-connected closed 4-manifolds, combined with Donaldson's 1983 [346] Diagonalisation Theorem, establishes the existence of non-smoothable topological 4-manifolds. The canonical example is the Freedman E8 manifold M_{E8} — the simply-connected closed topological 4-manifold with E8 intersection form: by Freedman's topological classification, M_{E8} exists as a topological manifold; by Donaldson's Diagonalisation Theorem, any smooth simply-connected closed 4-manifold with positive-definite intersection form must have diagonalisable intersection form, but the E8 form is positive-definite and *not* diagonalisable over \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}; therefore M_{E8} cannot be smoothed. By the exclusion of signature $(0,4)$ (Euclidean, four space dimensions, zero time dimensions) as a separate physical reality — it is the $\tau = x_4/c$ coordinate-identity re-reading of the same Lorentzian manifold of the present theorem, no consistent physical-spacetime identification \ensuremath{\iota}: M_{E8} \ensuremath{\rightarrow} McGucken Manifold \text{the McGucken Manifold} compatible with dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic is possible, because M_{E8} admits no differential structure on which the principle can be formulated. M_{E8} is therefore a *physically forbidden* topological-4-manifold configuration. By extension, the broader class of non-smoothable topological 4-manifolds is physically forbidden. \ensuremath{\blacksquare} for the exclusion of signature $(2,2)$ split signature — ruled out by the $+ic$ monotonicity of dx$_4$/dt = $+ic$.

*Joint conclusion.* The three statements the exclusion of signature $(0,4)$ (Euclidean, four space dimensions, zero time dimensions) as a separate physical reality — it is the $\tau = x_4/c$ coordinate-identity re-reading of the same Lorentzian manifold, the exclusion of signature $(4,0)$ (four time dimensions, zero space dimensions) — ruled out by the empirical of dx$_4$/dt = $+ic$ operating at every event with finite velocity $c$, the exclusion of signature $(2,2)$ split signature — ruled out by the $+ic$ monotonicity of dx$_4$/dt = $+ic$ jointly establish Theorem 29.7.10.18. Differential structure is the mathematical substrate on which the McGucken Principle is expressible; the McGucken Principle selects the physical smooth structure when multiple smooth structures are available; non-smoothable topological 4-manifolds are physically forbidden by the McGucken framework. \ensuremath{\blacksquare}

significance of Theorem 29.7.10.18. The theorem supplies a *sharp testable prediction* of the McGucken framework at the spacetime-topology level: the universe's spacetime manifold must be smoothable. Any future cosmological, quantum-gravity, or physics proposal that postulates a non-smoothable topology for spacetime — for example, attempting to accommodate E8-type topological structure as a fundamental feature of the universe — is ruled out under the McGucken-framework reading. The differential-structure requirement is a *physical-realizability constraint*: the McGucken Principle dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic cannot be formulated on a non-smoothable topology, and therefore cannot generate the empirical physics of the universe on such a topology. The Wikipedia statement of §29.7.10.26.2 — *"the results of Donaldson theory depend therefore on the manifold having a differential structure, and are largely false for topological 4-manifolds"* — is, under the McGucken-framework reading, the mathematical articulation of this physical-realizability constraint: Donaldson theory operates exactly on the physically-realizable topology class.

##### §29.7.10.26.5. The Donaldson-Framework-Cannot-Escape-dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt=ic Theorem

**Theorem 29.7.10.19 (Donaldson-Seiberg-Witten-Witten-Floer Framework Cannot Escape dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic).** *The Donaldson-Seiberg-Witten-Witten-Floer framework — encompassing the original Donaldson 1983–1986 anti-self-dual instanton moduli-space framework [346, 347, 351], the Seiberg-Witten 1994 [353] spinor-and-electromagnetic-coupling reformulation, the Witten 1988 [354] topological-quantum-field-theory derivation, and the Atiyah-Floer symplectic-Floer-homology connection — smuggles the imaginary unit i through six central sites (26.4\ensuremath{\alpha})–(26.4\ensuremath{\zeta}) catalogued in §29.7.10.26.4 of the present subsection. Each smuggling site is identified under Theorem 29.7.10.15 of §29.7.10.23.2 as a local algebraic-shadow descendant of dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic. The framework therefore cannot be formulated without smuggling the algebraic-shadow content of the McGucken Principle, even though the framework's surface presentation as "Euclidean Riemannian gauge theory" suppresses the physical-geometric source.*

**Proof.** By case analysis on each of the six smuggling sites (26.4\ensuremath{\alpha})–(26.4\ensuremath{\zeta}) catalogued in §29.7.10.26.4 of the present subsection.

*Site (\ensuremath{\alpha}) — SU(2) gauge group.* Donaldson's framework cannot be formulated without the SU(2) gauge group: the anti-self-dual instanton moduli spaces \ensuremath{\mathcal{M}}_k are defined as quotients of the affine space of SU(2) connections modulo gauge transformations. Removing SU(2) eliminates the framework's defining mathematical objects. By the Lie-algebra construction \ensuremath{\mathfrak{s}}\ensuremath{\mathfrak{u}}(2) = span{i\ensuremath{\sigma}_a/2}, the i is unavoidable in the connection 1-form A_\ensuremath{\mu}. \ensuremath{\blacksquare} for site (\ensuremath{\alpha}).

The ∗\ensuremath{^{2}} = +1 splitting \ensuremath{\Lambda}\ensuremath{^{2}} = \ensuremath{\Lambda}\ensuremath{^{+}} \ensuremath{\oplus} \ensuremath{\Lambda}\ensuremath{^{-}} is the algebraic prerequisite for the equation to make sense. #### §29.7.10.27. The Seven Sites of i-Smuggling in Donaldson's Fields-Medal-Winning Diagonalization Theorem (1983) — The Historical Documentation that the Most-Famous Theorem of Contemporary Dimension-4 Mathematics Cannot Be Proven Without the Algebraic-Shadow Content of dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic

The foundational claim of §29.7.10.26 of the present subsection — that the Donaldson-Seiberg-Witten-Witten-Floer framework as a whole smuggles i throughout its constituents — admits a sharpened version at the most-prestigious recognition site of contemporary mathematics: the Fields-Medal-winning *Donaldson's Diagonalization Theorem* of 1983 [346]. The present subsection establishes the Seven-Sites-of-i-Smuggling Audit of the diagonalization theorem's proof, demonstrating that the Fields-Medal-winning theorem cannot be proven without the algebraic-shadow content of dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic appearing at seven central sites of the proof itself.

##### §29.7.10.27.1. Statement of Donaldson's Diagonalization Theorem (1983) — The Fields-Medal-Winning Result

**Theorem (Donaldson 1983 [346] — Donaldson's Diagonalization Theorem).** *Let M be a smooth compact simply-connected oriented 4-manifold with positive-definite intersection form Q: H\ensuremath{^{2}}(M, \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}) \ensuremath{\times} H\ensuremath{^{2}}(M, \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}) \ensuremath{\rightarrow} \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}. Then Q is diagonalisable over \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}; equivalently, Q is isomorphic to the standard Euclidean form \ensuremath{\bigoplus}_{k=1}^{b\ensuremath{^{2}}(M)} \ensuremath{\langle}1\ensuremath{\rangle}.*

The theorem is the mathematical content for which Donaldson was awarded the 1986 Fields Medal. Combined with the Freedman 1982 [349] topological classification of simply-connected closed 4-manifolds, the theorem yields the existence of exotic \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}\ensuremath{^{4}} (uncountably many smooth structures on \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}\ensuremath{^{4}}) and supplies the mathematical content for the four-decade development of contemporary dimension-4 differential topology.

The proof, developed in Donaldson 1983 [346] and consolidated in the canonical Donaldson-Kronheimer 1990 monograph [351], proceeds by analysing the moduli space \ensuremath{\mathcal{M}}_1 of anti-self-dual SU(2) instantons with instanton number k = 1 on M. Donaldson establishes that \ensuremath{\mathcal{M}}_1 has the structure of an open 5-manifold whose "ends" are modelled on certain cone-like neighbourhoods, with the boundary structure controlled by the intersection form Q. The cobordism argument constraining \ensuremath{\mathcal{M}}_1's structure yields the diagonalisability of Q.

The present subsection audits the seven central sites of the proof at which the imaginary unit i is smuggled into the argument.

##### §29.7.10.27.2. Site 1 — The SU(2) Gauge Group as Donaldson's Central Computational Object

The first and most fundamental site at which i is smuggled into Donaldson's proof is the SU(2) gauge group itself, which serves as Donaldson's central computational object throughout the proof.

The anti-self-dual instanton moduli space \ensuremath{\mathcal{M}}_k(M, g) is defined per Definition 29.7.10.5 of §29.7.10.25.1 of the present subsection as the space of gauge-equivalence classes of SU(2) connections satisfying F\ensuremath{^{+}} = 0 with c\ensuremath{_{2}}(P) = k. The connection 1-form A_\ensuremath{\mu} takes values in \ensuremath{\mathfrak{s}}\ensuremath{\mathfrak{u}}(2), the Lie algebra of SU(2). By the explicit basis:

\ensuremath{\mathfrak{s}}\ensuremath{\mathfrak{u}}(2) = span{i\ensuremath{\sigma}_x/2, i\ensuremath{\sigma}_y/2, i\ensuremath{\sigma}_z/2},

every component of A_\ensuremath{\mu} at every spacetime point of M has i as an explicit multiplicative factor. The connection therefore decomposes as A_\ensuremath{\mu} = (i/2)(A_\ensuremath{\mu}^1 \ensuremath{\sigma}_x + A_\ensuremath{\mu}^2 \ensuremath{\sigma}_y + A_\ensuremath{\mu}^3 \ensuremath{\sigma}_z) with real-valued component functions A_\ensuremath{\mu}^a, with the *i* in the front making the connection take values in the anti-Hermitian (rather than Hermitian) matrices.

The curvature 2-form F = dA + A \ensuremath{\wedge} A inherits the i-content via the Lie-algebra structure: F is also valued in \ensuremath{\mathfrak{s}}\ensuremath{\mathfrak{u}}(2), with the i appearing throughout the curvature components. The Yang-Mills action S_{YM} = (1/g\ensuremath{^{2}}) \ensuremath{\int}_M |F|\ensuremath{^{2}} dvol involves the norm |F|\ensuremath{^{2}} computed via the Killing form on \ensuremath{\mathfrak{s}}\ensuremath{\mathfrak{u}}(2), with the negative-trace pairing −tr(AB) = tr(H_A H_B) (after factoring out the i\ensuremath{^{2}}s) yielding a positive-definite inner product — *but the i\ensuremath{^{2}}= −1 algebraic-shadow content is essential for the Killing form's positivity on \ensuremath{\mathfrak{s}}\ensuremath{\mathfrak{u}}(2)*.

Removing i from Donaldson's proof at Site 1 would eliminate the SU(2) gauge group as a meaningful object: \ensuremath{\mathfrak{s}}\ensuremath{\mathfrak{u}}(2) without the i would not be a Lie algebra of anti-Hermitian matrices, and SU(2) would not be the structure group of the principal bundle that Donaldson works with. Site 1 is unavoidable: Donaldson's framework is defined in terms of SU(2), and SU(2) requires i.

##### §29.7.10.27.3. Site 2 — The Chern Character in the Atiyah-Singer Index Calculation of dim \ensuremath{\mathcal{M}}_k

The second site at which i is smuggled into Donaldson's proof is the Chern character calculation in the Atiyah-Singer index theorem application that supplies the dimension formula for \ensuremath{\mathcal{M}}_k.

The dimension of the instanton moduli space \ensuremath{\mathcal{M}}_k is computed via the Atiyah-Hitchin-Singer 1978 [350] index calculation applied to the elliptic deformation complex of the anti-self-dual equation. The result is:

dim \ensuremath{\mathcal{M}}_k(M, g) = 8k − 3(1 + b\ensuremath{^{+}}(M)),

where b\ensuremath{^{+}}(M) is the dimension of the positive-definite part of the intersection form on H\ensuremath{^{2}}(M, \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}). The "8k" term comes from the Chern character calculation of the relevant Dirac operator's index, with:

ch(E) = tr(exp(iF/(2\ensuremath{\pi}))) = rank(E) + (i/(2\ensuremath{\pi})) tr(F) + (1/2)(i/(2\ensuremath{\pi}))\ensuremath{^{2}} tr(F \ensuremath{\wedge} F) + (1/6)(i/(2\ensuremath{\pi}))\ensuremath{^{3}} tr(F \ensuremath{\wedge} F \ensuremath{\wedge} F) + \ensuremath{\cdots}

The imaginary unit i appears explicitly in the exponent of the Chern character. Each term in the Chern-character expansion contains i raised to a power equal to the form degree of the term: (i)\ensuremath{^{1}} for tr(F), (i)\ensuremath{^{2}} = −1 for tr(F \ensuremath{\wedge} F), (i)\ensuremath{^{3}} = −i for tr(F \ensuremath{\wedge} F \ensuremath{\wedge} F), and so on. The signs of the terms in the Chern-character expansion alternate via i^k = i, −1, −i, +1, … — and these signs are essential for the index calculation to yield the correct integer value dim \ensuremath{\mathcal{M}}_k = 8k − 3(1 + b\ensuremath{^{+}}).

Removing i from the Chern character (replacing exp(iF/(2\ensuremath{\pi})) by exp(F/(2\ensuremath{\pi}))) would eliminate the sign-alternation structure, producing instead a real-valued exponential series that does not converge to the correct Chern character. The Atiyah-Singer index theorem application that supplies Donaldson's dimension formula requires i throughout the Chern-character computation.

##### §29.7.10.27.4. Site 3 — The Instanton Number c\ensuremath{_{2}}(P) via the Second Chern Class with Explicit i\ensuremath{^{2}} = −1

The third site at which i is smuggled into Donaldson's proof is the instanton-number / second Chern class identification, which uses i\ensuremath{^{2}} = −1 algebraic-shadow content in an essential way.

The instanton number k \ensuremath{\in} \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}} of an SU(2) connection on M is identified with the second Chern class c\ensuremath{_{2}}(P) \ensuremath{\in} H\ensuremath{^{4}}(M, \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}) \ensuremath{\cong} \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}. The explicit formula:

k = c\ensuremath{_{2}}(P) = (1/(8\ensuremath{\pi}\ensuremath{^{2}})) \ensuremath{\int}_M tr(F \ensuremath{\wedge} F).

Computing tr(F \ensuremath{\wedge} F) where F = i \ensuremath{\times} (Hermitian) is the \ensuremath{\mathfrak{s}}\ensuremath{\mathfrak{u}}(2)-valued curvature, we have F \ensuremath{\wedge} F = (iH)\ensuremath{\wedge}(iH) = i\ensuremath{^{2}} (H \ensuremath{\wedge} H) = −(H \ensuremath{\wedge} H), so:

tr(F \ensuremath{\wedge} F) = −tr(H \ensuremath{\wedge} H).

The minus sign in tr(F \ensuremath{\wedge} F) comes directly from i\ensuremath{^{2}} = −1. This minus sign is essential for the instanton number to be an integer: without the i\ensuremath{^{2}} = −1 algebraic shadow, the integrand tr(F \ensuremath{\wedge} F) would not have the sign structure needed to produce \ensuremath{\int}_M tr(F \ensuremath{\wedge} F) = 8\ensuremath{\pi}\ensuremath{^{2}} k with k \ensuremath{\in} \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}.

Removing i\ensuremath{^{2}} = −1 from the calculation would change the sign of tr(F \ensuremath{\wedge} F), eliminating the integer-valuedness of the instanton number and destroying the topological-class structure that Donaldson's framework relies on for the c\ensuremath{_{2}}(P) = k identification.

##### §29.7.10.27.5. Site 4 — The Ends of \ensuremath{\mathcal{M}}_1 Modeled on cone(\ensuremath{\mathbb{C}}\ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}\ensuremath{^{2}}) — The Critical Step

The fourth site at which i is smuggled into Donaldson's proof — and the most critical site of the entire argument — is the analysis of the ends of the moduli space \ensuremath{\mathcal{M}}_1 as modelled on cone(\ensuremath{\mathbb{C}}\ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}\ensuremath{^{2}}).

Donaldson's argument proceeds as follows: \ensuremath{\mathcal{M}}_1, the moduli space of anti-self-dual SU(2) instantons with instanton number k = 1 on M, is an open 5-manifold (under generic perturbation of the metric g). The "ends" of \ensuremath{\mathcal{M}}_1 — the points where the moduli space exits to infinity — are of two types: (a) the asymptotic end where the instanton concentrates at a point in M and shrinks (the "Uhlenbeck end"), and (b) the *reducible-connection ends*, which correspond to points where the SU(2) connection reduces to a U(1) \ensuremath{\oplus} U(1) connection in correspondence with a generator of the intersection form on H\ensuremath{^{2}}(M, \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}).

The critical content of Donaldson's argument is that each reducible-connection end of \ensuremath{\mathcal{M}}_1 has a neighbourhood modelled on the open cone cone(\ensuremath{\mathbb{C}}\ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}\ensuremath{^{2}}) = (0, \ensuremath{\varepsilon}) \ensuremath{\times} \ensuremath{\mathbb{C}}\ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}\ensuremath{^{2}}, where \ensuremath{\mathbb{C}}\ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}\ensuremath{^{2}} is the complex projective plane. The argument then uses the topology of cone(\ensuremath{\mathbb{C}}\ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}\ensuremath{^{2}}) — specifically, the structure of \ensuremath{\mathbb{C}}\ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}\ensuremath{^{2}} as a closed 4-manifold with intersection form \ensuremath{\langle}+1\ensuremath{\rangle} (positive-definite, one-dimensional) — to constrain the topology of M via a cobordism argument.

\ensuremath{\mathbb{C}}\ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}\ensuremath{^{2}} is fundamentally complex-geometric: it is defined as \ensuremath{\mathbb{C}}\ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}\ensuremath{^{2}} = (\ensuremath{\mathbb{C}}\ensuremath{^{3}} \ensuremath{\setminus} {0})/\ensuremath{\mathbb{C}}^*, the projective space of one-dimensional complex subspaces of \ensuremath{\mathbb{C}}\ensuremath{^{3}}. The construction of \ensuremath{\mathbb{C}}\ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}\ensuremath{^{2}} requires the field \ensuremath{\mathbb{C}} = \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}} + i\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}} throughout. Donaldson's argument runs through \ensuremath{\mathbb{C}}\ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}\ensuremath{^{2}} in an essential way at each reducible-connection end of \ensuremath{\mathcal{M}}_1, with the cobordism argument depending on the complex-projective structure of \ensuremath{\mathbb{C}}\ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}\ensuremath{^{2}}.

Removing i from Donaldson's proof at Site 4 would eliminate \ensuremath{\mathbb{C}}\ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}\ensuremath{^{2}} (which does not exist without \ensuremath{\mathbb{C}}), eliminating the cone(\ensuremath{\mathbb{C}}\ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}\ensuremath{^{2}}) end-structure of \ensuremath{\mathcal{M}}_1 and breaking the cobordism argument that constrains the intersection form Q on H\ensuremath{^{2}}(M, \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}). The Fields-Medal-winning conclusion that Q must be diagonalisable cannot be reached without the cone(\ensuremath{\mathbb{C}}\ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}\ensuremath{^{2}}) end-analysis, and the end-analysis cannot proceed without \ensuremath{\mathbb{C}}.

##### §29.7.10.27.6. Site 5 — Uhlenbeck's Compactification via Coulomb-Gauge Fixing with Complex-Analytic Apparatus

The fifth site at which i is smuggled into Donaldson's proof is Uhlenbeck's 1982 removable-singularities theorem [355], which Donaldson uses to construct the compactification of \ensuremath{\mathcal{M}}_1 and to analyse the Uhlenbeck end of the moduli space.

Uhlenbeck's theorem establishes that anti-self-dual SU(2) connections on the 4-ball B\ensuremath{^{4}}, with finite L\ensuremath{^{2}} Yang-Mills action, extend smoothly across point singularities after suitable gauge transformations. The analysis proceeds via complex-analytic techniques applied to the gauge-transformation group: local trivialisations of the principal bundle are analysed using holomorphic gauge transformations on complexified coordinate charts, with the Dolbeault operator \ensuremath{\partial}̄ appearing in the analysis of regularity.

The Coulomb-gauge condition d*A = 0 implicitly uses the (1, 0)/(0, 1) splitting of complexified 1-forms on the underlying 4-manifold via the choice of an almost-complex structure on the local chart. The i appears through the complex-analytic structure on the gauge-transformation group U(C^\ensuremath{\infty}(B\ensuremath{^{4}}, SU(2))) and through the Dolbeault operator \ensuremath{\partial}̄.

Removing i from Uhlenbeck's compactification would eliminate the complex-analytic techniques used in the proof of the removable-singularities theorem, eliminating Donaldson's ability to compactify the moduli space \ensuremath{\mathcal{M}}_1 and to analyse its Uhlenbeck end.

##### §29.7.10.27.10. The Historical Significance — The Fields Medal Awarded for a Theorem Whose Proof Depends Entirely on the Algebraic-Shadow Content of the McGucken Principle

The historical significance of Theorem 29.7.10.20 of §29.7.10.27.9 of the present subsection consolidates into the following composite observation.

**Observation 29.7.10.4 (Fields-Medal Recognition of a Theorem Requiring dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic's Algebraic Shadows Without Articulating the Foundational Source).** *The Fields Medal — the most prestigious recognition of mathematical-content in contemporary mathematics — was awarded to Donaldson in 1986 for a theorem whose proof depends essentially on the algebraic-shadow content of the McGucken Principle dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic at seven central sites (Sites 1–7 of §§29.7.10.27.2–29.7.10.27.8 of the present subsection). ##### §29.7.10.28.1. The Configuration-Class Refinement for the Lorentzian-Metric Question

*\ensuremath{\mathcal{Q}}_LEP:= {C = (M, g, \ensuremath{\tau}, dx_i/d\ensuremath{\tau}) \ensuremath{\in} \ensuremath{\mathcal{Q}}: g is a smooth Lorentzian metric of signature (−, +, +, +) on M, AND empirical physics (E_R) and (E_QM) are realised on C},*

*where:*

*(E_QM) Empirical quantum mechanics content: (E_QM1) wavefunctions \ensuremath{\psi}(x, t) evolving in time via Schrödinger evolution i\ensuremath{\hbar} \ensuremath{\partial}_t \ensuremath{\psi} = Ĥ\ensuremath{\psi} with non-trivial temporal dependence \ensuremath{\partial}_t \ensuremath{\psi} \ensuremath{\neq} 0 in general; (E_QM2) Heisenberg uncertainty principle [q̂, p̂] = i\ensuremath{\hbar} I with Planck's constant \ensuremath{\hbar} \ensuremath{\approx} 1.055 \ensuremath{\times} 10\ensuremath{^{-}}\ensuremath{^{3}}\ensuremath{^{4}} J\ensuremath{\cdot}s; (E_QM3) Feynman path integral \ensuremath{\langle}x_f, t_f | x_i, t_i\ensuremath{\rangle} = \ensuremath{\int}\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}[\ensuremath{\gamma}] exp(iS[\ensuremath{\gamma}]/\ensuremath{\hbar}) with action functional S[\ensuremath{\gamma}] evaluated along smooth paths \ensuremath{\gamma}(t).*

**Definition 29.7.10.8 (The Static-Lorentzian-Metric Sub-Class \ensuremath{\mathcal{Q}}_LEP-static).** *The hypothetical sub-class \ensuremath{\mathcal{Q}}_LEP-static:= \ensuremath{\mathcal{Q}}_LEP \ensuremath{\cap} \ensuremath{\mathcal{Q}}_static of configurations purporting to satisfy both the Lorentzian-empirical-physics content (E_R) and (E_QM) and the static-foursome condition dx_i/d\ensuremath{\tau} = 0 for all i \ensuremath{\in} {1, 2, 3, 4}.*

##### §29.7.10.28.2. Theorem 29.7.10.21 — The Lorentzian Metric of Empirical Relativity and Quantum Mechanics Requires an Active Dimension

**Theorem 29.7.10.21 (Lorentzian-Empirical-Physics Active-Dimension Necessity).** *The sub-class \ensuremath{\mathcal{Q}}_LEP-static of Definition 29.7.10.8 of §29.7.10.28.1 of the present subsection is empty. That is: no configuration C \ensuremath{\in} \ensuremath{\mathcal{Q}}_static (with all four coordinates static relative to \ensuremath{\tau}) can support the empirical content (E_R) of special relativity together with the empirical content (E_QM) of quantum mechanics. Equivalently: any configuration supporting the empirical Lorentzian-metric physics (E_R) and (E_QM) must satisfy C \ensuremath{\in} \ensuremath{\mathcal{Q}}_active, with at least one coordinate x_j satisfying dx_j/d\ensuremath{\tau} \ensuremath{\neq} 0.*

**Proof.** Suppose, for the sake of deriving a contradiction, that there exists a configuration C* \ensuremath{\in} \ensuremath{\mathcal{Q}}_LEP-static. Then C* is a static-foursome configuration (dx_i/d\ensuremath{\tau} = 0 for all i \ensuremath{\in} {1, 2, 3, 4}) with a smooth Lorentzian metric g of signature (−, +, +, +) that supports empirical content (E_R) and (E_QM). We derive five distinct contradictions, each independently sufficient to refute the existence of C*.

*Contradiction A — Lorentz transformations require relative motion between frames, which requires temporal evolution.* By (E_R1), C* supports Lorentz transformations connecting inertial frames in relative motion at velocities |v| < c with \ensuremath{\gamma} = 1/\ensuremath{\surd}(1 − v\ensuremath{^{2}}/c\ensuremath{^{2}}) finite for v \ensuremath{\neq} 0. By construction, the *notion of "relative motion between frames"* requires that the spatial coordinates (x\ensuremath{_{1}}, x\ensuremath{_{2}}, x\ensuremath{_{3}}) of one inertial frame transform into the spatial coordinates (x\ensuremath{_{1}}', x\ensuremath{_{2}}', x\ensuremath{_{3}}') of another inertial frame, with the transformation depending on the elapsed time-coordinate parameter — that is, the Lorentz boost mixes a spatial coordinate with the time coordinate by an amount proportional to v \ensuremath{\cdot} t. The mixing equation x' = \ensuremath{\gamma}(x − vt) requires that t (or equivalently x\ensuremath{^{0}} = ct or x\ensuremath{_{4}} = ict) be a coordinate that *advances* relative to the evolution parameter \ensuremath{\tau}; if t did not advance relative to \ensuremath{\tau} (i.e., dt/d\ensuremath{\tau} = 0), then the term −vt in the Lorentz transformation would not vary along the worldline parametrised by \ensuremath{\tau}, and the relative-motion content of the Lorentz transformation would be empty. By the static-foursome condition dx_i/d\ensuremath{\tau} = 0 for all i \ensuremath{\in} {1, 2, 3, 4} on C*, the time-like coordinate (whichever of x\ensuremath{_{0}}, x\ensuremath{_{1}}, x\ensuremath{_{2}}, x\ensuremath{_{3}}, x\ensuremath{_{4}} is identified with the time direction in the chosen orientation of g) does not advance relative to \ensuremath{\tau}, so the relative-motion content of (E_R1) cannot be supplied by C*. Contradiction with (E_R1). \ensuremath{\blacksquare} for Contradiction A.

*Contradiction B — Null light cones with photon propagation require photons to actually propagate.* By (E_R2), C* supports null light cones at every event with photon propagation along null worldlines satisfying ds\ensuremath{^{2}} = 0. By construction, a "photon propagating along a null worldline" is a worldline \ensuremath{\gamma}: I \ensuremath{\rightarrow} M parametrised by an affine parameter \ensuremath{\lambda}, with \ensuremath{\gamma}̇^\ensuremath{\mu} \ensuremath{\gamma}̇^\ensuremath{\nu} g_{\ensuremath{\mu}\ensuremath{\nu}} = 0 (null condition) and \ensuremath{\gamma}̇^\ensuremath{\mu} \ensuremath{\neq} 0 (the photon's tangent vector is non-zero — the photon is actually moving). The condition \ensuremath{\gamma}̇^\ensuremath{\mu} \ensuremath{\neq} 0 in turn requires that at least one of the coordinates x^\ensuremath{\mu} along \ensuremath{\gamma} has non-zero derivative dx^\ensuremath{\mu}/d\ensuremath{\lambda}. If the affine parameter \ensuremath{\lambda} is identified with the evolution parameter \ensuremath{\tau} (or with a worldline-parameter compatible with \ensuremath{\tau}), then the photon's coordinates must satisfy dx^\ensuremath{\mu}/d\ensuremath{\tau} \ensuremath{\neq} 0 along \ensuremath{\gamma}. By the static-foursome condition dx_i/d\ensuremath{\tau} = 0 for all i \ensuremath{\in} {1, 2, 3, 4} on C*, the photon's tangent vector along \ensuremath{\gamma} would be identically zero, contradicting the requirement that the photon actually propagates. Contradiction with (E_R2). \ensuremath{\blacksquare} for Contradiction B.

*Contradiction C — The Einstein dispersion relation E\ensuremath{^{2}} = (pc)\ensuremath{^{2}} + (mc\ensuremath{^{2}})\ensuremath{^{2}} requires energy and momentum as kinematic quantities.* By (E_R3), C* supports the dispersion relation E\ensuremath{^{2}} = (pc)\ensuremath{^{2}} + (mc\ensuremath{^{2}})\ensuremath{^{2}} with c the empirically-measured velocity of light. By the standard relativistic-mechanics derivation, the energy E = \ensuremath{\gamma}mc\ensuremath{^{2}} and the momentum p = \ensuremath{\gamma}mv with v the spatial velocity of the particle, \ensuremath{\gamma} = 1/\ensuremath{\surd}(1 − v\ensuremath{^{2}}/c\ensuremath{^{2}}) the Lorentz factor; the spatial velocity v is the rate of change of spatial position with respect to time, v = dx_spatial/dt. If the time coordinate does not advance relative to \ensuremath{\tau} (i.e., dt/d\ensuremath{\tau} = 0 on C*), then dx_spatial/dt is undefined (zero divided by zero), and the spatial-velocity v has no operational content. Without v, the Lorentz factor \ensuremath{\gamma} is undefined, and the energy-momentum (E, p) cannot be assigned to physical particles. The Einstein dispersion relation E\ensuremath{^{2}} = (pc)\ensuremath{^{2}} + (mc\ensuremath{^{2}})\ensuremath{^{2}} therefore has no operational content on C*. Contradiction with (E_R3). \ensuremath{\blacksquare} for Contradiction C.

*Contradiction D — The Schrödinger equation requires non-trivial temporal evolution of wavefunctions.* By (E_QM1), C* supports wavefunctions \ensuremath{\psi}(x, t) evolving in time via the Schrödinger equation i\ensuremath{\hbar} \ensuremath{\partial}_t \ensuremath{\psi} = Ĥ\ensuremath{\psi}, with non-trivial temporal dependence \ensuremath{\partial}_t \ensuremath{\psi} \ensuremath{\neq} 0 in general. The partial-derivative operator \ensuremath{\partial}_t acting on \ensuremath{\psi} along a worldline parametrised by \ensuremath{\tau} is, by the chain rule, \ensuremath{\partial}_t \ensuremath{\psi} = (\ensuremath{\partial}\ensuremath{\psi}/\ensuremath{\partial}\ensuremath{\tau}) \ensuremath{\cdot} (d\ensuremath{\tau}/dt). If dt/d\ensuremath{\tau} = 0 on C* (static-foursome condition applied to the time-like coordinate), then d\ensuremath{\tau}/dt is undefined (zero divided by zero) and \ensuremath{\partial}_t \ensuremath{\psi} has no operational content. Equivalently, applying \ensuremath{\partial}_t directly to \ensuremath{\psi}(x(\ensuremath{\tau}), t(\ensuremath{\tau})) along the worldline via the chain rule gives \ensuremath{\partial}_t \ensuremath{\psi} = (\ensuremath{\partial}\ensuremath{\psi}/\ensuremath{\partial}x^\ensuremath{\mu}) (dx^\ensuremath{\mu}/dt), which is identically zero if dx^\ensuremath{\mu}/dt = 0 for all \ensuremath{\mu} (which holds under the static-foursome condition). The Schrödinger equation i\ensuremath{\hbar} \ensuremath{\partial}_t \ensuremath{\psi} = Ĥ\ensuremath{\psi} would then reduce to 0 = Ĥ\ensuremath{\psi}, requiring all states \ensuremath{\psi} to be zero-energy eigenstates of Ĥ — contradicting the empirical content that wavefunctions support a continuous energy spectrum with non-zero eigenvalues. Contradiction with (E_QM1). \ensuremath{\blacksquare} for Contradiction D.

*Contradiction E — The Feynman path integral requires propagation between distinct spacetime points.* By (E_QM3), C* supports the Feynman path integral \ensuremath{\langle}x_f, t_f | x_i, t_i\ensuremath{\rangle} = \ensuremath{\int}\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}[\ensuremath{\gamma}] exp(iS[\ensuremath{\gamma}]/\ensuremath{\hbar}) with the action functional evaluated along smooth paths \ensuremath{\gamma}(t) connecting initial event (x_i, t_i) to final event (x_f, t_f). The path-integral amplitude is non-trivial only if t_f \ensuremath{\neq} t_i (paths exist that connect distinct time-coordinate values). By the static-foursome condition dt/d\ensuremath{\tau} = 0 on C*, the time coordinate has zero rate of advance relative to \ensuremath{\tau}, so for any pair of events on a worldline parametrised by \ensuremath{\tau}, the time-coordinate values t at the two events are identical — t_f = t_i for any \ensuremath{\tau}_f \ensuremath{\neq} \ensuremath{\tau}_i. The path integral then reduces to \ensuremath{\langle}x_f, t_i | x_i, t_i\ensuremath{\rangle} = \ensuremath{\delta}(x_f − x_i), the trivial delta-function amplitude with no propagation content. The empirical content of (E_QM3) — non-trivial path-integral amplitudes describing quantum-mechanical propagation — is therefore unrealisable on C*. Contradiction with (E_QM3). \ensuremath{\blacksquare} for Contradiction E.

*Joint conclusion.* The five contradictions A, B, C, D, E are each independently sufficient to refute the existence of C*. The supposition that C* \ensuremath{\in} \ensuremath{\mathcal{Q}}_LEP-static is non-empty is therefore false: the sub-class \ensuremath{\mathcal{Q}}_LEP-static is empty. By the configuration-class decomposition \ensuremath{\mathcal{Q}} = \ensuremath{\mathcal{Q}}_static \ensuremath{\sqcup} \ensuremath{\mathcal{Q}}_active per Definition 29.7.10.3 of §29.7.10.17.1, any configuration supporting the empirical content (E_R) and (E_QM) must satisfy C \ensuremath{\in} \ensuremath{\mathcal{Q}}_active, with at least one coordinate x_j \ensuremath{\in} {x\ensuremath{_{1}}, x\ensuremath{_{2}}, x\ensuremath{_{3}}, x\ensuremath{_{4}}} satisfying dx_j/d\ensuremath{\tau} \ensuremath{\neq} 0. \ensuremath{\blacksquare}

significance of Theorem 29.7.10.21. The theorem establishes that the Lorentzian metric of empirical relativity and quantum mechanics cannot exist on a static foursome of coordinates — the metric requires at least one actively-advancing dimension. This is a sharper version of the spinor-specific Static-Foursome No-Go Theorem 29.7.10.11 of §29.7.10.17.2: not only spinor physics, but the *entire empirical content* of special relativity and quantum mechanics (Lorentz transformations, light cones, dispersion relation, Schrödinger equation, path integral) requires C \ensuremath{\in} \ensuremath{\mathcal{Q}}_active. The contrapositive form supplies the physical statement: if the universe had a fully-static foursome of spacetime coordinates, the Lorentzian-metric physics we empirically observe — including special relativity, quantum mechanics, and the entire empirical content of physics — could not exist.

ds\ensuremath{^{2}} = (dx\ensuremath{_{1}})\ensuremath{^{2}} + (dx\ensuremath{_{2}})\ensuremath{^{2}} + (dx\ensuremath{_{3}})\ensuremath{^{2}} + (dx\ensuremath{_{4}})\ensuremath{^{2}} = (dx\ensuremath{_{1}})\ensuremath{^{2}} + (dx\ensuremath{_{2}})\ensuremath{^{2}} + (dx\ensuremath{_{3}})\ensuremath{^{2}} + (ic dt)\ensuremath{^{2}} = (dx\ensuremath{_{1}})\ensuremath{^{2}} + (dx\ensuremath{_{2}})\ensuremath{^{2}} + (dx\ensuremath{_{3}})\ensuremath{^{2}} − c\ensuremath{^{2}}(dt)\ensuremath{^{2}},

##### §29.7.10.28.4. Huygens' Reciprocal-Generative Wavefront Iteration — Lemma 29.7.10.13

The content of Huygens' principle (Huygens 1690 [82]) is the *every-point-as-secondary-source* mechanism: every point on a propagating wavefront is itself a source of secondary spherical wavelets, with the wavefront at later times being the envelope of these secondary wavelets. Under the McGucken-framework reading, this principle is the mechanism by which the McGucken-Sphere expansion self-iterates across the universe.

##### §29.7.10.28.5. Theorem 29.7.10.22 — The Physical Imaginary Unit Requires the McGucken-Sphere-Generating Active Expansion with Huygens-Iteration

The content of Lemma 29.7.10.12 (i as algebraic generator of the McGucken-Sphere) and Lemma 29.7.10.13 (Huygens' principle as self-iteration of the McGucken-Sphere expansion) consolidates into the following theorem establishing the necessity-of-active-expansion-with-Huygens-iteration for the physical content of the imaginary unit.

**Theorem 29.7.10.22 (Physical Imaginary Unit Requires McGucken-Sphere-Generating Active Expansion with Huygens-Iteration).** *The imaginary unit i, when serving as the physical-geometric content of physics (not merely as a formal algebraic device with i\ensuremath{^{2}} = −1), requires the following three conditions on the underlying configuration C \ensuremath{\in} \ensuremath{\mathcal{Q}}:*

*the first Nelson obstacle — that the Brownian motion in Nelson's framework is on configuration space $\mathbb{R}^3$ with time as an external parameter, not on spacetime Active dimension — C \ensuremath{\in} \ensuremath{\mathcal{Q}}_active, with at least one coordinate x_j satisfying dx_j/d\ensuremath{\tau} \ensuremath{\neq} 0 along worldlines of C, per Theorem 29.7.10.12 of §29.7.10.17.3 of the present subsection.*

*the second Nelson obstacle — that Nelson's drift velocity is supplied as an empirical parameter and is not derived from a physical principle McGucken-Sphere generation — The active dimension's rate satisfies dx_j/d\ensuremath{\tau} = ic at velocity c (per Theorem 29.7.10.10 of §29.7.10.15 of the present subsection); the i in this rate-expression generates the McGucken-Sphere expansion via the four-step chain the four-step derivation chain from dx$_4$/dt = ic to the Lorentzian null-surface structure — squaring to $i^2 = -1$, deriving the Lorentzian line element, obtaining the null-surface existence condition, and identifying the McGucken-Sphere expansion as the null-surface family of Lemma 29.7.10.12 of §29.7.10.28.3 of the present subsection.*

*the third Nelson obstacle — that Nelson did not connect his stochastic mechanics to the Second Law of thermodynamics Huygens-iteration — The McGucken Principle operates at every event of the McGucken Manifold; the resulting self-iteration of the McGucken-Sphere expansion via Huygens' principle (Lemma 29.7.10.13 of §29.7.10.28.4) supplies the globally-defined perpendicular-to-the-local-wavefront structure at every point on every wavefront simultaneously.*

*On a static-foursome configuration C \ensuremath{\in} \ensuremath{\mathcal{Q}}_static, none of the first Nelson obstacle — that the Brownian motion in Nelson's framework is on configuration space $\mathbb{R}^3$ with time as an external parameter, not on spacetime, the second Nelson obstacle — that Nelson's drift velocity is supplied as an empirical parameter and is not derived from a physical principle, the third Nelson obstacle — that Nelson did not connect his stochastic mechanics to the Second Law of thermodynamics can be realised: no active dimension exists (failure of N1); no McGucken-Sphere expansion is generated by the i\ensuremath{^{2}} = −1 squaring (failure of N2 — without an active rate, the squaring has no kinematic content); no Huygens-iteration self-generates secondary McGucken-Spheres at events on wavefronts (failure of N3 — without active expansion, no wavefronts propagate, no points on wavefronts become secondary sources). On C \ensuremath{\in} \ensuremath{\mathcal{Q}}_static, the imaginary unit i is stripped of its physical-geometric content and reduced to a formal algebraic device with i\ensuremath{^{2}} = −1 as the sole content — without any physical-empirical realisation as the perpendicularity-marker, the McGucken-Sphere-generator, or the Huygens-iteration mechanism.*

**Proof of Theorem 29.7.10.22.** The proof consists of three sub-claims: (i) the i with physical content requires the conditions the first Nelson obstacle — that the Brownian motion in Nelson's framework is on configuration space $\mathbb{R}^3$ with time as an external parameter, not on spacetime, the second Nelson obstacle — that Nelson's drift velocity is supplied as an empirical parameter and is not derived from a physical principle, the third Nelson obstacle — that Nelson did not connect his stochastic mechanics to the Second Law of thermodynamics; (ii) on a static-foursome configuration, none of the first Nelson obstacle — that the Brownian motion in Nelson's framework is on configuration space $\mathbb{R}^3$ with time as an external parameter, not on spacetime, the second Nelson obstacle — that Nelson's drift velocity is supplied as an empirical parameter and is not derived from a physical principle, the third Nelson obstacle — that Nelson did not connect his stochastic mechanics to the Second Law of thermodynamics holds; (iii) therefore the i with physical content cannot exist on a static-foursome configuration.

*Sub-claim (i) — the i with physical content requires the first Nelson obstacle — that the Brownian motion in Nelson's framework is on configuration space $\mathbb{R}^3$ with time as an external parameter, not on spacetime, the second Nelson obstacle — that Nelson's drift velocity is supplied as an empirical parameter and is not derived from a physical principle, the third Nelson obstacle — that Nelson did not connect his stochastic mechanics to the Second Law of thermodynamics.* The physical content of the imaginary unit i in physics consists of three distinct functions:

*(F_i^A) Perpendicularity marker for x\ensuremath{_{4}}'s active expansion direction.* The i in dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic encodes that x\ensuremath{_{4}} is perpendicular to the spatial 3-slice at every event. This perpendicularity is meaningful only if x\ensuremath{_{4}} is an active dimension (a dimension that is actually advancing); a static x\ensuremath{_{4}} has no advance-direction to be perpendicular to anything. Therefore the perpendicularity-marker content of i requires the first Nelson obstacle — that the Brownian motion in Nelson's framework is on configuration space $\mathbb{R}^3$ with time as an external parameter, not on spacetime — active dimension.

*(F_i^B) Algebraic generator of the McGucken-Sphere expansion.* Per Lemma 29.7.10.12 of §29.7.10.28.3, the i\ensuremath{^{2}} = −1 squaring of the rate dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic produces the Lorentzian line element ds\ensuremath{^{2}} = (dx_spatial)\ensuremath{^{2}} − c\ensuremath{^{2}}(dt)\ensuremath{^{2}} with null surfaces ds\ensuremath{^{2}} = 0 supporting the McGucken-Sphere expansion at velocity c. The squaring has kinematic content (produces the c\ensuremath{^{2}} factor with the minus sign) only if the rate dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt is an actual kinematic rate (i.e., if x\ensuremath{_{4}} is actually advancing); a static x\ensuremath{_{4}} has no rate to be squared. Therefore the McGucken-Sphere-generating content of i requires the second Nelson obstacle — that Nelson's drift velocity is supplied as an empirical parameter and is not derived from a physical principle — rate = ic at velocity c.

*(F_i^C) Local-perpendicular-to-wavefront marker via Huygens-iteration.* Per Lemma 29.7.10.13 of §29.7.10.28.4, Huygens' principle operates as the self-iteration of the McGucken-Sphere expansion; the i at each event marks the local-x\ensuremath{_{4}}-direction as perpendicular to the local wavefront. The Huygens-iteration content requires that the McGucken-Sphere expansion actually propagates (so that wavefronts can carry secondary source-events); without active expansion, no wavefronts propagate, no secondary sources are generated, and the local-perpendicular-to-wavefront marking has no physical content. Therefore the Huygens-iteration content of i requires the third Nelson obstacle — that Nelson did not connect his stochastic mechanics to the Second Law of thermodynamics — McGucken Principle operates at every event.

The three functions (F_i^A), (F_i^B), (F_i^C) jointly constitute the physical-geometric content of i in physics. Each requires the corresponding condition the first Nelson obstacle — that the Brownian motion in Nelson's framework is on configuration space $\mathbb{R}^3$ with time as an external parameter, not on spacetime, the second Nelson obstacle — that Nelson's drift velocity is supplied as an empirical parameter and is not derived from a physical principle, the third Nelson obstacle — that Nelson did not connect his stochastic mechanics to the Second Law of thermodynamics. \ensuremath{\blacksquare} for sub-claim (i).

*Sub-claim (ii) — on a static-foursome configuration, none of the first Nelson obstacle — that the Brownian motion in Nelson's framework is on configuration space $\mathbb{R}^3$ with time as an external parameter, not on spacetime, the second Nelson obstacle — that Nelson's drift velocity is supplied as an empirical parameter and is not derived from a physical principle, the third Nelson obstacle — that Nelson did not connect his stochastic mechanics to the Second Law of thermodynamics holds.* By Theorem 29.7.10.11 of §29.7.10.17.2 of the present subsection (the Static-Foursome No-Go Theorem applied to the first limit of the McGucken dx$_4$/dt = ic framework with respect to the Clay Navier–Stokes problem — that the framework does not by itself supply a PDE-level proof of smooth existence or blowup–the empirical matter/antimatter distinction confirmed by the Anderson 1932 positron discovery and subsequent pair-creation/pair-annihilation record empirical components of spinor physics), no configuration C \ensuremath{\in} \ensuremath{\mathcal{Q}}_static can support empirical content requiring active rates. By the configuration-class decomposition \ensuremath{\mathcal{Q}} = \ensuremath{\mathcal{Q}}_static \ensuremath{\sqcup} \ensuremath{\mathcal{Q}}_active, a static-foursome configuration has dx_i/d\ensuremath{\tau} = 0 for all i \ensuremath{\in} {1, 2, 3, 4}, so:

*(N1 fails)* No coordinate x_j has dx_j/d\ensuremath{\tau} \ensuremath{\neq} 0 on C \ensuremath{\in} \ensuremath{\mathcal{Q}}_static; no active dimension exists.

*(N2 fails)* The rate dx_j/d\ensuremath{\tau} = 0 for all j; squaring gives (dx_j/d\ensuremath{\tau})\ensuremath{^{2}} = 0, not −c\ensuremath{^{2}}. The Lorentzian line element with negative time-time component is not generated by the static configuration; the McGucken-Sphere expansion is not generated.

*(N3 fails)* The McGucken Principle dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic, requiring a non-zero active rate at every event, cannot be operating at any event of C if the static-foursome condition holds. No Huygens-iteration is generated; no wavefronts propagate. \ensuremath{\blacksquare} for sub-claim (ii).

*Sub-claim (iii) — the i with physical content cannot exist on a static-foursome configuration.* By sub-claim (i), the physical content of i requires the first Nelson obstacle — that the Brownian motion in Nelson's framework is on configuration space $\mathbb{R}^3$ with time as an external parameter, not on spacetime, the second Nelson obstacle — that Nelson's drift velocity is supplied as an empirical parameter and is not derived from a physical principle, the third Nelson obstacle — that Nelson did not connect his stochastic mechanics to the Second Law of thermodynamics. By sub-claim (ii), on C \ensuremath{\in} \ensuremath{\mathcal{Q}}_static, none of the first Nelson obstacle — that the Brownian motion in Nelson's framework is on configuration space $\mathbb{R}^3$ with time as an external parameter, not on spacetime, the second Nelson obstacle — that Nelson's drift velocity is supplied as an empirical parameter and is not derived from a physical principle, the third Nelson obstacle — that Nelson did not connect his stochastic mechanics to the Second Law of thermodynamics holds. Therefore the physical content of i (the three functions F_i^A, F_i^B, F_i^C jointly) cannot exist on C \ensuremath{\in} \ensuremath{\mathcal{Q}}_static. The i on C is reduced to a formal algebraic symbol with the sole abstract property i\ensuremath{^{2}} = −1, without the perpendicularity-marker, the McGucken-Sphere-generator, or the Huygens-iteration content that constitutes its physical-geometric content. \ensuremath{\blacksquare} for sub-claim (iii).

*Joint conclusion.* Theorem 29.7.10.22 is established: the physical imaginary unit i requires the McGucken-Sphere-generating active expansion with Huygens-iteration; on a static-foursome configuration, i is stripped of physical content. \ensuremath{\blacksquare}

significance of Theorem 29.7.10.22. The theorem establishes that the imaginary unit i with physical-empirical content is a kinematic-foundational object — specifically, the algebraic-shadow generator of the McGucken-Sphere expansion via Huygens-iteration at every event of the McGucken Manifold. ##### §29.7.10.29.1. Hamilton's Quaternions Formally Defined — The 1843 Construction and the Pre-Relativistic Epistemic Situation

**Definition 29.7.10.9 (Hamilton's Quaternion Algebra \ensuremath{\mathbb{H}}).** *The quaternion algebra \ensuremath{\mathbb{H}} is the four-dimensional associative real algebra*

*\ensuremath{\mathbb{H}} = {a + bi + cj + dk: a, b, c, d \ensuremath{\in} \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}},*

*equipped with the non-commutative multiplication operation generated by the defining relations:*

*i\ensuremath{^{2}} = j\ensuremath{^{2}} = k\ensuremath{^{2}} = ijk = −1,*

*from which the standard non-commutative products follow:*

*ij = k, ji = −k, jk = i, kj = −i, ki = j, ik = −j.*

*Each quaternion q = a + bi + cj + dk decomposes uniquely into a scalar part Re(q) = a \ensuremath{\in} \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}} and a vector part Vec(q) = bi + cj + dk \ensuremath{\in} Im(\ensuremath{\mathbb{H}}) \ensuremath{\cong} \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}\ensuremath{^{3}}, with the orthogonal decomposition \ensuremath{\mathbb{H}} = \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}} \ensuremath{\oplus} Im(\ensuremath{\mathbb{H}}) at the additive-group level. The conjugate quaternion is q* = a − bi − cj − dk; the norm is |q|\ensuremath{^{2}} = qq* = a\ensuremath{^{2}} + b\ensuremath{^{2}} + c\ensuremath{^{2}} + d\ensuremath{^{2}}. The unit quaternions form the 3-sphere S\ensuremath{^{3}} = {q \ensuremath{\in} \ensuremath{\mathbb{H}}: |q| = 1}, which inherits the multiplication operation of \ensuremath{\mathbb{H}} to become a Lie group, isomorphic to SU(2) via the standard isomorphism q \ensuremath{\leftrightarrow} U_q \ensuremath{\in} SU(2). The pure-imaginary quaternions Im(\ensuremath{\mathbb{H}}) = {bi + cj + dk: b, c, d \ensuremath{\in} \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}} form the three-dimensional Lie algebra \ensuremath{\mathfrak{s}}\ensuremath{\mathfrak{u}}(2) under the commutator [p, q] = pq − qp (restricted to pure-imaginary quaternions, with the result divided by 2 for the standard \ensuremath{\mathfrak{s}}\ensuremath{\mathfrak{u}}(2) normalisation).*

The content of Definition 29.7.10.9 is supplied by the standard mathematical references [358, 359] (the canonical Hamilton 1844 *Philosophical Magazine* publication and the 1866 *Lectures on Quaternions* posthumous monograph). The historical-canonical content is the following.

The 1843 epistemic situation. Hamilton's construction of the quaternions occurred on October 16, 1843 — a historical date carved by Hamilton into Brougham Bridge in Dublin. The construction occurred in the following pre-relativistic, pre-quantum epistemic context: Maxwell's electromagnetic-field equations would not appear for 22 years (Maxwell 1865); Lorentz's coordinate transformations preserving Maxwell's equations would not appear for 49 years (Lorentz 1892, with the canonical 1904 derivation); Poincaré's introduction of the imaginary time-coordinate x\ensuremath{_{4}} = ict in *Sur la dynamique de l'électron* would not appear for 62 years (Poincaré 1905 [7]); Einstein's special relativity would not appear for 62 years (Einstein 1905); Minkowski's spacetime articulation in *Raum und Zeit* would not appear for 65 years (Minkowski 1908 [9]); Cartan's discovery of spinors would not appear for 70 years (Cartan 1913 [333]); the Dirac equation would not appear for 85 years (Dirac 1928 [3]); the McGucken framework's foundational articulation would not appear for 183 years (McGucken 2026).

Hamilton's stated goal. Hamilton's stated goal in constructing the quaternions, articulated explicitly in his October 17, 1843 letter to John T. Graves [358, p. 489] and reproduced verbatim in the canonical secondary literature (Hankins 1980 *Sir William Rowan Hamilton* [360]), was: *"to extend the imaginary-unit-i of complex numbers, which had been geometrically interpreted by Argand and Gauss as the rotation-generator of the plane, to handle rotations in three-dimensional space"*. Hamilton spent fifteen years (1828–1843) attempting to construct an associative algebra of "triplets" — three-component numbers (a + bi + cj) that would handle 3D rotations algebraically. The fifteen-year effort failed: no such 3D triplet algebra exists (as Hamilton himself eventually proved, this is a consequence of the Frobenius theorem on real division algebras [361], stating that the only finite-dimensional associative real division algebras are \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}, \ensuremath{\mathbb{C}}, \ensuremath{\mathbb{H}}; a 3-dimensional associative division algebra is impossible). The breakthrough on October 16, 1843 was Hamilton's recognition that he needed four components, not three, with three orthogonal imaginary units i, j, k.

The historical content of Hamilton's pre-relativistic epistemic situation is the following: Hamilton's discovery of the quaternions occurred in a mathematical-physics context in which the physical content identified by the McGucken framework — the actively-expanding fourth dimension at velocity c — was not available conceptually. The question "is the fourth quaternion component the moving time-dimension?" could not be formulated in 1843 because the relevant physics (special relativity, quantum mechanics, fermion phenomenology) did not exist. Hamilton's construction is therefore not a conscious denial or articulation of the moving fourth dimension; it is a pre-relativistic mathematical construction that happens to encode the algebraic-shadow content of a kinematic structure that the relevant physical contexts would only articulate sixty-two years later.

Per the rigor standard of the present paper, the precise scope of Theorem 29.7.10.24 and the historical content of §29.7.10.29 must be stated with full honesty.

*the articulation that $i$ is the algebraic shadow of the geometric perpendicularity of $x_4$ to the three spatial dimensions* Theorem 29.7.10.24 (Hamilton Quaternions Encode McGucken-Sphere Algebraic-Shadow Content): The five identifications (Q-1)–(Q-5) are established at full mathematical rigour via the proofs of §29.7.10.29.3 of the present subsection. *the articulation that the Wick rotation is the toggle between two disjoint positions of $i$* The historical lineage of 22 algebraic-shadow rediscoveries the twenty-two prior algebraic-shadow rediscoveries of dx$_4$/dt = ic content across the 1545–2010 window across 1545–2010 is established at the documentation level: each node is anchored to a canonical primary-source reference, and the McGucken-framework reading of each node as algebraic-shadow content of dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic is supplied at the appropriate cross-reference within the present subsection and the broader §29.7.10 chain of the present paper.

##### §29.7.10.30.1. The Four-Link Historical Chain — Documentation of the Minkowski \ensuremath{\rightarrow} Einstein \ensuremath{\rightarrow} Cartan \ensuremath{\rightarrow} Chern Lineage

The historical chain transmitting the algebraic-shadow content of Minkowski 1908 spacetime through to Chern 1946 characteristic-class theory has four explicit links, each anchored to canonical primary-source documentation.

Link 30.1.1 — Minkowski 1908 spacetime foundation. Hermann Minkowski's address *Raum und Zeit* at the 80th Assembly of German Natural Scientists and Physicians at Cologne, September 21, 1908 [9] introduces the four-dimensional spacetime as the unified geometric structure of special relativity, with the (1 time + 3 spatial)-component metric signature \ensuremath{\eta} = diag(−c\ensuremath{^{2}}, +1, +1, +1) and the imaginary-time-coordinate convention x_4 = ict inherited from Poincaré 1905 [7]. The Minkowski 1908 spacetime is the geometric content from which the entire 1908–1946 differential-geometric program descends — supplying the four-dimensional Lorentzian-signature manifold structure on which Einstein 1915 builds general relativity and on which Cartan 1922–1937 builds the affine-connection / moving-frame apparatus.

Link 30.1.2 — Einstein 1915 general relativity built on Minkowski spacetime. Albert Einstein's 1915 publications [Einstein 1915a, 1915b, *Die Feldgleichungen der Gravitation*, Sitzungsberichte der Preussischen Akademie der Wissenschaften] establish general relativity as the curvature-of-spacetime theory of gravitation, with the Einstein field equations R_{\ensuremath{\mu}\ensuremath{\nu}} − (1/2) g_{\ensuremath{\mu}\ensuremath{\nu}} R = (8\ensuremath{\pi}G/c\ensuremath{^{4}}) T_{\ensuremath{\mu}\ensuremath{\nu}} formulated on the curved-spacetime manifold inheriting Minkowski's signature structure. The mathematical machinery Einstein uses — the Levi-Civita connection, the Riemann curvature tensor, the Ricci tensor, the metric tensor as dynamical field — is the differential-geometric foundation that Cartan 1922 generalises in the affine-connection direction.

Link 30.1.3 — Cartan 1922–1937 differential-geometric apparatus developed in dialogue with general relativity. Élie Cartan's research program from 1922 onward was substantially focused on the mathematical structure of general relativity and the geometric content of Einstein's field equations. The canonical Cartan publications include:

*(a) Cartan 1922 [364]* — *"Sur une généralisation de la notion de courbure de Riemann et les espaces à torsion,"* Comptes Rendus de l'Académie des Sciences 174, 593–595. Cartan introduces the affine connection generalising Levi-Civita's parallel transport, motivated explicitly by the extension of general relativity to incorporate torsion. The affine connection \ensuremath{\omega}_\ensuremath{\mu} \ensuremath{\in} \ensuremath{\Omega}^1(M, ad(TM)) with curvature 2-form \ensuremath{\Omega} = d\ensuremath{\omega} + \ensuremath{\omega} \ensuremath{\wedge} \ensuremath{\omega} supplies the foundational machinery that Chern 1946 will use in the (i/2\ensuremath{\pi})F normalisation of characteristic classes.

*(b) Cartan 1923–1925 three-paper sequence* — *"Sur les variétés à connexion affine et la théorie de la relativité généralisée,"* Annales scientifiques de l'École Normale Supérieure 40 (1923) 325–412; 41 (1924) 1–25; 42 (1925) 17–88. The mathematical framework for relativistic differential geometry, supplying the moving-frame method and the principal-bundle perspective on connections that Chern 1946 inherits.

*(c) Cartan 1928* — *Leçons sur la géométrie des espaces de Riemann*, Gauthier-Villars, Paris. The canonical textbook on Riemannian geometry with explicit relativistic applications, supplying the systematic presentation of the curvature-form apparatus.

*(d) Cartan 1937* — *La théorie des groupes finis et continus et la géométrie différentielle traitée par la méthode du repère mobile*, Gauthier-Villars, Paris. The moving-frame method that Chern would later use as the foundational technical tool of his characteristic-class constructions.

Link 30.1.4 — Cartan-Einstein 1929–1932 correspondence on unified field theory. The direct Cartan-Einstein intellectual exchange is documented in the canonical edited collection *Élie Cartan and Albert Einstein: Letters on Absolute Parallelism 1929–1932* (edited by Robert Debever, Princeton University Press, 1979) [365]. The correspondence contains over fifty letters in which Cartan develops the differential-geometric framework that Einstein uses for his teleparallel-gravity unified-field-theory attempt. The correspondence supplies the historical documentation that Cartan's affine-connection apparatus was not just adjacent to relativistic geometry but was the geometric language Einstein and Cartan jointly developed for the foundational extension of general relativity.

Link 30.1.5 — Chern's 1936–1937 Paris year under Cartan. Shiing-Shen Chern (1911–2004) arrived in Paris in 1936 on a fellowship to study under Élie Cartan after his initial year at Hamburg under Wilhelm Blaschke. He worked directly under Cartan at the Sorbonne for the academic year 1936–1937. In Chern's own retrospective writings, supplied in the canonical autobiographical collection *Chern: A Great Geometer of the Twentieth Century* (edited by Shing-Tung Yau and others, International Press, 1992) [367], Chern identifies his Paris year under Cartan as the formative experience of his mathematical career, with the curvature-form apparatus and moving-frame method as the central technical content he inherited from Cartan.

Shiing-Shen Chern's 1946 publication *"Characteristic classes of Hermitian manifolds,"* Annals of Mathematics 47(1), 85–121 [366] introduces the Chern classes c_k(E) \ensuremath{\in} H^{2k}(M, \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}) for complex vector bundles E \ensuremath{\rightarrow} M over Hermitian manifolds M. uses the curvature 2-form F of a Hermitian connection on E. The (i/2\ensuremath{\pi})F normalisation factor combines the imaginary unit i (from the complex-vector-bundle structure inherited from Cartan's moving-frame apparatus on Hermitian manifolds) and the 2\ensuremath{\pi} factor (from the Euclidean-circle angular period that emerges in the characteristic-class integration). #### §29.7.12.1. The Observed Matter-Antimatter Asymmetry and the Sakharov 1967 Framework

The observed baryon-to-photon ratio in the contemporary universe is:

\ensuremath{\eta} = n_B / n_\ensuremath{\gamma} \ensuremath{\approx} 6.1 \ensuremath{\times} 10\ensuremath{^{-}}\ensuremath{^{1}}\ensuremath{^{0}}

per the Planck Collaboration 2018 [376] CMB anisotropy measurements, with independent confirmations from Big Bang nucleosynthesis abundance constraints on D, \ensuremath{^{3}}He, \ensuremath{^{4}}He, \ensuremath{^{7}}Li, and the Lyman-\ensuremath{\alpha} forest. The five independent observational channels jointly establish \ensuremath{\eta} \ensuremath{\approx} 6.1 \ensuremath{\times} 10\ensuremath{^{-}}\ensuremath{^{1}}\ensuremath{^{0}} to within 1% precision. The observational fact: for every approximately 1.6 \ensuremath{\times} 10\ensuremath{^{9}} photons in the cosmic microwave background, there is approximately one baryon (proton or neutron) in the universe, with effectively zero antibaryons in the observable universe (cosmic-ray antimatter is produced in secondary processes; no significant primordial antimatter component is observed).

The historical reconstruction of the matter-antimatter asymmetry: at temperatures T \ensuremath{\gg} m_p c\ensuremath{^{2}} \ensuremath{\approx} 1 GeV (the proton rest-mass energy) in the early universe, baryon-antibaryon pair production from the thermal photon bath was in equilibrium with annihilation. The number densities of baryons and antibaryons were both comparable to the photon number density: n_B \ensuremath{\approx} n_B̄ \ensuremath{\approx} n_\ensuremath{\gamma}. As the universe cooled below T ~ 1 GeV, the pair-production rate dropped (insufficient thermal photon energy to create new pairs), and pair annihilation continued. In a perfectly symmetric universe, this would have driven both n_B and n_B̄ to zero, leaving only photons. The observed n_B / n_\ensuremath{\gamma} \ensuremath{\approx} 6.1 \ensuremath{\times} 10\ensuremath{^{-}}\ensuremath{^{1}}\ensuremath{^{0}} requires that a small excess of baryons over antibaryons existed at the time of freeze-out: roughly one excess baryon per 10\ensuremath{^{9}} baryon-antibaryon pairs, so that after annihilation, one baryon per ~ 2 \ensuremath{\times} 10\ensuremath{^{9}} photons survived.

The foundational question: what mechanism produced the initial baryon excess? This is the baryogenesis problem.

**Definition 29.7.12.1 (Baryon Asymmetry Parameter).** *The baryon asymmetry parameter at the time of baryogenesis is defined as:*

\ensuremath{\varepsilon} \ensuremath{\equiv} (n_B − n_B̄) / (n_B + n_B̄)

*evaluated at the time and temperature at which the net baryon number was frozen in. The observed contemporary universe requires \ensuremath{\varepsilon} \ensuremath{\approx} 10\ensuremath{^{-}}\ensuremath{^{9}} at the freeze-out time, producing the contemporary baryon-to-photon ratio \ensuremath{\eta} \ensuremath{\approx} 6.1 \ensuremath{\times} 10\ensuremath{^{-}}\ensuremath{^{1}}\ensuremath{^{0}} via the relation \ensuremath{\eta} \ensuremath{\approx} \ensuremath{\varepsilon} \ensuremath{\times} (g_*S /g_*0)^(-1) (with g_*S the entropy degrees of freedom at the freeze-out epoch and g_*0 the entropy degrees of freedom in the contemporary universe).*

Andrei Sakharov in his 1967 paper [373] articulated three necessary conditions for any physical mechanism to generate a matter-antimatter asymmetry from initially symmetric conditions. The three Sakharov conditions are universally required for baryogenesis in any cosmological model:

Sakharov Condition 1 (Baryon Number Violation): Some physical process must allow the conversion of baryons to non-baryons (or change the total baryon number). Without baryon-number-violating processes, an initial state with zero net baryon number remains at zero net baryon number forever, regardless of the dynamics.

Sakharov Condition 2 (C and CP Violation): Both charge conjugation symmetry C and the combined CP symmetry must be violated. If C is exact, then for every baryon-producing process there is an exactly equal antibaryon-producing process, and any C-violating asymmetry produced is undone by the corresponding CP-conjugate process if CP is exact. Both C and CP must be violated to allow a net asymmetry.

Sakharov Condition 3 (Out-of-Equilibrium): The baryon-number-violating processes must occur out of thermal equilibrium. In thermal equilibrium, the forward rate of any process equals the reverse rate by detailed balance (CPT theorem combined with thermal averaging), and any nascent asymmetry is washed out by the inverse process at the equilibrium rate.

The three Sakharov conditions are universally necessary; the orthodox baryogenesis literature has proposed several mechanisms supplying them (GUT baryogenesis [Yoshimura 1978, Weinberg 1979]; electroweak baryogenesis [Kuzmin-Rubakov-Shaposhnikov 1985 [374], Cohen-Kaplan-Nelson 1993 [377]]; leptogenesis [Fukugita-Yanagida 1986 [375]]; Affleck-Dine baryogenesis [1985]), none of which has been empirically confirmed. The matter-antimatter asymmetry remains one of the major unsolved problems of physics under the orthodox Standard Model.

Under the McGucken-framework reading developed in §29.7.11 of the present paper, the three Sakharov conditions are not phenomenological inputs added from outside the framework; they are Grade-1 theorems of dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic descending from substrate-level content of the +ic-expanding McGucken manifold. The content of §29.7.12 establishes the three Sakharov conditions as theorems and identifies the strength of the resulting baryon asymmetry \ensuremath{\varepsilon} \ensuremath{\approx} 10\ensuremath{^{-}}\ensuremath{^{9}} as the cosmological-scale algebraic-shadow articulation of the substrate-level strength of the +ic-orientation asymmetry.

#### §29.7.13.1. The Marolf 2009 Constraint on Emergent-Gravity Foundational Substrates

### §30.8.1. The Erlangen Double-Completion


Felix Klein's 1872 Erlangen Programme [175] classified geometries by their invariance groups under continuous transformations. The Programme replaced the prior Euclidean-vs-non-Euclidean dichotomy with a unified group-theoretic taxonomy: a geometry is the invariant theory of a group G acting on a space X, with the Klein pair (G, X) as the primitive. The Programme has been the canonical foundation of geometric classification for 154 years, but it has had two open gaps from the beginning: (i) it does not select which Klein pair corresponds to physical spacetime — Klein 1872 classifies geometries but does not pick out the geometry of the world; (ii) it postulates the group-space pair (G, X) as primitive, without supplying a deeper source from which both descend.
