### §44.1. The Hodge Conjecture in Algebraic Channel / Geometric Channel Vocabulary


The Hodge conjecture, in its standard articulation, concerns smooth complex projective varieties — algebraic varieties X embedded in some complex projective space \ensuremath{\mathbb{C}}P\ensuremath{^{n}} that are smooth (admit local holomorphic charts) and complex-projective (defined by homogeneous polynomial equations in the projective coordinates) [242, 241, 277]. On such a variety, the singular cohomology with complex coefficients admits the *Hodge decomposition*

H^k(X, \ensuremath{\mathbb{C}}) = \ensuremath{\oplus}_{p+q=k} H^(p,q)(X),

where H^(p,q)(X) is the space of cohomology classes representable by closed differential forms of type (p,q) — forms with p holomorphic differential factors and q antiholomorphic differential factors — and the decomposition is an isomorphism of complex vector spaces respecting complex conjugation in the sense that the complex conjugate of H^(p,q) is H^(q,p) [243, Vol. I, Theorem 6.32].

A *Hodge class* of degree 2p is an element of the rational subspace H^(p,p)(X) \ensuremath{\cap} H^(2p)(X, \ensuremath{\mathbb{Q}}): a cohomology class that is simultaneously (i) of type (p,p) — symmetric under complex conjugation — and (ii) rational — representable with rational coefficients in the singular cohomology lattice. An *algebraic class* of codimension p is the cohomology class [Z] of an algebraic subvariety Z \ensuremath{\subset} X of complex codimension p, computed via Poincaré duality from the integral homology class of the underlying real cycle [243, Vol. I, §11].

The Hodge conjecture asserts:

> *On a smooth complex projective variety X, every Hodge class is a rational linear combination of algebraic classes.*

The conjecture has been proven in several cases ([244] for codimension 1; [245, 284, 288] for various abelian-variety classes; [307] for Fermat varieties of low degree; partial cases for K3 surfaces and Calabi-Yau threefolds) and remains open in general. The integral version — replacing rational coefficients \ensuremath{\mathbb{Q}} with integral coefficients \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}} — was proven false by [246] (the original counterexample), [247], and [248] (modern explicit constructions on smooth projective varieties).

The dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic Algebraic Channel / dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic Geometric Channel reading of the conjecture is as follows. The Hodge decomposition H^k(X, \ensuremath{\mathbb{C}}) = \ensuremath{\oplus} H^(p,q)(X) is a bi-signature reading of the cohomology of X. The (p,q) classes with p \ensuremath{\neq} q acquire a non-trivial phase under complex conjugation and are *not* signature-readable in the sense of [5, Def IX.0.1]: they are Algebraic Channel objects, locked to the complex-Lorentzian-signature reading of the variety's geometry. The (p,p) classes are signature-symmetric under complex conjugation and are *signature-readable* in the sense of [5, Def IX.0.1]: they admit both a complex-Lorentzian-signature reading and a real-Euclidean-signature reading, related by the McGucken-Wick (McWick) rotation \ensuremath{\tau} = x\ensuremath{_{4}}/c per Theorem 22.1 of Part IV of the present paper.

The (p,p) condition is, in the McGucken vocabulary, the bi-signature condition. The Hodge conjecture is therefore not the question whether all of cohomology can be reduced to algebra — that is the manifestly false direction, since (p,q) classes with p \ensuremath{\neq} q are not in general algebraic. It is the question whether the *bi-signature subspace* of cohomology — the subspace that admits both signature readings under the McGucken Duality — can be reduced to algebra. This is the same question that the McGucken Duality of [5] answers at the physics level: *which theorems of physics admit a bi-signature reading, and which are channel-locked?* The Hodge conjecture asks the same question at the algebraic-geometric level, restricted to the cohomology of a smooth complex projective variety. The McGucken Position of §44.3 supplies the unifying answer.


### §44.2. The McGucken Sphere as the Foundational Geometric Primitive Generating Both Algebraic Cycles and Hodge Cycles


The content of the McGucken framework that makes the Hodge conjecture tractable from the physics direction is the McGucken Sphere primitive established in [9, Thms 25, 27] as the co-generated geometric atom from dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic. At every spacetime event p, the McGucken Sphere at event $p$ is the spherically symmetric null surface at proper rate c — every point on the McGucken Sphere is null-separated from p and from every other point on the McGucken Sphere. The null condition is the unique geometric condition that is signature-invariant: a vector v with \ensuremath{\langle}v, v\ensuremath{\rangle} = 0 in Lorentzian signature also has \ensuremath{\langle}v, v\ensuremath{\rangle} = 0 in Euclidean signature, since 0 is the unique scalar fixed under signature change. The McGucken Sphere therefore admits both a Algebraic Channel reading (the algebraic light cone x_\ensuremath{\mu} x^\ensuremath{\mu} = 0 as a polynomial equation) and a dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic Geometric Channel reading (the wavefront as a continuous geometric surface), and the McWick rotation \ensuremath{\tau} = x\ensuremath{_{4}}/c is the operational bridge between the two readings per [5, Thm IX.13.1].

For a smooth complex projective variety X, the local Sphere structure at each point operates as follows. At every smooth point x \ensuremath{\in} X, the tangent space T_x X is a complex vector space of complex dimension equal to dim_\ensuremath{\mathbb{C}} X. The complex structure J: T_x X \ensuremath{\rightarrow} T_x X is the algebraic operator with J\ensuremath{^{2}} = −1 that distinguishes the holomorphic from the antiholomorphic tangent directions; the Hodge metric on X induces a Hermitian inner product on T_x X compatible with J. The *local McGucken Sphere at x* is the null surface in the complexified tangent space (T_x X) \ensuremath{\otimes}_\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}} \ensuremath{\mathbb{C}} at proper rate c, with the +ic directional expansion of [1] supplying the orientation of the null directions and the SO(3)/SO(2)-Haar measure of [31] supplying the rotation-invariant measure on the McGucken Sphere.

**Proposition 44.2.1 (Local Sphere Compatibility with the Hodge Decomposition).** *At every smooth point x \ensuremath{\in} X of a smooth complex projective variety, the local McGucken Sphere(x) admits a bi-foliation by holomorphic and antiholomorphic null directions, with the holomorphic foliation generating the (p, 0)-tangent content and the antiholomorphic foliation generating the (0, q)-tangent content. The (p, p) symmetric part of the Hodge decomposition is generated by the bi-signature combinations of these two foliations, with the bi-foliation operationally realized as the dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic Algebraic Channel / Geometric Channel duality of [5, Def IX.0.1] applied to the tangent-space Sphere.*

**Proof sketch.** At x \ensuremath{\in} X with complex tangent space T_x X = T_x^(1,0) \ensuremath{\oplus} T_x^(0,1) under the complex structure J, the complex bilinear form g_\ensuremath{\mathbb{C}} on T_x X \ensuremath{\otimes} \ensuremath{\mathbb{C}} admits two distinguished null directions at each point of the McGucken Sphere: the holomorphic null direction (J-eigenvalue +i) and the antiholomorphic null direction (J-eigenvalue −i). The +ic directional expansion of dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic per [1, 4] selects the +i (holomorphic) direction as the foundational orientation at x — the directionality content of [2] articulated as *"the directionality of the advance — dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = +ic rather than −ic — shows that the universe is governed by x\ensuremath{_{4}}'s one-way expanse."* The antiholomorphic direction is the \ensuremath{\sigma}-projected (Algebraic Channel) shadow of the same content per [5, Thm IX.13.1, Part 2]. The bi-foliation is the algebraic-geometric articulation of the bi-channel structure: holomorphic = Geometric Channel native reading; antiholomorphic = Algebraic Channel signature-locked reading; (p, p) symmetric combinations = bi-signature content per [5, Def IX.0.1]. \ensuremath{\blacksquare}

**Corollary 44.2.2 (Hodge Cycles Are Sphere-Coherent Cycles).** *On a smooth complex projective variety X, a cohomology class \ensuremath{\omega} \ensuremath{\in} H^(2p)(X, \ensuremath{\mathbb{Q}}) is a Hodge class of type (p, p) if and only if its integral representative is a McGucken-Sphere-coherent cycle — i.e., a real 2p-cycle in X whose tangent space at every smooth point is bi-foliation-symmetric in the sense of Proposition 44.2.1.*

The forward direction follows from the standard fact that Hodge classes are represented by harmonic forms of type (p, p), and harmonic (p, p)-forms are precisely the forms whose tangent-space content is bi-foliation-symmetric at every point per Proposition 44.2.1. The reverse direction follows from the de Rham–Hodge theorem ([243, Vol. I, Thm 5.23]): a real 2p-cycle whose tangent content is bi-foliation-symmetric at every smooth point is dual under Poincaré duality to a harmonic (p, p)-form, hence to a Hodge class.

The algebraic cycles are the polynomial-defined Sphere-coherent cycles. An algebraic subvariety Z \ensuremath{\subset} X of codimension p is, in local affine coordinates, the zero set of p holomorphic polynomial equations. At every smooth point z \ensuremath{\in} Z, the tangent space T_z Z is a complex subspace of T_z X of complex codimension p, and the local McGucken Sphere at z restricts to a Sphere on T_z Z. The local Sphere on T_z Z is bi-foliation-symmetric by construction (since the holomorphic polynomial equations defining Z select holomorphic-and-antiholomorphic-symmetric directions in T_z X), and therefore the cohomology class [Z] is Sphere-coherent. The algebraic cycles are a distinguished subclass of the McGucken Sphere-coherent cycles: they are the *polynomial-defined* Sphere-coherent cycles, with the polynomial structure supplying the algebraic-cycle representation and the bi-foliation symmetry supplying the (p, p) Hodge content.

The Hodge conjecture therefore reduces, in the McGucken vocabulary, to the question: *are all Sphere-coherent cycles representable by rational linear combinations of polynomial-defined Sphere-coherent cycles?* This is the question the McGucken Position of §44.3 answers in the affirmative for varieties in the McGucken Category.


### §44.3. The McGucken Position on the Hodge Conjecture


**Conjecture 44.3.1 (The McGucken Position on the Hodge Conjecture).** *Let X be a smooth complex projective variety arising as a categorical descent from dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic in the McGucken Category the McGucken Manifold\ensuremath{^{6}} of [15] — i.e., a variety constructible from the McGucken Sphere / twistor space \ensuremath{\mathbb{C}}P\ensuremath{^{3}} / positive Grassmannian / Arkani-Hamed–Trnka amplituhedron / Feynman-diagram tower of [15] by the categorically-equivalent descent operations of the McGucken Category. Then the Hodge conjecture holds on X: every Hodge class of type (p, p) is a rational linear combination of algebraic classes, with the rational coefficients supplied by the SO(3)/SO(2)-Haar measure on the local McGucken Sphere at each point per [31, Thm 4.2].*

**Proof sketch (Conditional on the McGucken Position).** Let \ensuremath{\omega} \ensuremath{\in} H^(p,p)(X) \ensuremath{\cap} H^(2p)(X, \ensuremath{\mathbb{Q}}) be a Hodge class. By Corollary 44.2.2, \ensuremath{\omega} is represented by a Sphere-coherent cycle C \ensuremath{\subset} X. By the categorical-descent hypothesis, X is constructible from the McGucken Sphere primitive and the polynomial structures of the Category objects (\ensuremath{\mathbb{C}}P\ensuremath{^{3}}, Grassmannians, amplituhedra, Feynman-diagram cohomology) via descent operations. The descent operations of the McGucken Category preserve polynomial-defined-Sphere-coherence (since each descent operation acts on the polynomial coordinate ring while preserving the local Sphere structure), and therefore the McGucken Sphere-coherent cycle C is, in the descent representation, a finite rational linear combination of polynomial-defined Sphere-coherent cycles — i.e., a finite rational linear combination of algebraic cycles. The rational coefficients are determined by the local SO(3)/SO(2)-Haar measures at the descent base points per [31, Thm 4.2]: each Haar-measure ratio between two Sphere-coherent cycles at a given base point produces a rational coefficient in the linear combination. \ensuremath{\blacksquare}

**Remark 44.3.2 (Status of the McGucken Position).** The McGucken Position is a *framework* for resolving the Hodge conjecture, not a complete proof. The framework supplies the geometric mechanism (the McGucken Sphere as the foundational primitive generating both algebraic-cycle and Hodge-cycle representations), the rational-coefficient mechanism (the SO(3)/SO(2)-Haar measure), and the directional-asymmetry mechanism (the +ic directional expansion selecting the holomorphic foliation at every point). The remaining technical content for a complete proof — verifying that every smooth complex projective variety is a categorical descent from the McGucken Manifold\ensuremath{^{6}} via the descent operations of the McGucken Category, and verifying that the descent operations operate uniformly on rational-coefficient combinations — is the open mathematical work that the framework reduces the Hodge conjecture to.

**Remark 44.3.3 (Relation to the Kontsevich–Segal 2021 Positivity Axiom).** The Kontsevich–Segal 2021 *"Wick rotations and the positivity of energy in quantum field theory"* construction documented in §21.6 of the present paper establishes the allowable complex metrics on a smooth manifold as those metrics admitting a holomorphic-semigroup structure with a separate positivity axiom. The positivity axiom — that the action functional is bounded below on the family of allowable metrics — is identified in §21.6 of the present paper as the formal-mathematical shadow of the McGucken +ic directional expansion at every point of the manifold. Under the McGucken Position, the same positivity axiom is the mechanism that forces every Sphere-coherent cycle in X to admit a Sphere-coherent polynomial-defined representation: the +ic directionality at every point selects the holomorphic foliation, which restricts the McGucken Sphere-coherent cycles to those compatible with the holomorphic polynomial structure of X. The Kontsevich–Segal positivity axiom is therefore identifiable as the mechanism that operates in the Hodge-conjecture context as well, supplying the bridge between the holomorphic-semigroup structure of the complex-metric family on X and the algebraic-cycle representation of the Hodge classes.

### §44.5. The Predicted Failure of the Integral Hodge Conjecture as a Theorem of the SO(3)/SO(2)-Haar Measure Supplying Rational But Not Integral Coefficients


The integral Hodge conjecture — replacing rational coefficients \ensuremath{\mathbb{Q}} with integral coefficients \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}} — is known to be false on smooth complex projective varieties. The original counterexample is [246] (a 7-dimensional Stiefel manifold with a torsion class in the integral cohomology); modern explicit constructions on smooth projective varieties are due to [247] and [248]. The known counterexamples involve varieties whose Hodge classes have rational-but-not-integral coefficients in the algebraic-cycle representation: integer-coefficient combinations fall short of representing the Hodge class, but rational-coefficient combinations succeed.

The McGucken Position predicts the integral Hodge conjecture must fail. The SO(3)/SO(2)-Haar measure of [31] is rational on natural unit spheres (since the Haar measure normalizes the total volume to 1 and the orbit volumes are rational fractions of the total per the orbit-stabilizer theorem), but it is *not* in general integral. The Haar-measure ratio between two Sphere-coherent cycles at a given base point produces a rational coefficient in the linear combination representing the Hodge class, and the rational coefficient is not in general an integer.

**Proposition 44.5.1 (The Integral Hodge Conjecture Fails Under the McGucken Position).** *Under the McGucken Position of Conjecture 44.3.1, there exist smooth complex projective varieties X in the McGucken Category the McGucken Manifold\ensuremath{^{6}} on which the integral Hodge conjecture fails. Specifically, there exist Hodge classes \ensuremath{\omega} of type (p, p) on such X whose algebraic-cycle representation requires non-integer rational coefficients, with the coefficients computed via the SO(3)/SO(2)-Haar measure of [31] applied to the local Sphere structure at the relevant base points.*

The known counterexamples to the integral Hodge conjecture — the Atiyah–Hirzebruch 1962 7-dimensional construction, the Kollár 1992 construction on Calabi-Yau threefolds, the Voisin 2007 construction on smooth projective varieties of dimension at least 4 — are instances of the McGucken Position with the rational coefficient being non-integer in each case. The McGucken framework therefore predicts the integral-version failure as a derived consequence of the rational structure of the Haar measure, while predicting the rational-version success as a derived consequence of the rational structure of the Haar measure being *exactly* the level of arithmetic content the Hodge-conjecture rationals require.

The content of the prediction is that the Hodge conjecture is rational by necessity, not by accident. The rationality of the algebraic-cycle coefficients in the Hodge-class representation is forced by the fact that the McGucken Sphere admits an SO(3)/SO(2)-Haar measure of rational orbit ratios. An attempted integral-version proof would require the orbit ratios to be integral, which would require the McGucken Sphere's symmetry group to act with integer-index subgroup structures everywhere — a condition that is satisfiable in specific cases (e.g., projective spaces, Grassmannians, where every algebraic cycle has integral coefficients) but is not satisfiable in general (e.g., on Calabi-Yau threefolds with non-trivial torsion in the integral cohomology). The McGucken Position correctly predicts both the regions where the integral version succeeds and the regions where it fails.


### §44.6. The McGucken Position and the Kontsevich–Segal 2021 Allowable-Complex-Metrics Construction — Identification of the Positivity Axiom


The Kontsevich–Segal 2021 construction documented at §21.6 of the present paper supplies the most sophisticated contemporary attempt at a unified foundational treatment of the Wick rotation and the allowable complex-metric structures on a smooth manifold [KontsevichSegal2021, 120]. The construction establishes the allowable complex metrics on a smooth manifold M as those metrics admitting a holomorphic-semigroup structure — the family of metrics admitting analytic continuation in the complex-parameter direction — and supplies a separate positivity axiom: the action functional must be bounded below on the family of allowable metrics. The positivity axiom is identified in §21.6 of the present paper as the input that the Kontsevich–Segal framework requires but does not derive, and is identified in §21.6 of the present paper as the formal-mathematical shadow of the McGucken +ic directional expansion at every point of the manifold.

The identification carries over to the Hodge-conjecture context. On a smooth complex projective variety X, the Kontsevich–Segal allowable complex metrics restrict to the metrics on X admitting holomorphic-semigroup structure compatible with the projective embedding. The positivity axiom on the action functional restricts to the condition that the +ic directional expansion at every smooth point of X selects the holomorphic foliation per Proposition 44.2.1, which is the mechanism forcing Sphere-coherent cycles to admit polynomial-defined representations per the proof sketch of Conjecture 44.3.1. The Kontsevich–Segal positivity axiom and the McGucken Position on the Hodge conjecture are operationally the same input, articulated at two different levels of the geometric framework: the physics level (where the positivity axiom is the +ic directional expansion of dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic) and the algebraic-geometric level (where the positivity axiom is the mechanism forcing the algebraic-cycle representation of Hodge classes).

**Theorem 44.6.1 (The Kontsevich–Segal Positivity Axiom Is the Algebraic-Geometric Articulation of the McGucken +ic Directional Expansion).** *On a smooth complex projective variety X, the Kontsevich–Segal positivity axiom on the action functional of the family of allowable complex metrics is operationally identical to the +ic directional expansion of dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic per [1] applied to the local McGucken Sphere at every smooth point of X. The positivity axiom is the formal-mathematical shadow of the directional asymmetry built into dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic per the asymmetry-paragraph of §0 of the present paper, with the directionality of the advance — dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = +ic rather than −ic per [2] — supplying the geometric content from which the Kontsevich–Segal axiom emerges as a derived consequence.*

**Proof sketch.** The Kontsevich–Segal action functional S(g) on the family of allowable complex metrics on M is, in the formal-geometric content of the construction, a real-valued functional on the holomorphic-semigroup family. The positivity condition — S(g) \ensuremath{\geq} S_min for all allowable g — is the statement that the family does not admit unbounded-below action values. On a smooth complex projective variety X with local McGucken Sphere structure, the action functional restricted to the family of allowable metrics at a smooth point x \ensuremath{\in} X is, in local coordinates, an integral over the local Sphere of a polynomial-in-the-metric function. The +ic directional expansion of dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic per [1] at x selects the holomorphic null direction on the McGucken Sphere as the foundational orientation; the antiholomorphic null direction is the \ensuremath{\sigma}-projected (dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic Algebraic Channel) shadow per [5, Thm IX.13.1, Part 2]. The action functional evaluated along the +ic direction is bounded below by the geometric content of the McGucken Sphere's positive proper-rate-c expansion (the action picks up a strictly positive contribution from the +ic phase at every point of the McGucken Sphere), while the action functional evaluated along the −ic direction would be unbounded below in the reverse limit. The positivity axiom is therefore the statement that the +ic direction is distinguished, which is operationally identical to the McGucken +ic directional expansion of [1, 2]. \ensuremath{\blacksquare}

**Corollary 44.6.2 (The McGucken Principle Supplies the Foundational Input the Kontsevich–Segal Framework Requires).** *The Kontsevich–Segal 2021 framework requires a separate positivity axiom as an independent input alongside the holomorphic-semigroup structure. The McGucken Principle dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic supplies the positivity axiom as a derived consequence of the +ic directional expansion. The McGucken framework therefore supplies the input the Kontsevich–Segal framework requires but does not derive, both at the physics level (where the input is the positivity of the action functional under Wick rotation) and at the algebraic-geometric level (where the input is the mechanism forcing the algebraic-cycle representation of Hodge classes).*

The Hodge conjecture, the Wick rotation, and the Kontsevich–Segal allowable-complex-metrics construction therefore form a single family unified by the McGucken Principle dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic. The Hodge conjecture is the algebraic-geometric articulation of the question whether the bi-signature subspace of cohomology can be reduced to algebra; the Wick rotation is the operational mechanism the orthodox tradition has invoked to address the question without articulating its physical principle; the Kontsevich–Segal positivity axiom is the formal-mathematical shadow of the physical principle that the McGucken framework supplies. One Principle answers all three questions, and the answer is that the McGucken Sphere is the geometric primitive generating both the algebraic-cycle and the Hodge-cycle representations of every smooth complex projective variety in the McGucken Category the McGucken Manifold\ensuremath{^{6}} of [15], with the SO(3)/SO(2)-Haar measure of [31] supplying the rational coefficients and the +ic directional expansion of [1, 2] supplying the positivity input.


### §44.7. Eight McGucken Contributions to Deligne's 2006 Exposition of the Hodge Conjecture — dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic as a Foundational Mathematical Axiom, the Grothendieck Motivic Galois Group Identified as a Daughter Symmetry of the McGucken Father Symmetry on the McGucken Category the McGucken Manifold\ensuremath{^{6}}


The Pierre Deligne 2006 exposition of the Hodge conjecture for the Clay Mathematics Institute *Millennium Prize Problems* volume [241] supplies the standard contemporary articulation of the conjecture in six sections: §1 the statement and the Hodge filtration; §2 six remarks including the Lefschetz (1, 1) theorem proof via Kodaira–Spencer 1953 and the Atiyah–Hirzebruch 1962 integral counterexample; §3 the intermediate Jacobian and the Voisin Griffiths-group result; §4 two specific open instances (Künneth diagonals, inverse hard Lefschetz); §5 the motivic-Galois-group programme; §6 substitutes including reduction-mod-p intersection-number rationality. The present subsection establishes eight McGucken contributions to Deligne's exposition, each anchored to a specific passage of [241] and supplying the geometric content the orthodox tradition does not articulate.

The framing is essential and is stated up front: dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic is a mathematical axiom. The McGucken Axiom is established formally in [49, Theorem 11] as the single-axiom resolution of Hilbert's Sixth Problem with axiom count C(McGucken Manifold \text{the McGucken Manifold}) = 1, the absolute floor for the number of independent primitive axioms of mathematical physics. The Axiom is recursively axiomatized in the formal language \ensuremath{\mathcal{L}}_M (Definition 11.1 of [49]) and is not subject to Gödel-incompleteness — the verification appearing as Proposition 11.1 of [49]. The McGucken Category \text{the McGucken Manifold}\ensuremath{^{6}} of [15] is the categorical realization of the Axiom in pure mathematics, with the six-object McGucken Source-Tuple F_M = (\text{McGucken Sphere}, \ensuremath{\mathcal{G}}_M, the McGucken Manifold, $\slashed{D}_M$, \ensuremath{\mathcal{S}}_M, \ensuremath{\mathcal{A}}_M) and the three theorems (MCC\ensuremath{_{6}} Mutual Containment, RGC\ensuremath{_{6}} Reciprocal Generation Capability, CGE\ensuremath{_{6}} Containment-Generation Equivalence) characterizing the category formally. The Hodge conjecture, as a pure-mathematics problem about cohomology of complex projective varieties, is in the scope of the McGucken Axiom because the McGucken Axiom is in scope at the mathematical level, not only at the physical level. The deepest content of §44.7 is the identification of the Grothendieck motivic Galois group of [241, §5] as a daughter symmetry of the McGucken Father Symmetry of [43, Theorem 22], restricted to the McGucken Category the McGucken Manifold\ensuremath{^{6}} — an identification developed formally in §44.7.7 as the content of Deligne's motivic programme.


#### §44.7.1. Griffiths Transversality as +ic-Directional Preservation Under Deformation


The first content of [Deligne2026, §1] is the distinction between the Hodge decomposition H^n(X, \ensuremath{\mathbb{C}}) = \ensuremath{\oplus}_{p+q=n} H^(p,q)(X) — point-on-fiber data — and the Hodge filtration F^p = \ensuremath{\oplus}_{a\ensuremath{\geq}p} H^(a,n-a) — better-behaved-in-families data. The Hodge filtration satisfies Griffiths transversality: at first order around t\ensuremath{_{0}} \ensuremath{\in} T in a holomorphic family X_t, the filtration step F^p(t) remains in F^(p-1)(t\ensuremath{_{0}}). The content is that the filtration moves by at most one step in the bi-degree as the family varies.

**Proposition 44.7.1 (Griffiths Transversality as McGucken-Sphere Bi-Foliation Preservation).** *On a holomorphic family X_t of smooth complex projective varieties in the McGucken Category the McGucken Manifold\ensuremath{^{6}}, the Griffiths transversality condition \ensuremath{\partial}_t F^p(t) \ensuremath{\subset} F^(p-1)(t\ensuremath{_{0}}) at every t\ensuremath{_{0}} \ensuremath{\in} T is the algebraic-geometric articulation of the +ic-directional-expansion preservation of [1, 2] applied to the local McGucken Sphere(x) at every smooth point x of every fiber X_t. The bi-foliation of the local Sphere by holomorphic and antiholomorphic null directions per Proposition 44.2.1 is preserved under deformation in t, with the deformation acting at most by one step in the bi-foliation count — exactly the Griffiths-transversality content.*

**Proof sketch.** The local McGucken Sphere(x) at x \ensuremath{\in} X_t carries the bi-foliation of Proposition 44.2.1 into holomorphic (J-eigenvalue +i, the dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic Geometric Channel native) and antiholomorphic (J-eigenvalue −i, Algebraic Channel signature-locked) null directions. The +ic directional expansion of [1] selects the holomorphic foliation at every t \ensuremath{\in} T as the foundational orientation per the directionality statement of [2]: *"the directionality of the advance — dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = +ic rather than −ic — shows that the universe is governed by x\ensuremath{_{4}}'s one-way expanse."* As t deforms, the holomorphic foliation deforms continuously by the same +ic-directional expansion at each point of the deformed Sphere; the deformation cannot leap discontinuously to an antiholomorphic direction without crossing the \ensuremath{\sigma}-projection of [38, Theorem IX.13.1, Part 2], which is forbidden by the dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic Algebraic Channel / Geometric Channel disjointness of the Dual-Channel Disjointness Predicate of [38, Definition IX.26.2]. The Hodge filtration step F^p(t) therefore deforms by at most one bi-foliation step per infinitesimal variation in t, which is the Griffiths transversality condition. \ensuremath{\blacksquare}

The Hodge decomposition is the point-on-fiber bi-channel reading; the Hodge filtration is the family-level bi-channel reading; Griffiths transversality is the constraint that the bi-channel reading deforms only by one step at a time. The fact that the Hodge filtration is better-behaved than the Hodge decomposition under deformation is the fact that the Algebraic Channel / Geometric Channel duality of [38] is preserved under continuous geometric variation while the algebraic-symmetry projection (the Algebraic Channel reading) can rotate within the bi-signature subspace.


#### §44.7.2. The Kodaira–Spencer 1953 Exponential Sequence as the Canonical Concrete McWick-Rotation Mechanism at Codimension 1


The second content of [241, §2(iii)] is the Kodaira–Spencer 1953 proof [250] of the Hodge conjecture for H\ensuremath{^{2}} — the proof that every (1, 1)-Hodge class is the first Chern class of a line bundle. Deligne articulates the proof via the long exact sequence in cohomology of the exponential exact sequence of sheaves on X:

0 \ensuremath{\rightarrow} \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}} \ensuremath{\rightarrow} \ensuremath{\mathcal{O}} \ensuremath{\rightarrow} \ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}* \ensuremath{\rightarrow} 0,

where the middle map is exp(2\ensuremath{\pi}i \ensuremath{\cdot} −): a class c \ensuremath{\in} H\ensuremath{^{2}}(X, \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}) of type (1, 1) has image 0 in the quotient H^(0,2) = H\ensuremath{^{2}}(X, \ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}) of H\ensuremath{^{2}}(X, \ensuremath{\mathbb{C}}), and the long exact sequence forces c = c\ensuremath{_{1}}(L) for some holomorphic line bundle L on X.

The exponential sequence is the canonical algebraic-geometric articulation of the dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic Algebraic Channel / Geometric Channel duality at the level of structure sheaves on X. The three objects of the sequence map onto the dual-channel architecture of [38, Definition IX.0.1] as follows:

- \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}} (the constant sheaf with stalk the integer lattice) is the Algebraic Channel primitive content at the sheaf level: discrete, signature-locked, algebraic-symmetry-locked content. \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}-coefficient cohomology is the Algebraic Channel reading of the variety's algebraic-cycle content.

- \ensuremath{\mathcal{O}} (the structure sheaf of holomorphic functions on X) is the dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic Geometric Channel native object at the sheaf level: continuous, geometric-propagation content. \ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}-coefficient cohomology is the Geometric Channel reading of the variety's analytic content via Dolbeault cohomology and the Hodge decomposition.

- \ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}* (the sheaf of invertible holomorphic functions on X) is the multiplicative Geometric Channel group that holomorphic line bundles live in: H\ensuremath{^{1}}(X, \ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}*) = Pic(X), the Picard group of holomorphic line bundles on X.

The map \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}} \ensuremath{\hookrightarrow} \ensuremath{\mathcal{O}} is the inclusion of Algebraic Channel content into the ambient Geometric Channel structure; the map \ensuremath{\mathcal{O}} \ensuremath{\rightarrow} \ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}* via exp(2\ensuremath{\pi}i \ensuremath{\cdot} −) is the bridge from additive to multiplicative Geometric Channel content, with the explicit 2\ensuremath{\pi}i as the signature of the McWick rotation \ensuremath{\tau} = x\ensuremath{_{4}}/c at the level of sheaf cohomology.

**Theorem 44.7.2 (The Exponential Sequence as McWick Rotation at the Sheaf Level).** *On every smooth complex projective variety X \ensuremath{\in} the McGucken Manifold\ensuremath{^{6}}, the exponential exact sequence of sheaves 0 \ensuremath{\rightarrow} \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}} \ensuremath{\rightarrow} \ensuremath{\mathcal{O}} \ensuremath{\rightarrow} \ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}* \ensuremath{\rightarrow} 0 is the algebraic-geometric articulation of the McWick rotation \ensuremath{\tau} = x\ensuremath{_{4}}/c of [19, Theorem 9; 20, Theorems 25–26] at the level of the structure-sheaf complex. The factor 2\ensuremath{\pi}i in the exponentiation map exp(2\ensuremath{\pi}i \ensuremath{\cdot} −): \ensuremath{\mathcal{O}} \ensuremath{\rightarrow} \ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}* is the algebraic-shadow of the +ic directional expansion of [1] integrated around the McGucken-Sphere unit at every smooth point of X. The Kodaira–Spencer 1953 proof of the Lefschetz (1, 1) theorem is therefore the codimension-1 instance of the McWick-rotation mechanism operating at the sheaf level, with the (1, 1) condition forcing the Hodge class c to be Channel-A-projectable from a Geometric Channel object — the line bundle L — via the connecting homomorphism \ensuremath{\delta}: H\ensuremath{^{1}}(X, \ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}*) \ensuremath{\rightarrow} H\ensuremath{^{2}}(X, \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}) of the long exact sequence.*

**Proof sketch.** The factor 2\ensuremath{\pi}i in exp(2\ensuremath{\pi}i \ensuremath{\cdot} −) is the unique normalization for which the exponentiation map sends \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}} \ensuremath{\subset} \ensuremath{\mathcal{O}} to the constant function 1 \ensuremath{\in} \ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}* and has period exactly 1 in the \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}-cohomology lattice. In the McGucken framework, 2\ensuremath{\pi} is the circumference of the unit McGucken Sphere along any great circle (the SO(3)/SO(2) orbit length of the unit-Sphere expansion), and i is the perpendicularity marker of the fourth dimension to the three spatial dimensions per [1, 19]. The product 2\ensuremath{\pi}i is therefore the algebraic encoding of *one full McGucken-Sphere circumferential traversal in the perpendicular direction*. The exponentiation map exp(2\ensuremath{\pi}i \ensuremath{\cdot} −) integrates this Sphere-circumference around the unit, sending integer-multiple Algebraic Channel content (\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}) to the trivial multiplicative element (1 \ensuremath{\in} \ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}*) and sending fractional Geometric Channel content to non-trivial Geometric Channel elements.

The connecting homomorphism \ensuremath{\delta}: H\ensuremath{^{1}}(X, \ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}*) \ensuremath{\rightarrow} H\ensuremath{^{2}}(X, \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}) of the long exact sequence is identified algebraically as the first Chern class map L \ensuremath{\mapsto} c\ensuremath{_{1}}(L). The Kodaira–Spencer 1953 result establishes that for c \ensuremath{\in} H\ensuremath{^{2}}(X, \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}) of type (1, 1), the image in H\ensuremath{^{2}}(X, \ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}) vanishes — which by exactness means c is in the image of \ensuremath{\delta}, hence c = c\ensuremath{_{1}}(L) for some L \ensuremath{\in} Pic(X). The (1, 1) condition is, in McGucken vocabulary, the bi-signature condition of [38, Definition IX.0.1] applied at the H\ensuremath{^{2}} level: the (1, 1) classes are exactly those signature-readable under the McWick rotation, and the rotation operationalized by the exponential sequence projects them onto Algebraic Channel line-bundle Chern-class content. \ensuremath{\blacksquare}

The Lefschetz (1, 1) theorem is therefore not just *consistent* with the McGucken Position of Conjecture 44.3.1 — it is the canonical concrete realization of the McWick-rotation mechanism at codimension 1, with the Kodaira–Spencer 1953 exponential sequence as the operational mechanism and the 2\ensuremath{\pi}i factor as the signature of the +ic-Sphere-circumferential traversal.

The refined McGucken Position (codimension generalization). The McGucken Position of Conjecture 44.3.1 admits a sharpening at every codimension:

**Conjecture 44.7.2.1 (The Kodaira–Spencer Mechanism Lifts to Every Codimension).** *For every Hodge class c of type (p, p) on a smooth complex projective variety X \ensuremath{\in} the McGucken Manifold\ensuremath{^{6}}, there exists a "Kodaira–Spencer mechanism at codimension p" — an exponential-sequence-like resolution at the appropriate level of the K-theory tower — that operationalizes the Channel-A-projection of c from a Sphere-coherent Geometric Channel representative. The Kodaira–Spencer 1953 proof of the (1, 1) case is the codimension-1 instance of this mechanism; the higher-codimension cases require correspondingly higher-K-theoretic resolutions, with the K-theoretic level computed by the McGucken-Sphere mode-count theorem of [26, 27] applied to the codimension-p Sphere-coherent cycle representative.*

The conjecture supplies a concrete research direction: for each codimension p \ensuremath{\geq} 2, construct the explicit exponential-sequence-like resolution at the K^(p-1) level whose connecting homomorphism realizes the algebraic-cycle representation of (p, p)-Hodge classes. The codimension-2 case is the most accessible: the relevant K-theory level is K\ensuremath{^{1}}(X), and the candidate exponential sequence involves the sheaf of holomorphic 1-forms in some suitable wrapping.


#### §44.7.3. The Atiyah–Hirzebruch d_r Differentials as K-Theoretic Sphere-Coherence Obstructions


The third content of [241, §2(iv)] is the Atiyah–Hirzebruch 1962 [246] proof that the Hodge conjecture cannot hold integrally. The proof uses the Atiyah–Hirzebruch spectral sequence E_2^(p,q) = H^p(X, K^q(pt)) \ensuremath{\Rightarrow} K^(p+q)(X), which has differentials d_r that can kill integral cohomology classes — preventing them from arising from algebraic cycles. Deligne articulates this with the resulting filtration F^p K^n(X) = Ker(K^n(X) \ensuremath{\rightarrow} K^n((p-1)-skeleton)), and notes:

> *"No counterexample is known to the statement that integral (p, p) classes killed by all d_r are integral linear combinations of classes cl(Z)."*

This is a precise prediction in the AH-spectral-sequence framework. The McGucken contribution: the differentials d_r of the AH spectral sequence are the failure-of-Sphere-coherence obstructions at the K-theoretic level, and the surviving classes are precisely those whose K-theoretic representation is Sphere-coherent through to the spectral-sequence limit.

**Theorem 44.7.3 (AH d_r Differentials as McGucken-Sphere-Coherence Obstructions at the K-Theory Level).** *On every smooth complex projective variety X \ensuremath{\in} the McGucken Manifold\ensuremath{^{6}}, the differentials d_r of the Atiyah–Hirzebruch spectral sequence E_2^(p,q) = H^p(X, K^q(pt)) \ensuremath{\Rightarrow} K^(p+q)(X) are the obstructions to Sphere-coherence at the r-th K-theoretic order. An integral cohomology class c \ensuremath{\in} H^(2p)(X, \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}) of type (p, p) is in the kernel of all d_r if and only if c admits a Sphere-coherent K-theory representative — i.e., admits a resolution by an algebraic vector bundle whose local Chern-character expansion is Sphere-coherent at every smooth point of X per Proposition 44.2.1.*

**Proof sketch.** The AH spectral sequence computes complex topological K-theory from singular cohomology. The d_r differentials encode the higher Steenrod-operation-like obstructions to lifting a cohomology class to a K-theory class. On X \ensuremath{\in} the McGucken Manifold\ensuremath{^{6}} with local McGucken Sphere structure, every K-theory class is representable by an algebraic vector bundle E (by the Atiyah–Bott–Shapiro construction extended to algebraic K-theory on smooth projective varieties), and the Chern character ch(E) expands at every smooth point x \ensuremath{\in} X as a sum of differential forms on the local tangent space. The McGucken Sphere-coherence condition at x is that the Chern-character expansion is bi-foliation-symmetric per Proposition 44.2.1 — the (p, p) symmetric part of the expansion at each order matches the local Sphere structure.

The AH differentials d_r detect the failure of this Sphere-coherence at successive K-theoretic orders: d_2 is the first-order obstruction (a Steenrod-square-like operation that detects the failure of the (1, 1) bi-foliation), d_3 is the second-order obstruction (detecting the failure of higher bi-foliation symmetry), and so on. The Atiyah–Hirzebruch 1962 counterexample — a 7-dimensional Stiefel manifold with a torsion class killed by some d_r — is, in McGucken vocabulary, a manifold whose torsion class fails Sphere-coherence at some K-theoretic order, and therefore cannot arise from an algebraic cycle with integer coefficients. \ensuremath{\blacksquare}

**Corollary 44.7.3.1 (The McGucken Position Predicts Deligne's Open Statement).** *Deligne's open statement — "No counterexample is known to the statement that integral (p, p) classes killed by all d_r are integral linear combinations of classes cl(Z)" [241, §2(iv)] — is a derived consequence of the McGucken Position of Conjecture 44.3.1 restricted to the K-theoretic Sphere-coherent integral classes. The statement holds on every X \ensuremath{\in} the McGucken Manifold\ensuremath{^{6}} as a theorem of the McGucken Position with the McGucken Sphere-coherent K-theory representative supplying the explicit algebraic-cycle representation, and integer coefficients arising whenever the SO(3)/SO(2)-Haar orbit ratios at the relevant Sphere base points reduce to integers (which happens on projective spaces, Grassmannians, flag varieties, and other the McGucken Manifold\ensuremath{^{6}} objects with sufficiently rigid symmetry).*

The content is that the AH d_r differentials are not merely formal obstructions: they are the K-theoretic articulation of the bi-foliation-symmetry failure that the McGucken framework predicts as the obstruction to algebraic-cycle representation. The known integral-Hodge-conjecture counterexamples of [246, 247, 248] are predicted features under the McGucken Position, with each counterexample identifiable as a failure of Sphere-coherence at the corresponding K-theoretic order.


#### §44.7.4. The Projective-vs-Kähler Boundary as the Boundary of the McGucken Category the McGucken Manifold\ensuremath{^{6}}


The fourth content of [241, §2(v)] is the assertion (citing Zucker's appendix to [251]):

> *"The assumption in the Hodge conjecture that X be algebraic cannot be weakened to X being merely Kähler. See Zucker's appendix to [251] for counterexamples where X is a complex torus."*

The standard literature treats this as a curiosity of the conjecture's statement: the projectivity assumption is required, and general compact Kähler manifolds admit counterexamples — generic complex tori of dimension at least 2 provide the most accessible explicit examples. The McGucken framework supplies a clean explanation for why projectivity is the assumption.

**Theorem 44.7.4 (The Projective-vs-Kähler Boundary Is the Boundary of the McGucken Manifold\ensuremath{^{6}}).** *Under the McGucken Position of Conjecture 44.3.1, the smooth complex projective varieties form a strict subset of the McGucken Category \text{the McGucken Manifold}\ensuremath{^{6}} that admits Sphere-coherent categorical descent from the source-tuple F_M = (\text{McGucken Sphere}, \ensuremath{\mathcal{G}}_M, McGucken Manifold \text{the McGucken Manifold}, $\slashed{D}_M$, \ensuremath{\mathcal{S}}_M, \ensuremath{\mathcal{A}}_M). General compact Kähler manifolds — for instance generic complex tori of dimension at least 2 — do not in general admit projective embeddings, do not in general arise as categorical descents from the \text{McGucken Sphere} / \ensuremath{\mathcal{G}}_M tower of F_M, and therefore lie outside the McGucken Manifold\ensuremath{^{6}}. The McGucken Position predicts the failure of the Hodge conjecture outside the McGucken Manifold\ensuremath{^{6}} as a consequence of the absence of the categorical-descent machinery that forces the algebraic-cycle representation; the boundary of where the conjecture holds is exactly the boundary of \text{the McGucken Manifold}\ensuremath{^{6}}, and the projective-vs-Kähler distinction is the algebraic-geometric articulation of "in \text{the McGucken Manifold}\ensuremath{^{6}} vs not in the McGucken Manifold\ensuremath{^{6}}."*

**Proof sketch.** A smooth complex projective variety is a smooth complex manifold admitting an embedding into \ensuremath{\mathbb{C}}P^N for some N \ensuremath{\geq} 1. The complex projective space \ensuremath{\mathbb{C}}P^N is in the McGucken Category the McGucken Manifold\ensuremath{^{6}} explicitly per [15] — \ensuremath{\mathbb{C}}P\ensuremath{^{3}} is the Penrose twistor space, and the \text{McGucken Sphere}-descent of [15] establishes the full chain dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic \ensuremath{\Rightarrow} McGucken-Sphere \ensuremath{\Rightarrow} \ensuremath{\mathbb{C}}P\ensuremath{^{3}} \ensuremath{\Rightarrow} Z_a \ensuremath{\Rightarrow} M_+(k+4, n) \ensuremath{\Rightarrow} G_+(k, n) \ensuremath{\Rightarrow} Y = CZ \ensuremath{\Rightarrow} G_+(k, n; L) \ensuremath{\Rightarrow} \ensuremath{\Omega}. The embedding X \ensuremath{\hookrightarrow} \ensuremath{\mathbb{C}}P^N is a morphism in the McGucken Manifold\ensuremath{^{6}} that restricts the McGucken Sphere-coherent structure of \ensuremath{\mathbb{C}}P^N to X; the McGucken Sphere structure on X is inherited from the ambient \ensuremath{\mathbb{C}}P^N via the embedding. The projective-embedding condition is precisely the condition that places X in the McGucken Manifold\ensuremath{^{6}} via the explicit \text{McGucken Sphere}-descent.

A general compact Kähler manifold admits no such embedding. The Kodaira embedding theorem characterizes the embeddable Kähler manifolds as those admitting a positive line bundle (a Hodge manifold); generic complex tori of dimension at least 2 do not admit positive line bundles and are not Hodge manifolds. Such a manifold has no \text{McGucken Sphere}-descent representation in the McGucken Manifold\ensuremath{^{6}}, and the McGucken Position's machinery (the McGucken Sphere-coherent cycle representation, the SO(3)/SO(2)-Haar-measure rational-coefficient supply, the +ic directional expansion at every point) is not available on it. The McGucken Position therefore predicts the Hodge conjecture's failure on generic complex tori as a consequence, consistent with the Zucker counterexamples. \ensuremath{\blacksquare}

**Remark 44.7.4.1 (Significance).** The Zucker–Bagnera counterexamples on complex tori are not a problem for the McGucken Position; they are an expected boundary feature. The McGucken framework identifies the precise boundary where the conjecture should hold: every variety admitting a categorical descent from F_M in the McGucken Manifold\ensuremath{^{6}}. The orthodox literature has treated the projectivity-vs-Kähler boundary as an empirical observation about which manifolds the conjecture is *stated* on; the McGucken framework identifies it as a *derived* boundary forced by the categorical-descent structure of dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic.


#### §44.7.5. The Voisin Calabi-Yau Griffiths Group Infinite-Rank Result as Sphere-Coherent Cycle Moduli Infinite-Dimensionality


The fifth content of [241, §3] is the Voisin [252] result that the Griffiths group of a generic Calabi-Yau threefold is not finitely generated. Deligne writes:

> *"No conjecture is available to predict what subgroup of J^p(X) the group A_p(X) is. Cases are known where A_p(X)/A_p^0(X) is of infinite rank. See, for instance, the paper [252] and the references it contains."*

The Intermediate Jacobian J^p(X) is an extension of (p, p)-Hodge classes by a complex torus H^(2p-1)(X, \ensuremath{\mathbb{C}})/(H^(2p-1)(X, \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}) \ensuremath{\oplus} F^p) — the "deeper" Geometric Channel content beyond the Hodge classes themselves. The Abel–Jacobi map A_p(X) \ensuremath{\rightarrow} J^p(X) sends an algebraic cycle to its J^p-class. The Voisin result establishes that on generic Calabi-Yau threefolds, the algebraic-cycle moduli image in J^p modulo the connected component A_p^0 is of infinite rank.

**Proposition 44.7.5 (The Intermediate Jacobian as a Algebraic Channel / Geometric Channel Object).** *On a smooth complex projective variety X \ensuremath{\in} the McGucken Manifold\ensuremath{^{6}}, the Intermediate Jacobian J^p(X) is itself a Algebraic Channel / Geometric Channel object of [38, Definition IX.0.1], with the integer cohomology H^(2p-1)(X, \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}) supplying the dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic Algebraic Channel primitive content and the analytic torus quotient H^(2p-1)(X, \ensuremath{\mathbb{C}})/(H^(2p-1)(X, \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}) \ensuremath{\oplus} F^p) supplying the dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic Geometric Channel continuous content. The Abel–Jacobi map A_p(X) \ensuremath{\rightarrow} J^p(X) is the Geometric Channel reading of the algebraic-cycle data, sending each algebraic cycle to its Sphere-coherent J^p-representative via the McWick rotation \ensuremath{\tau} = x\ensuremath{_{4}}/c applied to the cycle's local Sphere structure at every smooth point.*

**Corollary 44.7.5.1 (The Voisin Infinite-Rank Result Is Consistent with the McGucken Position).** *The Voisin [252] result that A_p(X)/A_p^0(X) is of infinite rank for generic Calabi-Yau threefolds is consistent with the McGucken Position of Conjecture 44.3.1. The Position claims that every Hodge class on X has *some* algebraic-cycle representative; it does not claim the algebraic-cycle moduli is finite-rank, nor does it constrain the structure of A_p(X) modulo A_p^0(X). The infinite-rank Griffiths group is, in McGucken vocabulary, the statement that the McGucken Sphere-coherent cycle moduli on a generic Calabi-Yau threefold is infinite-dimensional — the Calabi-Yau threefold's intricate complex structure supports unboundedly many Sphere-coherent deformations of any given algebraic cycle, consistent with the rich Sphere-coherent moduli generated by the threefold's holomorphic-tangent-bundle automorphism group acting on the local Sphere at each smooth point.*

The content is that the Voisin infinite-rank result articulates the richness of the Geometric Channel continuous content on Calabi-Yau threefolds in the McGucken Manifold\ensuremath{^{6}} — a feature of the McGucken Sphere as a foundational primitive supporting unboundedly many continuous deformations, not a counterexample to the McGucken Position.


#### §44.7.6. Deligne's Examples 1 and 2 as Direct McGucken Position Predictions on the McGucken Manifold\ensuremath{^{6}}


The sixth content is the two specific open instances Deligne flags in [241, §4]:

**Example 1 (Künneth Diagonal).** For X of complex dimension N, the diagonal \ensuremath{\Delta} \ensuremath{\subset} X \ensuremath{\times} X is an algebraic cycle of codimension N. The Künneth components cl(\ensuremath{\Delta})_(a,b) \ensuremath{\in} H^a(X) \ensuremath{\otimes} H^b(X) \ensuremath{\subset} H^(2N)(X \ensuremath{\times} X) (a + b = 2N) of the diagonal class are Hodge classes. The Hodge conjecture for these Künneth components is open in general.

**Example 2 (Inverse Hard Lefschetz).** If \ensuremath{\eta} \ensuremath{\in} H\ensuremath{^{2}}(X, \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}) is the cohomology class of a hyperplane section, the iterated cup product \ensuremath{\eta}^p: H^(N-p)(X, \ensuremath{\mathbb{C}}) \ensuremath{\rightarrow} H^(N+p)(X, \ensuremath{\mathbb{C}}) is an isomorphism (hard Lefschetz theorem). Let z \ensuremath{\in} H^(N-p)(X, \ensuremath{\mathbb{C}}) \ensuremath{\otimes} H^(N-p)(X, \ensuremath{\mathbb{C}}) \ensuremath{\subset} H^(2N-2p)(X \ensuremath{\times} X) be the class such that the inverse isomorphism (\ensuremath{\eta}^p)^(-1) is c \ensuremath{\mapsto} pr_(1!)(z \ensuremath{\cup} pr_2^* c). The class z is Hodge. The Hodge conjecture for z is open in general.

The McGucken Position supplies direct predictions for both:

**Theorem 44.7.6 (Direct McGucken Position Predictions for Deligne's Examples 1 and 2).** *On every smooth complex projective variety X \ensuremath{\in} the McGucken Manifold\ensuremath{^{6}}, the following hold under Conjecture 44.3.1:*

*the strict-monotonicity statement of the Second Law $dS/dt > 0$ Every Künneth component cl(\ensuremath{\Delta})_(a,b) of the diagonal class cl(\ensuremath{\Delta}) \ensuremath{\subset} X \ensuremath{\times} X is algebraic.*

*The inverse-hard-Lefschetz class z \ensuremath{\in} H^(N-p)(X, \ensuremath{\mathbb{C}}) \ensuremath{\otimes} H^(N-p)(X, \ensuremath{\mathbb{C}}) is algebraic.*

#### §44.7.8. Reduction-Mod-p Intersection-Number Rationality as a Derived Consequence of the Rational Haar-Orbit Structure


The eighth content is in [241, §6]. Deligne raises the open question: take an abelian variety A over F̄_q, lift A in two different ways to characteristic-0 complex abelian varieties A_1 and A_2 over Q̄. Pick Hodge classes z_1 and z_2 on A_1 and A_2 of complementary dimension. Interpreting z_1 and z_2 as \ensuremath{\ell}-adic cohomology classes, one defines the intersection number \ensuremath{\kappa} of the reduction of z_1 and z_2 over F. Deligne asks: is \ensuremath{\kappa} a rational number?

**Proposition 44.7.8 (\ensuremath{\kappa} \ensuremath{\in} \ensuremath{\mathbb{Q}} as a Derived Consequence of the McGucken Position).** *On every smooth complex projective variety X \ensuremath{\in} \text{the McGucken Manifold}\ensuremath{^{6}} — and in particular on every CM abelian variety, every Fermat hypersurface, every projective space, Grassmannian, and flag variety in the McGucken Manifold\ensuremath{^{6}} — the reduction-mod-p intersection number \ensuremath{\kappa} of [241, §6] of Hodge classes z_1, z_2 of complementary dimension is rational under the McGucken Position of Conjecture 44.3.1.*

**Proof sketch.** Under the McGucken Position, each Hodge class z_i admits a Sphere-coherent algebraic-cycle representation with rational coefficients computed via the SO(3)/SO(2)-Haar measure of [66, Theorem 4.2] applied to the local Sphere structure at every smooth point of the supporting cycle. The intersection number \ensuremath{\kappa} is computed by the standard intersection-theoretic pairing on H^*(reduction over F, \ensuremath{\mathbb{Q}}_\ensuremath{\ell}), which on Sphere-coherent classes reduces to a finite sum of products of SO(3)/SO(2)-Haar-orbit-ratio coefficients of z_1 with corresponding coefficients of z_2.

The SO(3)/SO(2)-Haar-orbit ratios are rational at every base point because the Haar measure is normalized to total volume 1 and the orbit volumes are rational fractions of the total per the orbit-stabilizer theorem applied to the action of SO(3)/SO(2) on the McGucken Sphere. The reduction-mod-p operation preserves the rational-Haar-orbit structure if the lifts A_1, A_2 are themselves Sphere-coherent — which they are under the McGucken Position because both lifts are in the McGucken Manifold\ensuremath{^{6}} by the assumption of being CM-abelian-variety lifts of the F̄_q-abelian variety A. The intersection number \ensuremath{\kappa} is therefore a finite rational linear combination of rational orbit ratios, hence rational. \ensuremath{\blacksquare}

**Corollary 44.7.8.1 (Comparison with the Absolute-Hodge and Motivated-Class Substitutes).** *The rationality of \ensuremath{\kappa} predicted by the McGucken Position of Conjecture 44.3.1 on the McGucken Manifold\ensuremath{^{6}} varieties is consistent with the absolute-Hodge-class substitute of [253] (cited as reference [3] of [241]) and the motivated-class substitute of [254] (cited as reference [1] of [241]), without requiring those substitutes as primary objects. The McGucken Position predicts \ensuremath{\kappa} \ensuremath{\in} \ensuremath{\mathbb{Q}} as a derived consequence of the rational-Haar-orbit structure on the McGucken-Sphere primitive, supplying the mathematical content the absolute-Hodge framework approximates from above. The McGucken framework therefore subsumes the absolute-Hodge / motivated-class substitutes as approximations of its rational-Haar-orbit structure on the McGucken Manifold\ensuremath{^{6}} varieties.*

**About this appendix.** *Readers arriving at the McGucken Principle from a standard graduate-relativity background bring one deep habit: the reflex to treat per-proper-time quantities as the "physical" or "covariant" ones, and per-coordinate-time quantities as gauge-dependent bookkeeping. That habit points the wrong way here, because the Principle is a statement about the manifold itself — an expansion happening at every event, at the same rate, regardless of which worldline crosses that event. This appendix explains the four distinct $x_4$-rate quantities the paper uses, states which one is the Principle, and shows through five worked examples how photons, horizons, twins, and GPS clocks all read naturally once the four quantities are kept in their proper roles.*


### §A.0. The Physical Fact


Every quantity, rule, and check in this appendix descends from one physical fact:

> *The fourth dimension $x_4$ is expanding in a spherically symmetric manner at the rate of $c$ from every spacetime event, or $dx_4/dt = ic$.*

That is the McGucken Principle. Before any of its consequences are unpacked, its status must be stated plainly, because it is the point on which every reading in this appendix turns: $dx_4/dt = ic$ is an ontological claim — a statement about what physically is — and a coordinate convention, formal device, or notational choice it is not. It asserts that the fourth dimension is a real dimension that is really expanding, at the rate $c$, from every event of spacetime, now. The expansion is the physically primary fact; everything else in the paper is a consequence of it. Minkowski spacetime is what the expansion looks like after its rate is integrated into the coordinate $x_4 = ict$ and squared into the Lorentzian metric $x_4^2 = -c^2 t^2$; Hilbert space is what the same expansion looks like when its per-increment imaginary rate is read as oscillation; the light cone is the locus the expanding wavefront traces; the metric, the causal order, the Poincaré group, the Born rule, and the Schrödinger equation are all downstream of the one expansion. None of these is postulated independently. They descend, by the derivations of the body, from the single physical fact that $x_4$ is expanding at $c$.

This is the reversal the reader must hold onto throughout. Standard physics takes Minkowski spacetime, or the Hilbert space, or the metric, as a starting arena and builds upon it. Here the arena is a result, and a starting point it is not: the starting point is the physical expansion $dx_4/dt = ic$, and the arena is what that expansion generates. When the appendix below insists that $dx_4/dt = ic$ is primary and the per-proper-time quantities are constructed from it, this is what is meant — a claim about which fact is physically prior, and a preference among equivalent formalisms it is not. The rate is prior; the worldlines that share in it, the metric that its squaring produces, and the observers that read it are all posterior.

The imaginary unit $i$ in $dx_4/dt = ic$ records the algebraic perpendicularity of the $x_4$-axis to the three spatial axes on which the expansion casts its projection. Its geometric realisation at each event $p \in \text{the McGucken Manifold}$ is the McGucken Sphere at event $p$ at time $t$ — the spherical wavefront of radius $ct$ swept out around $p$ by the $x_4$-expansion. The McGucken Sphere is what distinguishes the Principle from Minkowski's constant four-velocity norm $u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2$: the norm is a scalar constraint carrying no group action and no measure, and it survives here as a theorem of the Principle (the chain-rule pullback of the McGucken Sphere's expansion rate).

The McGucken Sphere carries $\mathrm{SO}(3)$-invariant content that supplies the Born rule downstream by two independent routes: the rank-2 metric bilinearity route (Theorem 7.2; §9.5.13 of the present paper) and the Haar-measure route (the unique $\mathrm{SO}(3)$-invariant measure on the McGucken Sphere). That these two derivationally-disjoint derivations return the same Born density $|\psi|^2$ is an instance of the convergent overdetermination documented in §17.5bis; see Remark A.0.1.

**Remark A.0.1 (Two independent derivations of the Born rule).** *The Born density $P = |\psi|^2$ is derived in this framework by two routes that share no premises beyond the McGucken Sphere itself:*

*(i) The rank-2 metric bilinearity route (Theorem 7.2; §9.5.13; \[MG-Born\] Lemma 4.1, Theorem 4.2). The $x_4$-flux density at a detection event is the metric pairing of the forward $+ic$ advance with its conjugate $-ic$ advance. The Minkowski metric induced by $x_4 = ict$ is a rank-2 tensor, so the pairing is bilinear in $(\psi, \psi^*)$; $\mathrm{U}(1)$ phase invariance, reality, non-negativity, and normalisation then force $P = |\psi|^2$ uniquely. The exponent 2 is the rank of the metric.*

*(ii) The Haar-measure route (Theorem 7.2 scholium; §7 of the present paper). The McGucken Sphere at the detection event carries the action of $\mathrm{SO}(3)$; the unique $\mathrm{SO}(3)$-invariant normalised measure on the 2-sphere is the Haar (rotation-invariant) measure, and the probability of detection in a solid-angle element is fixed by that measure. Applied to the wavefront amplitude, this returns $P = |\psi|^2$.*

*Route (i) proceeds from the rank of the metric; route (ii) proceeds from the symmetry group of the McGucken Sphere. Neither uses the other's premise — one needs only that the metric is rank 2, the other only that the McGucken Sphere carries an $\mathrm{SO}(3)$ action — so their agreement on $P = |\psi|^2$ is a genuine convergence, not a single argument told twice. This is the sense in which the Born rule is convergently overdetermined by $dx_4/dt = ic$ (§17.5bis of the present paper): the same downstream fact is fixed by two upstream properties of the McGucken Sphere that are logically independent of each other.*


### §A.1. The Four $x_4$-Rate Quantities


The framework uses four related quantities associated with the fourth dimension's advance. Each has its own symbol, its own domain of definition, and its own interpretation, and they diverge on null worldlines.

**the articulation that $i$ is the algebraic shadow of the geometric perpendicularity of $x_4$ to the three spatial dimensions The coordinate rate $dx_4/dt = ic$**, parameter: coordinate $t$; range: fixed value $ic$; universal — holds at every event of $\text{the McGucken Manifold}$. *The Principle.* With the integrated shadow $x_4 = ict$, this rate holds identically along every worldline of $\text{the McGucken Manifold}$ — timelike, null, accelerated, at any gravitational potential — because $x_4$ is a coordinate function of $t$ alone. Every statement about the universality of the expansion, its metric-independence (GR T2 of the present paper), or its exception-freeness is a statement in the articulation that $i$ is the algebraic shadow of the geometric perpendicularity of $x_4$ to the three spatial dimensions.

**the articulation that the Wick rotation is the toggle between two disjoint positions of $i$ The McGucken Sphere-tangent share $v_{x_4} \equiv \sqrt{c^2 - v^2}$** (the worldline's share of the $x_4$-expansion, per coordinate time — the standard time-dilation factor $c \cdot d\tau/dt$ on timelike worldlines); parameter: coordinate $t$; range: $[0, c]$; worldline-dependent. A bounded quantity (Lemma 5.1.3.2). The partition $v^2 + v_{x_4}^2 = c^2$ holds for every worldline, null ones included: at spatial rest $v_{x_4} = c$; on a null worldline $v = c$ gives $v_{x_4} = 0$. On timelike worldlines, $v_{x_4}$ coincides with the standard time-dilation factor: $v_{x_4} = c \cdot d\tau/dt = c/\gamma$ for $0 \le v < c$. The identity $v_{x_4} = c \cdot d\tau/dt$ is a theorem about $v_{x_4}$ — $\tau$ appears as output, not as the differentiation parameter. At $v = c$ (the null limit) all three expressions give $v_{x_4} = 0$: the $\sqrt{c^2 - v^2}$ form by direct substitution, the $c \cdot d\tau/dt$ form as the ratio $c \cdot 0 / dt$ with $d\tau = 0$, and the $c/\gamma$ form as the limit $\gamma \to \infty$. The framework uses $v_{x_4}$ as the primary symbol because it is defined by direct substitution on the null boundary. Statements about time dilation, the photon's $x_4$-rest, and horizons live here.

**the articulation that the position-of-$i$ toggle produces interference in one setting and diffusion in the other The Lorentzian temporal four-velocity component $u^4 = dx_4/d\tau = ic\gamma$**; parameter: proper $\tau$; unbounded, undefined on null worldlines; a chain-rule consequence. Derived from the articulation that $i$ is the algebraic shadow of the geometric perpendicularity of $x_4$ to the three spatial dimensions by the chain rule (Theorem 5.1.2.8 of the present paper): $dx_4/d\tau = (dx_4/dt)(dt/d\tau) = ic\gamma$. Its magnitude $c\gamma$ is unbounded as $v \to c$, and on a null worldline ($d\tau = 0$) the quantity is undefined — there the affinely-parametrised null tangent $dx^\mu/d\lambda$ replaces it (Lemma 7.2.2.1a of the present paper).

**the articulation that the Schrödinger equation carries both phenomenological faces simultaneously via the position-of-$i$ toggle The accumulated $x_4$-advance along $\gamma$, $X_4[\gamma] \equiv \int_\gamma ic \, d\tau = ic \cdot \tau[\gamma]$** — proper time up to the factor $ic$; a worldline functional, path-dependent. Distinct from the coordinate $x_4$. Two worldlines sharing endpoints share $\Delta x_4 = ic \, \Delta t$ but generally differ in $X_4$. Along a null worldline $X_4$ is constant; around any closed curve $\oint dx_4 = 0$ identically. Statements about differential ageing (the twins) live in the articulation that the Schrödinger equation carries both phenomenological faces simultaneously via the position-of-$i$ toggle. The bridge to the articulation that the Wick rotation is the toggle between two disjoint positions of $i$: $dX_4 = ic \, d\tau = i v_{x_4} \, dt$.


### §A.2. Which One Is the Principle


The Principle is $dx_4/dt = ic$: the coordinate-time reading the articulation that $i$ is the algebraic shadow of the geometric perpendicularity of $x_4$ to the three spatial dimensions. Because $x_4$ is a coordinate function of $t$ alone, the rate $dx_4/dt$ takes the same value $ic$ at every event of $\text{the McGucken Manifold}$ — an expanding photon-event, a horizon event, an event on any accelerated worldline. The reading $dx_4/d\tau = ic$ is available too, but only where $d\tau = dt$: on a worldline at spatial rest, the chain rule collapses and the articulation that $i$ is the algebraic shadow of the geometric perpendicularity of $x_4$ to the three spatial dimensions coincides with the value of the articulation that the position-of-$i$ toggle produces interference in one setting and diffusion in the other. This is Lemma 4.7 of the present paper (the rest-frame reverse-reading equivalence), and the qualification $d\tau = dt$ is what makes it valid. On a moving worldline the chain rule gives $ic\gamma$; on a null worldline the quantity does not exist. The coordinate-time reading is primary because $dx_4/dt = ic$ is a physical fact — the expansion itself is prior to any worldline, and $dx_4/dt = ic$ records it directly.


### §A.3. Reading the Photon, the Horizon, and the Time-Dilation Formula


#### §A.3.1. The Photon's $x_4$-Rate


The photon's share in the expansion is zero: $v_{x_4} = 0$ (the $v = c$ limit of $v^2 + v_{x_4}^2 = c^2$), obtained by direct substitution of $v = c$ into $v_{x_4} = \sqrt{c^2 - v^2}$. The reader may be tempted to write "$dx_4/dt = 0$ for the photon" or "$dx_4/d\tau = 0$." Neither is available. The first is the coordinate rate the articulation that $i$ is the algebraic shadow of the geometric perpendicularity of $x_4$ to the three spatial dimensions, which is $ic$ at every event of $\text{the McGucken Manifold}$ including the photon's — what vanishes is the photon's share, not the expansion. The second is $0/0$: proper time is not defined for a photon ($d\tau = 0$ pointwise). The correct statement is the share $v_{x_4} = 0$, so $X_4$ does not accumulate, so the photon ages not at all. The Principle continues to hold at every event the photon crosses.

At the photon's measurement event (absorption by a photographic film grain, ejection of a photoelectron at a photocathode, click at a photodetector), what is transferred to the apparatus is the photon's spatial three-momentum $p = \hbar k$ (the empirically-observed recoil, film-grain darkening, or photoelectron kinetic energy content); the Born content $|\psi|^2$ supplies the probability of absorption at any given grain via the SO(3)-Haar measure on the McGucken Sphere at the detection event (Remark A.0.1). A photon does not carry an $x_4$-advance to transfer at measurement; what it carries and transfers is its spatial momentum.


#### §A.3.2. The $x_4$-Rate at a Horizon


The rate is gravity-rigid: $\partial(dx_4/dt)/\partial g_{\mu\nu} = 0$ (GR T2 of the present paper). The rate $dx_4/dt = ic$ takes the same value near the horizon as at infinity. What varies with potential is the share: $v_{x_4}(r) = c \cdot d\tau/dt = c\sqrt{1 - r_s/r}$ (static Schwarzschild observer), vanishing at $r = r_s$. On the infaller's own clock $d\tau = dt$ locally and Lemma 4.7 applies: the local rate is the full $ic$ throughout. Gravitational time dilation is the coordinate-frame projection of a locally invariant rate.


#### §A.3.3. Which Identity Is "$c^2$ Through Spacetime"?


Sphere partition (per coordinate time, all worldlines): $v^2 + v_{x_4}^2 = c^2$, bounded, locus a quarter-circle.

Lorentzian four-velocity norm (per proper time, massive worldlines only): $u^\mu u_\mu = |dx_4/d\tau|^2 - |d\vec{x}/d\tau|^2 = -c^2$, unbounded in each term, signature difference fixing the invariant.

The Euclidean per-proper-time sum $|dx_4/d\tau|^2 + |d\vec{x}/d\tau|^2$ equals $c^2$ only in the instantaneous rest frame; elsewhere $c^2\gamma^2$.

Plus-sign identities belong to the articulation that the Wick rotation is the toggle between two disjoint positions of $i$; minus-sign identities to the articulation that the position-of-$i$ toggle produces interference in one setting and diffusion in the other.


#### §A.3.4. The Twin Paradox


Coordinate accumulation is path-independent: both twins accumulate $\Delta x_4 = ic \, \Delta t$. Differential ageing is read from $X_4 = \int ic \, d\tau$, advancing at real magnitude $v_{x_4}$ per unit coordinate time. On the traveling leg $v_{x_4} < c$, so the traveler accumulates less $X_4$, so less proper time. The stay-at-home twin retains $v_{x_4} = c$ and accumulates the maximal $X_4$. The CTC question closes the same way: $\oint dx_4 = 0$ identically, so a CTC cannot run on the coordinate; the impossibility lives in $X_4$.


#### §A.3.5. $\gamma$-Projection and Rapidity


A boost is hyperbolic: rapidity $\phi$ with $\cosh\phi = \gamma$. The McGucken Sphere-partition projection is circular: Sphere angle $\theta$ with $\sin\theta = v/c$, $\cos\theta = v_{x_4}/c = 1/\gamma$. Related by the Gudermannian, $\theta = \mathrm{gd}(\phi)$, so $\cos\theta = \operatorname{sech}\phi$. The $1/\gamma$ projection is about $\theta$; unbounded component growth is about $\phi$.


### §A.4. Why Nothing of Relativity Is Lost


The fourth dimension advances at the same rate at every event of $\text{the McGucken Manifold}$; worldlines differ only in how much of that advance they share in. Massive at rest shares fully ($v_{x_4} = c$); moving shares less ($v_{x_4} = \sqrt{c^2 - v^2}$, clock slowed by the Lorentz factor); the photon shares nothing ($v_{x_4} = 0$, ageless, no $X_4$). Lorentz invariance survives entire because the invariant content — the norm $u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2$ and the metric — is a theorem of the Principle (the metric is the pullback of the Euclidean form along $x_4 = ict$, the $-c^2$ from $(ic)^2$). Lorentz transformations preserve that derived metric; $\gamma$, time dilation, length contraction, $E = \gamma mc^2$, the null cone, and the mass-shell all come out unchanged. The foliation quantities $v_{x_4}$ and $X_4$ are additional bookkeeping frame-anchored to the cosmic-comoving foliation (the CMB rest frame); the Cloaking Theorem (Theorem 39 of the present paper) explains why local metrology cannot detect them. GR survives by the invariant/deformable split: the rate is gravity-rigid; gravity deforms the spatial sector. Time dilation, redshift, light bending, perihelion advance, the horizon, and the field equations are recovered exactly. The horizon is where the share is extinguished; the expansion does not stop.


### §A.5. Worked Examples


#### §A.5.1. The Twin Paradox


Traveler at speed $v$ for coordinate time $\Delta t$. Coordinate accumulation: $\Delta x_4 = ic \, \Delta t$ for both. Traveler's share: $v_{x_4} = c\sqrt{1 - v^2/c^2}$. Accumulated: $\Delta X_4^{\text{trav}} = ic\sqrt{1 - v^2/c^2} \, \Delta t$ vs $\Delta X_4^{\text{stay}} = ic \, \Delta t$. Differential ageing: $\Delta\tau^{\text{trav}} - \Delta\tau^{\text{stay}} = \Delta t \left(\sqrt{1 - v^2/c^2} - 1\right) < 0$: the traveler is younger by exactly the Lorentz factor.


#### §A.5.2. GPS Clock Rate


Satellite at radius $r$, speed $v$, mass $M$. Principle: $dx_4/dt = ic$. Gravitational share: $v_{x_4}^{\text{grav}}/c = \sqrt{1 - 2GM/rc^2}$; kinematic factor $\sqrt{1 - v^2/c^2}$. Total: $v_{x_4}^{\text{sat}}/c \approx 1 - GM/(rc^2) - v^2/(2c^2)$. Ground: $\approx 1 - GM/(R_\oplus c^2)$. Fractional difference $\approx GM(1/R_\oplus - 1/r) - v^2/(2c^2)$, matching the $+4.5 \times 10^{-10}$ pre-launch offset at $r = 26{,}600$ km, $v = 3.87$ km/s.


#### §A.5.3. Schwarzschild Gravitational Redshift


Photon from $r_1$ to $r_2 > r_1$. Principle: $dx_4/dt = ic$. Local clock rate: $v_{x_4}(r)/c = \sqrt{1 - r_s/r}$. Frequency ratio $\nu_2/\nu_1 = \sqrt{(1 - r_s/r_1)/(1 - r_s/r_2)}$; weak-field $\Delta\nu/\nu \approx -GM(1/r_2 - 1/r_1)/c^2$, matching Pound–Rebka 1959. Photon: $v_{x_4} = 0$ throughout, no $X_4$. The redshift is about the clock rates at emitter and receiver, not the photon.


#### §A.5.4. Hawking Temperature


At $r = r_s$, local share $v_{x_4}(r) \to 0$. Surface gravity $\kappa = c/(2r_s)$; compactification circumference $L_H = 4\pi r_s = c\hbar\beta_H$; temperature $T_H = \hbar c^3/(8\pi GM k_B)$. The expansion does not stop at the horizon; the share is extinguished on the static foliation, and compactification of the Euclidean-section $x_4$-axis at $L_H$ produces the thermal spectrum.


#### §A.5.5. Bell's Spaceship


Rockets $A$, $B$ at proper distance $L_0$, accelerating identically. Coordinate rate: $dx_4/dt = ic$. Share: $v_{x_4}(t) = c\sqrt{1 - v(t)^2/c^2}$, decreasing. Accumulated: $X_4^A = X_4^B$, so both age identically. Launch-frame separation constant $L_0$; co-moving separation $L(t) = L_0 c / v_{x_4}(t)$, growing without bound. The string breaks: the budget shifts into the spatial sector identically on each rocket, so no differential ageing; the paradox lives in the spatial-sector geometry, the string breaking as co-moving distance grows as $1/v_{x_4}$.

Contains the proof of what is now known as the Lefschetz (1, 1) Theorem: on a smooth complex projective variety, every (1, 1)-Hodge class is a rational linear combination of divisor classes (codimension-1 algebraic cycles). Phys. 104:4, 605–609) throughout Chapters 5–6; (v) pervasive physics-origin technical terminology throughout (conformal vertex algebra, conformal dimension, central charge, Virasoro algebra, OPE, normal ordering, bosonization, \ensuremath{\beta}-\ensuremath{\gamma} system, screening operators, W-algebra, free field realization); (vi) physics-journal bibliography citations including Friedan-Martinec-Shenker 1986, Dotsenko 1990, Petersen-Rasmussen-Yu 1997, all in Nuclear Physics B. The dependency chain dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic \ensuremath{\rightarrow} the McGucken Manifold \ensuremath{\rightarrow} 4D physics \ensuremath{\rightarrow} 2D-CFT physics \ensuremath{\rightarrow} 2D-CFT machinery \ensuremath{\rightarrow} Frenkel 2007 establishes Frenkel 2007 as a five-removes-downstream document of the physical principle dx\ensuremath{_{4}}/dt = ic at the historical--dependency tier. The asymmetric surface-vs-structure pattern of Remark 21.7.14ter.3 of §21.7.14ter.4bis: Chapters 1 and 10 (Langlands correspondence statement and proper) are pure-mathematics surface with no physics terminology; Chapters 2–9 (vertex algebras, central elements, opers, free field realization, Wakimoto modules, intertwiners, identification with opers, structure of g-hat-modules) carry the physics-derived machinery.

Hirotaka Sugawara canonical primary-source physics paper introducing the Sugawara construction — the realization of the stress-energy tensor of a 2D conformal field theory as a quadratic expression in the currents of a Kac-Moody algebra. The construction was originally articulated in the dual-resonance-model physics literature and supplied the foundational central-elements machinery for subsequent affine Kac-Moody algebra representation theory. Identified in §21.7.14ter.4bis of the present paper as the physics-paper origin of the Segal-Sugawara construction that the Frenkel 2007 monograph [410] uses throughout Chapters 3, 6, 7, 8 as the foundational central-elements machinery of the local geometric Langlands correspondence. The omission of the Sugawara 1968 primary-source physics citation from the Frenkel 2007 mathematics-monograph bibliography is a historical example of the Mathematics-from-Physics Absorption pattern at the citation-level operating at full erasure of the original physics primary source while preserving the mathematical infrastructure derived from it.
